一晃都玩了快40小时了，对于一个类似于辐射4这样的生存建造游戏来说其实也就刚到中期的程度，然而由于《流放者柯南》没有任务记录系统，我已经卡关了，不知道该做什么，现在感觉打怪毫无意义。玩这游戏的初衷是我一段时间特别想要玩纯粹近身肉搏的动作游戏。这游戏我早就入库，但直到看见视觉升级的通知我才想要尝试一下。刚进入游戏让我回忆起游玩《魔法门6》的感觉，特别是当这游戏可以开管理员模式的时候就更像了。一开始我选了双手大剑，战斗体验还挺带感，我什么都没调按部就班的玩，只不过遇到Boss就傻眼了。我最高700血，Boss非人型基本都4000+血，我记得我是开了简单模式来着？结果当然是打不过。从这一刻，我的游玩方式彻底改变了。我发现了单人模式可以用管理员权限调整增伤和受伤比例，可以快走和传送。发现这游戏可以极为方便的使用MOD，真的小地图和9999仓库MOD简直是必装。虽然会了这些难度降低了，可任务目标的问题还是没有解决，感觉把地图探索完我就可以退游了。

从兴致勃勃的猛肝4天到突然兴趣全无，游戏的明显问题和亮点如下 先说亮点吧 本作的奴隶系统和建造系统是我玩过的同类游戏中最让我感兴趣和眼前一亮的设计， 即便是评论区里也有很多上千上百小时的建筑休闲玩家。玩过的其他同类游戏中就流放者柯南最让我有过这种上头的感觉， 那种从一个锤子开始到一个全是随从的基地的成就感简直拉满了。我也很喜欢本作的奴隶和动物养成系统。 特别是重置后的增强版，画质直接上升到了偶尔夕阳落在山峰上都忍不住截图的电影级画质。 有时候被鬓狗追着到处跑后，偶然看到这种画面也是一种视觉上的绝对享受，我特别喜欢沙暴即将来临时那种黄沙和云卷在 一起倾泄向天空的画面。 然后是不足 1.战斗手感 作为一个开放世界砍杀类生存游戏，蹩脚的砍杀反馈和僵硬的攻击动作是玩家开局最先发现的点，那种难以言喻但总之就是很难受的战斗体验会贯穿游戏始终，这个不好形容，可以自行体会。 2.开局体验 其实我一直都不理解制作组在游戏开发过程中的思路，换句通俗易懂的话讲制作组真的玩过自己做的游戏吗？游戏的出生地是在一片沙漠，但是你除了睡袋之外没有任何靠传送来缩短赶路时间的方法，等到把可以传送到各个石碑的物品做出来的时候，已经几乎是游戏的中期偏后期了，每次在遗迹或者地牢探索过程中途就暴毙了结果要从睡袋老家跑到死亡点继续战斗的体验我已经不想体验第二次了，简而言之，我作为一个本作的新手来说，前期和中期的体验基本上就是用双脚丈量整个沙漠，差一点就能跑到北边的什么人类屠龙者和东边的人类头领什么女巫的地盘上了。 所以不想折磨自己的话就开管理员权限进行副本传送吧。 3.重复使用的boss建模 我打到后面探索亡者之城和什么滓迷宫的时候，突然发现这些boss一个比一个眼熟，比如地牢里的深渊之蟒和亡者之城和竞技场的大蟒蛇，可以当boss又可以当小怪的酷似狼人的骷髅哥，明明建模一样，有的连色都不换了，调整个数值和大小就丢出来当小怪或区域大boss了。 4.越玩越感到乏味的真相 等到游戏中期，随从奴隶培养基本成型，说人话就是数值上来了，你就会发现基本上你的体验就是你明明站在旁边唯唯诺诺的不断走位翻滚，然后你的极品首领级动物或者传奇奴隶和boss单挑胜利后，一边摸着boss的尸体一边感慨道，“咱们三个真强！” 因为随从过于强大所以后期基本都是类似赛博斗鸡的战斗体验，玩家只需要别死就已经很不错了，基本上就像个小队的指挥核心，比如re0的男主486？反正你不是负责战斗爽的那个。可能扯得有的远了，总的来说意思就是随从小弟的数值爆炸导致了玩家和随从的战斗力严重脱节，特别是联机的时候，基本上都是4个小弟冲上去和boss互A，就看谁先顶不住。 5.基本没有的boss战机制 这个没什么好说的了，字面意思，boss只会三板斧，连快慢刀和机制都没有，这里只有最原始的数值碰撞 作为一个罕见的能让对生存游戏一直都不感冒的我上头猛肝4天，足以说明其亮点的优秀， 再加上重制版精美的画质，我仍然会给它一个好评

声音一直语音话筒音效，改了半天都没用。只要一联网自动开话筒根本改不了，只能断网玩。 我现在只玩了致远星，只能说真不咋地。战斗非常重复无聊，敌人和己方都有盾基本上一梭子才能打死一个小怪，遇到有盾有技能的精英怪就要打半天，重复开枪回盾再开枪回盾的循环。精英怪一多武器威力大的时候基本上就是在不停回盾，敌人打半天就是死不了，而且不得不说的一点就是这些武器射程太近了，一堆未来武器除了狙击枪几乎个个都是五十米射程，稍远一点不是没伤害就是打不中。而且明明枪半天打不死人，给的子弹还那么少，每一局都在到处找枪。 载具驾驶手感也是烂，到底是哪个天才想出的鼠标操作转向的，知道这玩意操作起来有多别扭吗？战斗机和外星人载具还好说，毕竟是可以射击和多方向移动的，人类那个越野车真难开，还不能边开车边控制机枪，结果就是开车ai打不到人，用机枪ai老是乱跑不给瞄准时机。 整个游戏重复性极高战斗不够爽玩的太累，作为一个老游戏没什么补票的必要了。 现在吧周年进化打完了。感觉上虽然周年在玩法上比致远星简陋很多，没有技能没有奔跑，但难度上要比致远星低多了。同样是困难难度，怪的盾和血条明显比致远星少，一两梭子子弹就能连盾带人一起带走。那个绿色的左手盾牌右手能量炮的怪，在致远星半天打不死，打要害要好几枪，但在周年里手枪要害一枪就死，正面也可以用手雷散弹枪直接打死。还有就是周年里越野车没血条，队友的血也很厚，一辆越野车可以打满全场。 当然缺点也有不少比如逃离那个关卡，指引太差让我迷路了好久，还有就是关卡重复都太高，跑到基地里拿数据在跑回来那段一张地图用两次很无聊。还有有些地方太难了没掩体敌人从四面八方用过来很难打，尤其是在上一个关卡子弹没剩太多或者武器不克制现在敌人的时候。 我总结的经验就是，激光枪是万能武器破盾，打洪魔都很好用，其次是散弹枪，近距离一枪破盾一枪打死，打洪魔近距离都是一枪死，其他武器都很一般。打绿盾怪最好用的是火箭炮其次是散弹枪，只要距离近怪就不会开炮用散弹枪一梭子内就能打死。还有看到载具能用就用，有一个桥上的关卡一开始停着一架飞机只要速度够快是可以强的，还有一个是敌人会开一架飞机和两辆幽灵打你，那关让队友吸引火力自己直接往存档点冲就行，不要尝试对抗。 总体来说游戏机制有些太老了，如果经常玩现代射击游戏的话可能很难适应，不太建议游玩，后面几部我也不太想玩了。
它的节奏很快，上手也不算难，选个角色进去打几局，很快就能感受到把人打飞出场的爽感。操作看着简单，但玩久了会发现里面还是有不少细节，走位、连招、武器切换、回场和追击都挺讲究。刚开始可能只是乱按。

光环4的优化也太离谱了，前面的几作都是开最高，到4直接给显卡干崩溃了（打一会直接黑屏加强制重启后显卡出小毛病），画质调为低再限制帧数才让显卡占用降下来，能稳定游玩；本作的剧情真是一言难尽，完全没有之前作品的故事感觉，基本是二人闯所有，科塔娜与士官长的情感交流也有些变味，然后序章对斯巴达战士的起源做了说明并有一些负面评价，但又跟后续剧情完全没关联，太诡异了，更别说主线剧情的星盟突然倒戈以及先行者的实力表现很低，唯一好的地方就是补充了先行者、古人类以及洪魔的故事，填坑了halo的由来。这4代前因后果完全没交代，要自行搜索他人总结的相关官方游戏外的设定补充，这太离谱了。 整个合集讲出的故事，感觉比质量效应的差些，没有明显的连贯性，尤其是部分情节的跳跃，整个故事并不能自圆其说，不算完整，尤其是一部分故事放在游戏外的周边上（甚至是游戏的部分新事物的发展过程放在其中，而完全没在游戏里提及），使得体验很差；游戏设计上也是纯粹的线性，不算半开放，没有构造出一个鲜活的幻想外星世界的画面，人物刻画也少，很多脸谱化甚至是酱油瓶型推动剧情的角色；大体上，体验一次不一样的射击太空旅行还是不错的，就是在沉浸感上略显单薄，但还是值得一试的。

游戏本身是相当不错的，很推荐给想要入坑这个游戏的新人朋友，当然这个游戏也有十分劝退的地方。 我主要活跃在移动与ns平台，并非steam。总游戏时长超700小时。 1.如果你只是把brawlhalla当作休闲大乱斗游戏（本质也是平台格斗），你可以玩得很开心（如果你有愿意和你一起玩的朋友）。但如果要体验它纯粹的格斗部分（特别是1v1模式），你将会被恶臭的环境（包括但不限于：嘲讽，被动，粪招复读）与惊人的elo机制恶心。 2.此游戏的服务器是土豆做的。大多数时候甚至挂加速器都无法稳定连上东南亚或日本服务器（这是距离中国最近的两个服务器）。 3.bmg在越来越多次的更新中，将游戏的平衡性做的很烂（主要是在1v1模式中），很多角色的攻击过于变态。 4.这款游戏的时间与学习成本是非常巨大的，上百小时才刚入门（这里同样指格斗技术方面的） 5.游戏对新手非常不友好。 总之，如果你只是想与朋友们（如果有的话）一起玩玩休闲大乱斗，你可以很快地在brawlhalla中寻找到快乐。但如果你想在格斗技术方面有所发展，你要做好吃苦与被恶心的准备。

8.5/10 挺超出预期的，也有不少的意料之中。 地图做得是真的好，像这种大片的沙漠地形其实是不太好设计的，毕竟除了沙子就是沙子，但这游戏硬是设计出了一片高低错落的，令人充满探索欲的大世界，画风既写实又魔幻也很加分，再加上有爬墙这个打破空间限制的功能，整个大地图的探索是充满了趣味的，哪怕没有奖励，有时候我就想爬上某个高塔上看看也很满足。 游戏机制也很对味。一是没有回档，所以不能像其他游戏那样仗着能回档瞎作死瞎试错，每一个决策都必须过脑子，一旦乱来就很容易暴毙，然后就飘洋过海来捡尸体吧，我觉得这其实正是生存游戏应该给到的压力，如果时间可以任意回溯，那死亡还有什么威慑力呢？死亡都不怕了，还生存个毛。二是完全无引导，这里说的不是说像大部分生存游戏的那种弱引导，就是用一些稀有资源或宏伟奇观把你吸引过去，然后触发主线剧情等等，这游戏压根就没有任何主线剧情，也完全不在乎你要在这个世界里干些什么，也不会给你生存压力来逼迫你收集资源发展科技，它只负责把世界搭建好，然后把玩家丢进去，你就依着本能自己给自己找事做吧。 以上几点，让我实在是很惊喜，这和那些最顶尖的开放世界游戏是一样的思路。但是越玩到后面，小毛病就暴露得越多，不算致命，但整体品质也就到这了。 最值得吐槽的毛病就是生态这一块。如果说这游戏在静态风光上做得又多好，那它在动态活物上就有多烂，分为动物和人和奴隶。动物，初见还好，给人危机四伏的紧张感，到后面越熟悉，越觉得它们完全就是被设置好的机关，你一进入监测范围就触发，虽然游戏本质上都是这么个原理，但这游戏做得也太僵硬太明显了，各种动物都是行为模式一样的换皮机关，就不能加点差异，加点生态？它们除了等着扑我以外就没有自己要干的事吗？纯纯机械路障。人类，就更糟糕，一类是和动物没区别的机关，另一类中立的则纯纯木桩，不能对话，也没有自己的生活，纯站着...明明这游戏开局就有那么多种族那么多宗教，蛮王柯南这个IP也有着庞大世界观，本可以有很多有趣的人文风光，结果这里面的人类却全被做成了僵尸，真的太可惜。奴隶，能跟随的还好，那些放在家里的，那真是硬邦邦的纹丝不动啊，前面那俩还算是僵尸，这个就已经是标本了。。。不要说这些是不重要的细节，首先开放世界游戏的NPC要有生态这本就是基本要求，不然哪来的“世界”感，再者这游戏地图做得这么庞大瑰丽，结果内里空空洞洞，本来旺盛的探索欲逐渐变成了习得性无助的疲惫感，大优点硬是被拖成了缺点。 总之，还是很优秀的，甚至有成神作的潜力，甚是可惜。补上了生态和人文这一块，就会是另一个世界观的《天国拯救》了。

只推荐《光环：致远星》。 以下是原因，可能涉及剧透，所有评价仅限战役模式，无法评价多人模式因为没玩过… 光环 1：关卡后期重复拖沓，没有载具抢夺，没什么亮点 光环 2：其实光环 2 做得相当好，不管是剧情、过场还是双持武器系统，但依然有关卡重复的问题 光环 3：可能是个人原因，但尸脑兽那关真的想吐，以及，前作中的俩好朋友在这里被送走了，非常不爽 光环 3 ODST：故事设定和 2 的剧情是平行的，以 ODST 的视角讲了另一个故事，挺有趣，但是前期关卡流程上时间线切换太多，比较乱 光环 4：呵，喜欢我 343 工作室拉的吗？时间线上与 3 相隔太久，中间发生了什么需要自己场外找资料去补；关卡重复度还是老问题；武器上值得吐槽的是，先行者这么领先的科技，结果武器难用得要死？最高难度下先行者敌人很难对付，可以说完全就是灌满伤害才能打死，根本没有前面几作的趣味啊；剧情方面雷比较多，最后科塔娜走了，你猜我玩下来感觉到了啥？ 光环致远星，讲的是光环 1 发生前的故事，故事不长，结局很坏，致远星陷落，但是玩家不必去走完其他几部的流程，也能了解到这一作中的 noble 小队的所有努力都没有白费，最后一章的氛围烘托十分到位，代入感极强。是我心目中光环系列里的神作，没有之一。 唯一一个可能没做好的平衡点是最高难度下的太空战部分（哪一章忘了）太弱，基本就是玩家被敌方飞行战斗单位咬着打。

先说结论：它仍然是你能找到的画面最精致的太空船建造模拟器（除了自家的SE2），但不能当做合格的太空探索游戏来玩。 先说结论的前半部分，作为模拟器，游戏自带了海量的方块可以使用，旋转，伸缩，折叠，各种可动功能都有，星球，太空，无缝衔接，编程块更是实现了要啥功能自己做的可自定义性，如果还不够，还有创意工坊来供玩家选择，建造这一块可以说同类领先，画面曾经过多次改进，现在看也仍然不算落后，美术风格也算得上美观。 然后说后半部分，作为太空探索游戏，十年过去了，它仍然不及格，即使经过了近几年的修修补补，其本质仍然还是当年那个造完船就几乎没事干了的造船模拟器，现在的更新更像是加进去了几个挑战任务来让你测试飞船，还远远谈不上真正的游戏体验。 最后是针对开发组的开发态度，如果说他们没在开发或者不知道玩家想要什么，那是假的，但又很难说得上勤奋，差强人意这个词，可以说是对他们最好的形容，也就是仅仅略微高于及格线，没完全摆烂的程度。 总而言之，就像开头说的，截至目前为止，合格的造船模拟器，失败的太空探索游戏。（顺便祝我自己能活到后半部分也合格的那一天）

It was weird when it released, but it has gotten much better over years. I’ve been playing on and off for years and finally decided to write a review. On the plus side: The gameplay loop is fun, there is a plenty of different modes, and you don't even need to play against real players if you don't want to. (Expert bots are better than 70% of the playerbase, beware, they are scary). The game also has good optimization. On the downside: Most players are on the asian server, so expect longer queue times if you are elsewhere. The learning curve is also rather steep; being stunlocked until you figure out all the animation cancels and timings is basically a given. (Again, expert bots are a good learning tool here). Overall, if you are interested in wuxia themes, battle royale, or extraction modes, it's definitely worth a try. Game is f2p but you can only buy cosmetics, no gameplay related power items.

放两年前我刚玩完那会儿评价，肯定开口就是“神作！此生必玩系列！” 但这两年看过很多人的负面评价“操作难受，晕3d”“引导弱”“流程太长”“难度太大”“手感一般”后，我就知道，半条命2注定只在我这里是一部好作品了。 毕竟1000个人眼里有1000个哈姆雷特，没有什么游戏是所有人都喜欢的，即便是这种被玩家圈里公认的好作品。 （P.S.沟槽的v社为什么把半条命整合了呀，搞的当时我原本打的全成就没了，最后只能通过下载第一章和第二章然后重新导入成就，所以这也是为什么我成就都是基本同一个时间开的，你们要看可以去看我库里那个半条命2第一章和半条命2第二章的成就，这个现在已经被v社归类到插件类和半条命2合并了，但当时是游戏，我就是分着下载玩的。） 虽然有以上种种，但并不妨碍这部作品在我这里的地位。 他帮我度过了我大学低配电脑那些年的窘迫和无味。那时候看着库里买的2077，战地1和底特律变人等等大作但是带不动，很是悲哀。 直到有天看到了半条命，买了橙色包后一发不可收拾，把这一整个系列都玩完了，而且还特意买了橙色包没包含的蓝色沸点和针锋相对这两部。 我感觉这个系列的游戏很对我胃口，不管是地图设计，武器手感，还有一代移动时轻微的晃动感，感觉太舒服了，除了画质和建模，给我的感觉不像是个二十多年前的游戏。 尤其是第二部，可以说对比一代是巨大的提升，武器丰富，玩法创新，角色ai比早期高级了好几个档次。当时在宿舍里玩的废寝忘食，打到进入联军控制塔后本来以为游戏都结束了，结果还有老长一段，给我整的激动的，差点熬夜。 以及那个不用枪械通关莱温霍姆的成就，很多时候极限操作给我玩的头皮发麻，那个场景和怪物的设计给人很强的压迫感，玩的时候感觉那些子爬墙的红色怪能爬出电脑给我吃了。 还有2结局重返城里集结那些流浪的反抗军然后带着小队跟联军对抗真的沉浸感拉满，在废墟下面躲三脚架机器时给我的恐惧感一直到后来玩死亡空间都没有再出现。 还有海边开车冲破一个个关卡，以及监狱里边操纵沙蚁边绕迷宫都让我印象深刻。算是我玩完后为数不多能每个环节都让我记忆犹新的游戏了，希望你在很多游戏都做不到，玩完就忘了。 我还给我弟安利，他也还好，玩到监狱末尾那一段，但后来也放弃了，果然这游戏还是不太适合现在。 如果现在让我评价他，那我绝对会说这是我steam上迄今为止买过最不亏的游戏。

《半衰期 2》毫无疑问在玩法创意，画面质量，引导水平三个方面做到的那个年代的顶尖水准。有些方面甚至是革命性的。 作为起源引擎的首秀，展现出了惊为天人的可交互性，即使在现代，拥有这种交互性单人FPS游戏也不多见。无论是地上的罐子或者木箱，游戏绝大部分物件玩家都可以捡起来或者移动，并且对npc或者玩家有碰撞反应。拥有重力枪时，可以重力枪吸起附近的物件射出去击杀敌人，或者把一些物件吸过来当跳板进行解谜。非常有趣味性。 在引导方面，不像一些现代游戏，往物件上涂上黄色油漆告诉你这有路可走。而是通过坏境的引导。我印象深刻的一个解谜应该是第二章的一段，应该是类似于滑轮的谜题，你需要把上面的洗衣机推下去让电梯拉不上去，从而搭建出一个跳板。这种引导，解谜在游戏中还有很多，但是来的基本恰到好处，V社对节奏把控的很好。这样的解谜不难，但又能给玩家足够的满足感。连我一个非常厌恶解谜的人都玩的很享受，基本没卡过几次关。 音乐也是顶中顶，好听而且非常契合战斗场景，更加战斗爽。 总结：12/10，必玩之作。即使在2026年的今天，它的gameplay依旧丝毫不过时。 现在真希望我有一台VR设备去玩alyx。

Naraka: Bladepoint is one of those games that feels strange at first, but once the combat finally clicks, it becomes incredibly hard to put down. The biggest strength is definitely the combat. Fights are not just about having better gear — timing, positioning, counters and knowing when to attack actually matter. Every weapon feels different, and there is always something new to learn. The movement system makes it even better, especially the grappling hook and climbing. Chasing someone across the map or escaping a fight by flying over rooftops never gets old. I also really like how much room there is for improvement. At the beginning, you will probably get destroyed by more experienced players, but after some practice you start understanding combos, spacing, counters and different hero abilities. Winning a difficult duel after that feels much more satisfying than winning a typical BR gunfight. The game also has a great visual style. The characters, weapons, animations and environments give Naraka its own identity, and the combat often feels more like a martial arts movie than a traditional battle royale. There are definitely some frustrating parts. The learning curve can be rough, matchmaking is not always fair, and ping/netcode issues can make certain fights feel completely out of your control. These problems can be especially annoying when you are trying to improve. Still, the core gameplay is so unique that I think Naraka is worth trying even if you normally don't like battle royale games. If you enjoy competitive combat and games where getting better actually changes how you play, this one can be seriously addictive.

⭐ Option 1 — Bold, energetic, hype-filled review Naraka: Bladepoint is honestly one of the most refreshing battle royale experiences out there. The game blends gorgeous wuxia and kung‑fu action with a cast that’s incredibly diverse — different cultures, body types, personalities, and aesthetics all represented with real love. NetEase didn’t just make a stylish game; they built one of the most queer‑friendly and welcoming communities in the genre. As a player who values inclusivity, it’s amazing to see LGBTQ+ folks openly enjoying the game without the usual toxicity you see in other BRs. The character creation freedom is wild. You can build beautiful, fierce, cute, masculine, feminine, and everything in-between. The sliders go deep, and the game actually lets you express yourself instead of forcing you into one look. And the skins? Let’s be real — Naraka has some of the hawtest outfits in any action game. Elegant robes, badass armor, seductive cosmetics, stylish streetwear… they know exactly what they’re doing. The kung‑fu combat is fast, fluid, and feels like you’re in a martial arts movie. Every clash feels personal, every dodge feels intentional, and every victory feels earned. NetEase really crafted something special: a game that’s not just fun, but free, expressive, and welcoming to everyone — especially queer players and BIPOC gamers. ⭐ Option 2 — More polished, review-style tone Naraka: Bladepoint stands out as a battle royale that celebrates diversity and player expression. Its roster features characters inspired by various Asian cultures, and the game’s deep kung‑fu and wuxia influences give every fight a cinematic flair. The character creation system is one of the best in the genre, offering players the freedom to craft unique identities rather than cookie‑cutter avatars. NetEase deserves credit for fostering a genuinely queer‑friendly community. It’s rare to find a competitive game where LGBTQ+ players feel comfortable and supported, but Naraka’s player base is surprisingly welcoming. The cosmetic designs also deserve praise — the skins and outfits are stylish, bold, and undeniably attractive, adding personality and flair to every match. Overall, Naraka is a standout title for players who value representation, creativity, and martial‑arts‑driven gameplay.

刚开始玩还行，到后面就会越打越红温，越打越烦。 就不说游戏本身的服务器问题和匹配机制还有各种的系统问题。 这个Brawlhalla本来一个非常好的格斗游戏，就是与各类格斗游戏一样是来体验不同角色带来的各种不同攻击形式以及不同的连击配合带来的快乐，但是这个游戏的机制并不是很鼓励你去体会和研究各种不同攻击形式以及不同连击，而是会让你变成只会重击放技能恶心对手折磨对手的状态。 因为游戏里存在着不同角色的重击技能都有不同形态的攻击状态和统一轻击的攻击状态，而且重击技能不会有任何代价，不费蓝不费时间而且伤害高范围大。 然而就是因为技能收益高大于低收益的存在，让这个游戏出现了只会盲目重击的游戏群体，而这群只会放技能的群体让这个格斗游戏变质了，变成了不再挖掘各种攻击连招和玩法，只会重击放技能的老赖。 我玩了五六年了，从没做过改变。有些人喜欢这个游戏就会去专研轻击配合重击带来的连招快乐，但是永远比不上只会重击的人群来得简单粗暴。你不停的攻击他很多下，不如对面放重击击中两三次就结束了，如果都鼓励大家用重击打人的话，轻击不如删了，连招教学也别放了。 强烈建议给重击附加一些条件 这行为就像盲人园丁一样，精确地挥舞那把荒谬的镰刀，把整片麦田变得无比杂乱。

I came back to Battlefield 2042 after playing Battlefield 6 and honestly I never expected to say this I used to hate Battlefield 2042 I was one of the people who thought it was a huge disappointment. But after spending a lot of time with Battlefield 6 I decided to go back to 2042 and now I finally understand what this game was trying to be For me, Battlefield 2042 is simply more comfortable and more fun to play. The visual presentation might not be as technically impressive as Battlefield 6, but I actually prefer how 2042 looks and feels. The image is clear, the characters are easy to see, the UI is comfortable, and the menus are simple and easy to understand. I can look at my loadout, weapons, attachments and character and immediately know what I'm doing. And the biggest thing for me is the sandbox. The vehicles, jets and helicopters are a huge part of what makes Battlefield feel like Battlefield. I love being able to spend time learning how to fly, practicing maneuvers, attacking objectives and just having those crazy Battlefield moments that you remember after the match. Battlefield 2042 also gives me that feeling of freedom that I personally miss in Battlefield 6. Now, Battlefield 6 definitely has some great things. The graphics are impressive, the animations are polished, the gunplay can feel satisfying, and the overall presentation is very modern. But after playing it for a long time, I started noticing things that really bothered me. For me, the visual design is sometimes too busy, the weapon presentation doesn't feel as good, and the overall experience doesn't feel as comfortable to read and play as 2042. The game can look technically incredible while still not looking or feeling better to my eyes. And that's the important part: Technical quality doesn't automatically mean better gameplay. I bought and played both games. I gave Battlefield 6 a real chance. And instead of making me forget about 2042, it actually made me appreciate 2042 more. So yeah… I went from: I hate Battlefield 2042. to: Why the hell am I having more fun here than in Battlefield 6? 😂 I'm going back to 2042, and this time I'm actually going to learn the game properly — especially the jets and helicopters. Maybe 2042 wasn't as bad as I thought. Maybe I just needed Battlefield 6 to make me appreciate it. Back to 2042. ✈️🚁🔥

9/10 I was not entirely convinced at first but upon learning the game, this has got to be the best battle royale ever made. Picture Sekiro-like combat on a set of different battle royale maps with a lot of characters, each having their own (gimmickey) set of abilities and playstyles that you can choose. It's melee favored, because ranged weapons are mainly used to poke the enemy before engaging or to catch them from escaping. Tare limited to durability and that takes time to replenish amidst the fight and to collect beforehand, upon other things that you will loot during the match. But that's of course not everything in the game. The combat is really high quality and despite what noobs might want you to believe; button mashing will quite literally get you owned. There is an increidbly in depth attack system full of combos, for every single weapon that can dictate your entire playstyle or approach to combat and a set of souljades that go from neat stacking buffs to literal alterations that enhance your current weapon attacks. There are some annoying and spammy ultimate abilities, however they can only be used once per fight and most of them leave you unable to chase, which makes securing kills pretty hard, as the movement in this game is probably the most important part. Whatever can't catch you, can't fight you. And whatever can't fight you, can't kill you. With that being said, when starting out freshly, there certainly should be a lot of players that will be able to defeat you, since that is how niche competetive games work. With not enough casuals the sweats start cannibalizing eachother and thats not even neccessarily a bad thing, but as a new player with an unrecognized MMR you will mostly fight against bots in the beginning until the game starts dropping in real opponents, Even if I know that the guy that chased me down through the whole match will probably end me, I can at least start learning his attack pattern, like with some Sekiro boss. Or maybe I could just sneak away and let him take out his wrath on some other unfortunate souls. That kind of experience is entirely unique to Naraka. The game is completely Free to Play and everything I describe in the following segment are purely optional cosmetics that do not alter the mechanical gameplay. The in-game store is detailed and if you don't find luck with mostly free lootcrates that have an unmissable chance system, should you get unlucky enough, You could also purchase some cosmetics directly from the store for mostly real money. However, the game to me seems quite generous and whilst I spent some real currency, I also got multiple legendary outfits, weapon skins and cosmetic accessories and extremes (even rarer) just by playing. Since the community on asian servers (f.e. china) is so large, there are tons of events where they hand out free stuff and I managed to get quite lucky with some legacy lootboxes. Sadly the only negatives I have to give is the games incredible size on my harddrive. Whilst that can be explained by tons of modes. Next to the usual battle royale casual, and ranked with solos, duos and trios, with some vanilla - like event modes or a team deathmatch. We also have f.e. the whole single player/ coop stuff the extraction mode, some event mode,.. Whilst everything is semi-regularly maintained, you can occasionally hit the 10-20+ GB seasonal patch, but that's probably just an internet (skill) issue on my end. It runs surprisingly stable and you will quickly have patched access to the newest settings (upscaling algorythms, etc) The only real bad thing that to me isn't objective is, that the game keeps getting shoved into a direction that to me looks more like a mobile game. Flashy new characters that basically force a disengage when ultiling since they will statcheck you. That#s not really bothering me though. What's awkward to me is the powercreep that leaves older and more beloved (and balanced and more fun to fight) characters in the dust. Then again, with enough gamesense on these aforementioned characters you can definitely still perform. Just maybe not as easily. It's a difficult debate and calling something "no skill" in an enviroment where "hold checking" has become the basic means of traveling the map on foot. Overall the best free game that I haver ever played. And I definitely haven't played enough, If you can give this game a shot and learn just the basics of the simple movement tech or combat 1&1, you will find yourself become anime. And that's also a feeling that no other game can provide. Also the trailers look dope every season.

推荐，非常好玩。 先说缺点，一个角色玩腻了想试试别的角色需要单开一个档，重新过一遍剧情，虽然可以跳过，但还是比较麻烦；然后虽然是出了很久的游戏，但社区缺乏详细且热门的攻略，需要花一定时间在查攻略上。谁懂搜攻略第一个视频点进去跟着跑图刷了几十轮都没出，又去查了阅览量小很多的攻略，然后看评论区才知道还有前置任务。虽然做攻略是纯热爱，但是既然要做至少要做全吧，当然也不排除老资历做攻略的时候距离当时已经过了很久，都忘记要做前置任务了；还有一个缺点就是这是个刷宝游戏，但刷装备很复杂。你打完boss没出，要退回标题再重进游戏刷新boss，这一点比较烦。如果是单人的话，反复刷花不了多少时间，但是多人的话就不行，很麻烦（而且这游戏居然还是鼓励联机的，在游戏说明中，联机的掉宝率会提升） 然后是优点。各个角色都很有意思，可以构筑不同的流派玩法，每个角色都很有特点；剧情的话中规中矩，而且dlc里的剧情有点辣眼睛，但是中配很有意思；说是刷宝游戏，但其实也可以当作是割草游戏。谁懂构筑好想玩的流派之后，在最高难度的怪堆里游龙割草的爽感啊！ 总的来说，有一定缺点，但是值得一玩。

从箱庭世界到巷战竞技场：战地系列地图设计的迷失与挣扎 战地系列的地图设计，在不少老玩家眼中，走过了一条从“精美箱庭”到“概念空壳”再到“巷战竞技场”的下坡路。这不是某一张地图的失误，而是一种设计理念的系统性偏移。 [hr][/hr] 大换血：制作组核心的流失 这种偏移的根源，首先指向制作组本身。据前DICE开发人员透露，参与制作战地系列的大部分核心开发人员都已经离开了EA。在经历了 战地2042 、 质量效应：仙女座 等一系列项目的挫折后，DICE工作室的老领导层离职，成立了Embark工作室，并带走了工作室一半的人才。EA随后聘请了 使命召唤 总经理来重建战地系列，新团队中98%的成员此前从未参与过任何一款战地游戏的制作。换言之，从 战地5 开始，那个缔造了 战地1 “箱庭世界”的团队就已经在事实上解体了。 [hr][/hr] 战地1：不可复制的箱庭标杆 回头看 战地1 ，它的地图之所以被反复怀念，是因为每一张图都像精心搭建的沙盘。地图里有大量可交互的场景道具——野战炮、固定机枪、可破坏的掩体，突破模式下的每一个据点都像一个小关卡，层层递进。战争巨兽的加入更是把“地图叙事”推到了系列巅峰：当一方被压制到濒临出局时，装甲列车、齐柏林飞艇或无畏舰会作为翻盘手段登场，让整张地图的节奏和情绪都发生剧变。这些巨兽不是简单的数值加成，而是地图设计的一部分——它们有自己的行进路线、攻击逻辑和弱点位置，迫使双方围绕它们重新组织战术。这种 “地图即玩法” 的思路，在后续作品中再未真正复现。 [hr][/hr] 战地5：设计退步的起点 战地5 的地图设计已经开始暴露问题。大量开阔平坦的地形让步兵举步维艰，医疗兵只有在20米内才能有效击杀，而机枪和突击兵却能在中远距离轻松压制。硫磺岛这样本应成为经典的战役地图，目标点设置在线性与非线性之间“纠结不清”，平地和山地地形割裂，最终只能被归入突袭式地图的范畴。玩家抱怨地图“平淡、扁平、过于暴露”，想要冲点几乎不可能。更令人遗憾的是，二战欧洲战场的标志性场景——柏林国会大厦、诺曼底登陆——在游戏中几乎缺席，取而代之的是一堆缺乏辨识度的村庄地图。 战地5 的欧洲内容远未兑现二战题材应有的史诗感。 [hr][/hr] 战地2042：概念先行的空中楼阁 到了 2042 ，问题从“设计退步”变成了“设计脱离实际”。DICE官方在核心反馈中承认了几个关键问题：128人模式导致地图过大，旗帜之间移动时间过长，玩家用“行走模拟器”来形容游戏体验；空旷空间缺乏掩体，视线问题严重，战斗变得分散。这些不是玩家苛刻，而是设计逻辑本身的矛盾——为了适配128人而放大的地图，并没有让战斗变得更丰富，反而让玩家在空旷地带疲于奔命。 更根本的问题在于， 2042 的地图像是从概念图直接搬进了游戏。首尔的大平地、高楼和中心数据中心想要营造“战斗高度差”，两张有大轮船的地图想要实现“室内外战斗切换”，但实际游玩中玩家根本进不到室内，这些设计意图完全落空，最终沦为打狙堵门的僵局。地图的“概念性”压倒了一切——宣传片里那些激烈的室内外切换战斗，在正常游玩中几乎无法复现。 2042 的地图像是一个大型概念展板，每一张都在展示“我们想做什么”，而不是“玩家实际会怎么玩”。直到最后几个赛季，DICE才开始收缩设计野心，把地图改回可正常游玩的状态，算是勉强收场。 [hr][/hr] 战地6：巷战竞技场的全面失控 如果说 2042 的问题是“太大太空”，那 战地6 的问题恰恰相反：太小、太挤、太像COD。 社区整理的数据证实了玩家的直观感受。 战地6 中最大的地图“火线风暴行动”重制版，其可玩区域在系列87张地图中仅排第32位，而原版排名第7；最大的原创地图“米拉克山谷”排第35位；最小的“圣徒区”是系列倒数第二小。第一赛季的“布莱克韦尔油田”引发了集中爆发的不满——地图太小、太线性、太开阔，重生点直接暴露在狙击手视野中，玩家刚重生就被秒杀的情况屡见不鲜。有玩家在Reddit上分享，驾驶喷气式飞机重生后立刻被激光标记，勉强起飞也只能飞出地图外约100米，根本无法穿越或躲避。更令付费玩家不满的是，免费大逃杀模式的地图设计反而优于本体多人地图。 但真正让老玩家感到陌生的是 战地6 的巷战地图。第一赛季的地图大量采用两层楼高的小屋和小巷，设计成四通八达、纵横交错的结构，前后左右随时有人冒出来，一堆人挤在狭窄空间里对射。这种设计的问题不在于“不好玩”，而在于它从根本上取消了战地系列的玩法多样性。当地图的空间尺度被压缩到巷战级别，载具就失去了存在意义——悍马又脆又难开，坦克数量极少，载具一出现就被打炸。没有空间让载具展开，没有距离让狙击手发挥作用，没有开阔地让团队配合产生战术纵深。 战地6 的地图像是直接照搬了COD的团队竞技地图逻辑——每个人都在近距离刚枪，地图的“设计感”只剩下通道和掩体的排列组合。 至于最新的海岛地图，情况更加微妙。第4赛季的“津留礁”在媒体预览中获得了不少好评，被评价为“可能是游戏发布以来最好的地图”，支持海陆空三栖作战，空中和海上载具都能找到发挥空间。但玩家社区的反应依然分裂——有玩家指出，这张图分几个区域，每个地方摆点能开门进去的建筑物，结构上更像是一个微缩的吃鸡地图，而非战地系列传统的大型沙盒战场。从好的一面看，DICE至少在尝试回归“大战场”的方向；但从坏的一面看，即便是系列史上最大的地图，其设计思路依然没有摆脱“分区+据点”的吃鸡式框架，而非 战地1 那种浑然一体的箱庭叙事。 [hr][/hr] 迷失的核心 纵观这条线索，战地地图设计的问题可以归结为一句话： 制作组不再理解“战地感”来自哪里。 战地1 的箱庭之所以成立，是因为每一张地图都是一个自洽的微型战场，有地形逻辑、有道具互动、有节奏起伏，玩家在其中能感受到“我身处一个真实的空间”。 2042 试图用规模制造“大战场”，却忽略了大战场的核心不是面积，而是战斗的密度和层次。 战地6 则走向了另一个极端，用巷战的紧凑感替代了战场的纵深，把“战地”做成了“有载具的COD”。 当核心团队流失、设计理念断裂、玩家反馈被忽视，地图设计就不再是“创造空间”，而变成了“填充内容”。 战地6 的首席制作人承认“需要更多大型沙盒地图”，这至少说明问题被看见了。但看见问题和解决问题之间，还隔着一整支理解 战地1 为何伟大的设计团队——而那样的团队，可能已经不存在了。

Obviously not the best Battlefield game, but definitely not the worst. I understand the hate and controversies the game has undergone, but from my experience so far, its not that bad for a Battlefield game. Yes a lot of the cosmetics are paid and can be very expensive, but you can't really expect them to be cheap nowadays. Most games sell expensive cosmetics, so you cant really blame EA/DICE. The gunplay and tactical aspects are decently balanced and polished, I love the gun customization, especially where you can attach multiple variants of the same attachment at once, though its not as a good and polished as COD games, its still really cool and fun to play with, especially for someone like me whose only ever played BF1 and BF5 (counting only BF franchise). In other words, if you haven't tried the game and are hesitant because of what people have said, honestly, I would personally say just try it out and see if it's for you. I was in this state too before I tried it out. And anyways, if you don't really like it, Steam's refund feature is there for a reason, and l40 - 60 minutes is more than enough time to get the feel of the game.

这游戏其实是一个3D机械拼图模拟器，套了个太空的壳子。 游戏是好游戏，也是真的折磨人 我的体验是：花三个小时精心设计的飞船，试飞因为推进器推力分布不对，直接在空中原地打转然后一头栽进地里，炸成一堆零件。然后就享受急头白脸地排除故障吧。(＾▽＾) 这个游戏不像按个按钮就自动飞起来的太空游戏。飞船能不能飞，取决于推进器的位置、陀螺仪的配置。一个管道不通，就飞不起来。 生存模式里，最开始只有一个初始车和三个废物工具。没有任何便利功能，就连一块铁皮都得自己焊出来。 但我刚刚玩的时候确实挺上瘾的( 先挖矿，造基础组件，再搭出第一个精炼厂和装配台，然后自己一步步升级——从手钻到采矿船，从步行到第一辆地面载具，从地面基地到轨道空间站。每一步都要自己亲历亲为地搭出来，没有任何捷径。 单人玩《太空工程师》是工程师模拟器，多人玩就是胡闹太空( 和朋友联机的时候，分工自然就出来了：一个人负责挖矿，一个人负责设计蓝图，一个人负责焊接组装。一艘大型飞船可能需要几个人配合好几个晚上才能完工。造好之后一起试飞，一起打基地，一起去小行星带采矿——这种感觉在其他沙盒游戏里很少能体验到。 当然也有翻车的时候，比如什么叫做队友把你的飞船开炸了( 当然新手引导就是一坨，建议购买前请仔细斟酌是否喜欢这种类型。购入后可以先去B站搜索新手教程，当然你要喜欢跟我一样自己探索发现坐大牢也是可以的( 还有星球表面确实是有些单调了，而且它DLC的定价着实离谱。

However, after moving to Linux I’ve had some strange issues. The most annoying one is occasional weird, slow-motion like gameplay that feels like low FPS without actual being it. When it occur it’s getting worse over time until re-log. It may have been fixed, I’ve haven’t played the game for some time, just coming back after a long break. Other issues has been and still are, error messages when starting the game. Latest one is a “Windows” popup dialog claiming the game can’t be started, but it starts just fine anyway. None of what I’ve seen has been game breaking though. One of the best thing with SE, is the Steam Workshop that contains tons of great mods where some completely change the goal in the game. Another advantages that need to be mentioned, is the way mods hardly ever gets broken after game file updates. I’ve been away from the game for up to a year and still been able to load old saves, continue to play without problems. I know of no other games with this advantage. Finally I need to mention the regular free updates that comes with cheap cosmetic DLC’s. In other games I can't even buy a single item for the price of what a full DLC in SE provides giving 20-40 items. Even though the devs are working on SE2 they still releases new content to Space Engineers.

Battlefield 2042 introduced the much needed self-hosted servers to the series, providing in-depth controls for creating and sharing custom scenarios. It also brought back official bot support, which was last seen in a limited capacity in Battlefield 2142. These addressed some major pain points in previous titles, where accomplishing similar things sometimes required third-party plugins or paid services. The game also sweetens the deal with a huge selection of maps and weapons, including content from previous Battlefield games. Despite all the bells and whistles, I can't overlook some game breaking bugs I've experienced that I didn't encounter in other Battlefield games. Disabling the EA overlay also strangely disables the Steam overlay. The game controls would often become unresponsive, a problem many have experienced and EA has been aware of for many years now. The "Create a Squad" button would also frequently fail to let me create a new squad when hosting a bot game. Hazard Zone, the extraction shooter mode, is currently a ghost town. With 3 achievements tied to it, it'll require the coordination of a minimum of 8 players to start this mode and complete the game's achievements. Overall, there's a lot to like here and it's worth trying at the heavily discounted price, especially with the amount of customization and content available, but the technical issues make it difficult to overlook the game's rough edges. My viewpoint is from a very late stage in the game and I'm passing through for the achievements but I cannot imagine dealing with these issues daily without an official fix.

After almost 250 hours on this game I've concluded the following: - 1) THE GAME IS IN DIRE NEED OF A DEDICATED 1V1 GAME MODE - The current "lobby" 1v1 game mode is very slow and bottle necked due to its current structure. The current structure forces players trying to do a 1v1 battle to just sit there and watch as the whole lobby franticly fights to be next in que, waiting around 1 stone statue to be next in line. A dedicated "1v1" game mode, that also gives you a rank like "bloodbath" game mode, would be an excellent addition to this game, Providing more dynamic choices for play styles. - 2) THE GAME DOES NOT SUPPORT PLAYSTATION CONTROLLERS PLUGGED INTO PC. - As an older gamer, i still enjoy using my controller on my pc when playing this game, however, due to the games lack of compatibility for different controller types, I am forced to whip out the old Xbox controller instead, which as much as we love Xbox, the controller is not my favorite for daily use. This game would benefit significantly by focusing on this patch note, thus be able to reach a larger player base for people coming from the console world and joining us in the pc world. - 3) POSTIVE FEED BACK AND RECOGNITION. - The game has been making successful updates for years now, which shows this piece of art work will continue to evolve as time progresses. This is very important for a player base that stays loyal to the platform over the years. ( we want to make sure we are not forgotten about). NARAKA BLADEPOINT has successfully shown us that they have not forgotten us and have done what they can to listen to the community and take our feedback in stride to help evolve the art work as time goes on. The in game fight animation and mechanics and overall game play in both PVP ONLINE, PVE OFFLINE, have made a touch to them that feel like the perfect diamond in a rough that will continue to shine for ages. I wish NARAKA all the success in the world for there future and provided these adjustments are made, I can see the game going to the next level of major adoption real soon!

I haven't come across any game that requires players to change their BIOS settings until Battlefield 2042. This is the first one, and there's no intention of being sarcastic. This is truly a genius anti-cheating design. It catches cheaters before they even start the game. If you don't have the intelligence and energy to independently change the BIOS settings, you don't deserve to play Battlefield 2042. This significantly eliminates the disruption of the gaming experience caused by novices and cheaters. Although there are no players at all. I think if the planes of the 9/11 terrorists had crashed into the EA headquarters in Redwood City, California instead of the Twin Towers, humans would have already colonized other star systems and left the solar system. 直到《战地2042》之前，我从未遇到过任何一款游戏要求玩家修改BIOS设置。这是第一款，而且我并非讽刺。这真是一项天才般的反作弊设计，能在作弊者甚至还没开始游戏时就将其拦截。如果你没有足够的智慧和精力去独立修改BIOS设置，那你根本不配玩《战地2042》。这极大地减少了新手和作弊者对游戏体验造成的干扰。尽管现在根本没有任何玩家。我想，如果9·11恐怖分子的飞机当时撞向的是位于加利福尼亚州红木城的EA总部，而不是双子塔，人类或许早已殖民其他恒星系统，离开太阳系了。

1. FPS 发展史的教科书，当年直接重新定义线性叙事射击，没有强制播片，全程保持玩家第一人称沉浸感。 2. 重力枪是游戏设计的神来之笔，利用物理环境解谜杀敌，这个玩法放到 20 多年后依旧新鲜感十足。 3. 17 号城的压迫氛围塑造无敌，联合军占领下的压抑末世，配乐、路人台词、环境细节全部服务世界观。 4. 莱温霍姆小镇永远是经典名场面，紧张恐怖感拉满，神父这个 NPC 塑造至今很难超越。 5. 汽船 / 越野车长途驾驶段落争议很大，喜欢的觉得沉浸，讨厌的觉得重复跑路，节奏拖沓枯燥。 6. 老游戏枪械手感偏厚重，没有现代 FPS 顺滑的反馈，习惯 COD、泰坦陨落的玩家上手会不习惯。 7. 20 周年更新自带优质中文语音，配音水准很高，重温体验提升巨大，对国内玩家非常友好。 8. 创意工坊 MOD 生态极其繁荣，无数民间重制、剧情 MOD，通关本体之后还能玩大量衍生内容。 9. 敌人 AI 有年代局限，有时行为比较僵硬，怪物种类不算多，战斗模式后期略有重复。 10. 结局戛然而止，故事并未完结，一定要连着 EP1、EP2 一起玩；只玩本体的话会卡在悬念处意难平。

So what's it about? In POE you are a criminal sentenced to death but instead shipped to the cursed continent of Wraeclast. You start with nothing and end up fighting Gods and other divine being. But to get there you will go through many beautifully crafted levels with many systems. At first it is intimidating and for your first run I highly recommend using a guide from for example Mobalytics . POE is an older game but can be measured against new releases as it has received and continues to receive updated. I've been an avid fan of Diablo and Diablo 2 since they were released (I was one of the first in D2 in Europe to hit lvl 99 back in the day). D3 was OK but not what I was looking into an ARPG and I've avoided D4 ever since the "don't you have phones" and all of the monetization; it's clear the Blizzard of old is no longer there. POE is F2P but it doesn't mean P2W. Every couple of months new supporter packs are released that are time limited. But they are just cosmetics and the game comes with plenty. Only buy those if you want to support the developers. At most you probably spend about £30 to make your life easier with more inventory tabs but only gets those after you've played the game for a while and it's still not required for the first play through but it will help a lot managing all the loot you collect later on. Consider the campaign the trial or demo version to see if the game is for you. You pick one of the available 7 classes when you start the game. As you progress you can then further specialise the class in the direction you like. There is so much to choose from that it will keep you busy for a long time. The campaign has 10 acts and those are really just the tutorial to avoid overloading you with the many systems POE has. After that the real game begins and it's all about completing maps at an increased difficulty for better rewards. Following that you arrive at the real end-game. It's a big game for sure :-). It's great solo but multiplayer is good too. There is even PVP if you're interested in that. The good It has the most extensive systems I have ever seen in any ARPG. Just the skill tree alone is massive. This allows for a lot of experimentation to find the ideal setup. Your class is just a starting point and you can adjust how you feel fit. I love the voice acting, the enemies and the graphical effects; GGG voice actors and artists are some of the best in class. There are many different leagues you can play (comparable to seasons in other games), including hard core and you can build even your own if you feel like. The developers play their game and there are frequent updates. Tournaments are organised and if you watch them on Twitch you even get nice stuff from time to time. The inner loot goblin is always satisfied when doing one of the many side activities in game. There is so much to collect and there is a variation of activities to keep it all fresh. You have your own hideout that you can decorate as you please. Later this becomes your central hub. There is in-game trading with other players and multiplayer is supported. There is also a trade post where you can buy and sell items you want or find. The game plays really fast at times - much higher speed than D2; which is great it’s a constant adrenaline rush. The drawback is if your build has a weakness there is little room for error on the high end levels as it leaves you with little time to counter act. The not so good There is definitely a deep learning curve hence I advise using a guide for the first play through so you get an understanding of the basics. End game (lvl 90 - 100) can be really challenging depending on your build. Some require expensive (as in rare items they are player trade) to be effective and the AI will relentlessly punish you if you have a weak build to the point you want to give up. To counter this you probably want to start with a character that is less depended on gear and more on skills which are easier to come by. A second build could be one that is more depending on gear as you can use the first character to farm where necessary. In general: ranged class / skills are easier than melee especially later in the game. For every new character you create you need to go through all 10 acts of the campaign; thankfully because of the stash, your hideout and all the other different game modes, including the progress in the second part (Atlas) is account wide it's not a major issue but it would be better if you would be given the option to skip the whole campaign after the first time that you've completed it (similar to like GW2 for example). I disapprove of the lootbox mechanic introduced every season. It's not required, it's not in your face but it can cause serious issues for people that are vulnerable to gambling addiction. The positive maybe is that all the loot from the loot boxes are released later in the MTX store but still it should not be in the game. The DLCs There are no DLCs other than supporter packs that only add cosmetics to the game. There is a microtransactions (MTX) store to buy cosmetics and QoL items. If you want to get any of those wishlist them and wait for a sale (every couple of weeks). Note that some of the MTX from POE is compatible with POE2 in particular most of the inventory tabs. Summary The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago, the second best time is now. This is true for POE. I wish I had discovered it earlier but I'm happy I did eventually. If you're into ARPG it's one of the best games to get. Highly recommended.

抛开剧情、人设、中文配音、各类大小bug、操作手感、战斗表现等等，消逝的光芒2依旧是当下最好玩的丧尸末日跑酷生存游戏！ 游玩到最终章还给我来了个死档的恶性bug，直接退档重来美美享受。 反派拉万的塑造非常成功，屡次想害死主角并且差点得手，站中间串四面八方也是主线剧情的核心冲突点；意气用事、冲动鲁莽、粗俗暴躁、毫无大局等性格特点也是经典反派形象了；外貌难评、脏话乱喷，还磕过药，一个底层混混形象跃然纸上；最后在主角的劝导下自我牺牲，这一反转大快人心，拉万终于悔过，尽显角色弧光。 剧情演绎到最终章才终于明白一名老父亲对女儿的深情，为了拯救女儿忍辱负重，不惜对自己生化改造，对抗各路妖魔神人，直到最后还想要利用导弹夷平城市，为人类铲除这么一个无药可救的鬼地方，正义之心令人动容。 相比第一代，这一作人类对抗丧尸末日明显轻松愉快得多，不仅幸存者众多，而且拉帮结派分成了三个阵营，还各自建立起了颇具规模的基地和各有特色秩序，而不用团结起来去对抗危险的夜魔和毒尸；不像第一部那样，幸存者都寥寥无几，安全点只能被迫建造在险峻的高处。看来到了第二部的时间点，人类战胜末日已经指日可待啦。 玩法上其实和第一部没有太大差别，钩爪的性能似乎更差一些，让人不爽。还给了不少多模式人任务，可惜单人玩家无福享受啦。（不要想着单人去挑战多人任务，牢） 建议打折到40元以下时，并且对第二部没有过多期待的游戏荒玩家再考虑慎重购买。好玩是好玩滴，毕竟消光系列确实有别于一大票经典丧尸末日游戏，据说相比刚发售时优化了很多，还给了一个拉万护眼版皮肤，现在肯定是能玩一玩的。坐等第三部困兽打折。

Battlefield 2042 sells out franchise tradition for cheap gimmicks. If you are thinking of picking up Battlefield 2042, think twice. It is a deeply disappointing entry that completely abandons key series staples, offering a thin, unpolished package that fails to justify its full asking price. Here is why you should stay away from this installment: • No Campaign or Narrative Anchor: In a lazy design shift, DICE opted to forego a single-player story campaign entirely to focus exclusively on multiplayer. Without a narrative mode to add value, teach mechanics, or anchor the experience, the severe lack of core content becomes painfully obvious the moment you launch the game. • Extinct Game Modes: Matchmaking is a complete ghost town for anything outside of standard play. While you can find region-based matches for basic Conquest and Team Deathmatch, the rest of the game is effectively dead. The heavily marketed Hazard Zone mode has been completely abandoned, and the lack of meaningful post-launch content updates means the few active modes get boring fast. • Cheap, Free-to-Play UI: The user interface and HUD feel shockingly unpolished and low-quality. Instead of looking like a premium, triple-A military shooter, the menus and in-game displays look like they were ripped straight out of a cheap, generic free-to-play mobile title. • Aggressive Microtransactions: Progression feels hollow and unrewarding. Instead of earning cool unlocks through gameplay milestones or traditional reward crates, the progression system has been gutted to push microtransactions. The game constantly pesters you to spend real money on paid operator bundles and weapon skins. Final Verdict: As a daily shooter, this title falls completely flat and cannot be recommended over superior options on the market. If you are absolutely determined to try it, do not pay full price—put it on your wishlist and wait for a steep discount.

Most of the people giving this game a thumbs-up probably don't even play it anymore. A lot of the positive opinions seem to come from nostalgia or a few flashy gameplay moments. But if you actually play the game seriously, you quickly realize how many frustrating mechanics it has. Here are just a few examples: * **Advanced-tech wars:** The moment you reach the advanced tech era, suddenly BARBAR TANKS or BARBAR SAM launchers start spawning out of literally nowhere. No warning, no reasonable explanation — they just appear because the game wants to punish you. You can be rich, powerful, and well-prepared, and the game basically says: *"Oh, you're doing well? Let's make your gameplay poor and bad because we can."* * **DLC multiplayer:** The game is so badly designed that if YOU own a DLC but your friend doesn't, your friend can't properly join/play with you. It's basically the game saying: *"Your friend doesn't have the DLC? Too bad. Go play something else with your broke buddy."* So yeah, nostalgia can make people remember this game fondly, but nostalgia doesn't magically make bad mechanics good. If you're looking for a strategy game, there are plenty of better options. **Don't play this just because people remember it fondly.**

### Conan Exiles: A Game That Left Its Most Dedicated Console Players Behind I have spent an enormous amount of time 4854 hours and money on **Conan Exiles**. Like many long-time players, I supported this game through DLCs, expansions, cosmetics, and countless hours of gameplay. That is why it is so disappointing to see the direction the game has taken for console players. The biggest problem is not that Conan Exiles is an old game. Games age. The problem is that **the players who supported Conan Exiles for years feel like they have been left behind.** Funcom has continued moving forward with enhanced versions and newer technology, while a large portion of the existing console community has been left dealing with an experience that increasingly feels outdated and neglected. ### Console Players Paid for the Game — Yet Feel Like Second-Class Players Many console players have spent hundreds of dollars supporting Conan Exiles over the years. We bought the expansions. We bought the DLC. We bought the cosmetic packs. We invested thousands of hours into our characters, bases, clans, and servers. And yet when improvements and enhanced technology arrive, those same players can be left wondering: **What exactly did all that support get us?** The expectation isn't unreasonable. Players aren't asking Funcom to give us something for nothing. We are asking for the same level of attention and consideration given to other platforms. ### The Server Experience Has Become a Major Problem One of the biggest issues is server performance. Lag, rubber-banding, delayed actions, disconnects, and inconsistent server performance can make the game incredibly frustrating. For a survival game where combat, building, farming, and PvP all depend on server responsiveness, this isn't a minor inconvenience. **Server performance is the game.** When you can spend hours building something, gathering resources, fighting enemies, and maintaining a character only to have the experience ruined by server problems, it becomes difficult to justify continuing to play. ### And Then There Is the Population Problem Another major issue is the declining player population. It becomes a vicious cycle: Fewer players means fewer active servers. Fewer active servers means fewer people to play with. Fewer people playing means even more players leave. Eventually, longtime players log in and find that the world they invested so much time into simply doesn't feel alive anymore. That is particularly frustrating when the game itself still has tremendous potential. Conan Exiles could still be an incredible long-term survival MMO-style experience. The foundation is there. The problem is that the community needs to feel like Funcom actually wants to keep those players. ### The Community That Supported Conan Exiles Should Matter What bothers me most is the feeling that the people who helped keep this game alive are being forgotten. Content creators, streamers, server owners, modders, clans, and everyday players spent years creating communities around Conan Exiles. They promoted the game. They brought their friends into the game. They bought the DLC. They maintained servers. They created videos and streams. They built enormous communities around it. Those people weren't just customers. **They were part of what made Conan Exiles successful.** When those players start saying they feel abandoned, Funcom should be listening. ### Curators, Streamers, and the Players Who Actually Supported the Game There is also a growing disconnect between how the game is presented and what many longtime players actually experience. You can watch streams, promotional content, curated gameplay, and videos showing Conan Exiles at its best. But longtime console players know that the actual experience can be very different. A game can look great in a curated video while the average player is dealing with lag, low-population servers, technical problems, and an aging console experience. That doesn't mean streamers or creators are doing anything wrong. It means **Funcom needs to address the difference between the best-case presentation of Conan Exiles and the day-to-day experience of the players who have supported it for years.** ### This Isn't About Wanting Everything for Free I want to make that clear. This isn't a complaint from someone expecting endless free upgrades. The complaint is about **value and respect for the existing customer base.** If players have spent years buying DLC and supporting the game, they should not feel like their platform has been abandoned while the company moves on to newer technology. At some point, you have to ask: **Why should a player continue investing money into a game when they aren't confident that their platform and community will continue to receive meaningful support?** ### Conan Exiles Still Has Potential The frustrating part is that I still like Conan Exiles. That's why this criticism exists. If I didn't care about the game, I wouldn't bother writing this. Conan Exiles has one of the best foundations for a survival game: building, exploration, combat, thralls, clans, sieges, crafting, progression, and an enormous world. But the game needs more than new cosmetics and additional monetized content. It needs **investment in the player experience.** It needs better server performance. It needs a healthy population. It needs meaningful support for console players. And most importantly, it needs to show longtime customers that their years of support actually mean something. ### Final Verdict **Conan Exiles is a great game that is increasingly difficult to recommend to longtime console players.** The game itself deserves better. The community deserves better. And the players who have spent years and hundreds of dollars supporting Conan Exiles deserve better. Funcom shouldn't look at longtime console players as an old customer base that can simply be left behind. **We are the people who supported Conan Exiles when it needed us.** Now it's time for Funcom to show that it still supports us. **Rating: 3/5** Not because Conan Exiles is a bad game. But because the experience for longtime console players no longer matches the loyalty and money many of us have invested into it and the developers really don't care

It's alright. If you're sure you want to get into it, be sure to grab the ultimate edition and get the extra skill tree (yes, things like skill trees are locked behind DLC) I'm not one to lose my mind over "X-plotline kills off this character that I love or ruins this character" cause I'm not the most invested in Borderlands games, but I can sympathize with the people upset about that as there are games where that was a major problem for me. Gearbox has a pretty good (or bad, depending on your perspective) reputation for pulling this kind of stuff in their writing and game design though, so it's par for the course. What I will say is that your character and your party at large constantly feel like they are secondary, side characters to the *ACTUAL* side characters who push the plot forward, every sense of accomplishment you have from advancing the story gets overshadowed by whatever they're doing. Especially towards the ending, and that's pretty annoying to me. It's pretty abysmal storytelling and character development. It's fun, the different classes and skillsets is a step up from earlier games in this series that I have played... but you definitely have to overlook some pretty irritating game design and writing decisions to keep having fun. There are some questionable decisions here and there, some that can be solved with modding, others not so much. There are also some bugs, nothing that hardlocks the game but you might have to reset sections, go to main menu and restart, which sucks when you've looted some awesome gear and will now never see it again. 6.5/10.

My complaint about the dialogue: There's too much damn idle dialogue. in the first few hours, most of the game is spent standing around waiting for characters to either stop talking or to finish a walking animation. In Borderlands 2, most of the dialogue was during a task, so you were still playing the game while the characters were talking. But I guess the devs forgot that the point of a game is to play it, and they added too much idle dialogue. Even with the dialogue skipper mod, there's so many times where you just have to stand for about 30 seconds for characters to finish their animations. My feelings about everything else: There's a lot of QOL things added, however there are many things that they changed for the worse. For instance, the map scroll and panning speeds are terribly slow, it makes navigating them so unbearable awful. While BL2 required its own BL2 fix mod for the gun drops and levels, this game seems to have fixed that which is good. There's also too much walking and barely any checkpoints, it's another issue that I had with BL2. At least in this game you can TP to unlocked TP points from any location, you don't need to walk to a TP to teleport. But the issue is there are barely any TP locations, so even if you do TP, you have to either walk or drive an entire map's length to get to an objective, and when each mission has 5 objectives that go back and forth, it's pretty annoying. The gunplay is a bit different, it's fine I guess. It feels a lot more arcadey than the second, I honestly prefer BL2 gunplay more (and no it's not nostalgia, I never really played borderlands as a kid). The performance was really weird. My pc specs are attached, and usually I can hit pretty high fps with most graphics settings in most games, but my fps seemed capped around 120ish despite my gpu and cpu sitting at 40% usage. Personally, I would not recommend the game because of the dialogue and minor QOL things, just get BL2 and download some mods before playing (a bit tedious but def worth it).

I spent the night huddled next to the sheer cliffs by the beach. I was caught between a rock and a hard place. There was a brigand camp just a bit up the road, and the beach was infested with giant crocodiles which, I hoped, would be asleep. The huge moon rose over the mountains lighting everything with its eerie light. On the horizon, magical flares erupted with a crackling sound that gave me a start. I clutched the razor-sharp falcata sword that I found on the body of a bandit who'd attacked me a few days ago. If only I knew how to make such wondrous swords! The best that I was able to achieve myself was a primitive stone cleaver. That's why I was here, on this hostile shore, away from my humble camp, looking for ironstone which, I had heard, could be used to smelt that most valuable of all metals - iron. Armour, swords, iron-tipped arrows… all of these would be mine if only I could survive this adventure. I didn't dare to start a campfire and I welcomed the first rays of the sun with gratitude, even though I knew I would curse it during the day as it scorched my already brown-tanned skin. A beast roared as the sun rose and an avalanche of stones rumbled down a slope in the distance. I braced myself, ate the remnants of my dried fish and set off deeper into this dangerous but beautiful desert land. To be honest, I bought this game because it was on sale, and I never expected it to bo so utterly, amazingly good. I'm quite critical of modern games, which usually seem to be all about monetization. Here, I've played it for two days non-stop and I can see I'm only just beginning to comprehend how vast it is, even though I don't have any DLC. I've only visited a fraction of the map and I love the grind, which isn't too bad but you're not progressing too quickly either. As a result, you really get into the vibe of a lone exile, trying to survive on the edges of civilisation. A trek across the land, hiding from creatures that I know are too powerful to fight, gingerly skirting their territories, shows how fragile you still are at level 20, even though you might think you're tough because you've killed some minor creatures and fought off humans. Animals are territorial, they don't chase you forever like in some other games. They just want you to leave their territory but if you don't, they'll attack. They fight also with each other (I don't think I've seen this in any other game), not because they're scripted to do so but because their territories might overlap. Character customisation is great, especially with a few basic mods from the Steam workshop. One more thing: the music. To be honest, I normally switch music off in most games. Usually it's pretty generic, bombastic stuff that becomes boring rather quickly. This is different. The music is very varied, well suited to what's happening and adds to the suspense in combination with the amazing sounds of the jungle, roars of distant animals etc. All in all, so far - a great game, even if you're not a fan of the Conan universe.

So for Space Engineers, I'd say it's a great creative "engineering" game (though there's very little actual engineering involved), but I do need to caution anyone reading this, there's no learning curve; it's more of a learning "sheer cliff". Youtubers like Splitsie have helped me get over that learning cliff a little easier. This game will not hold your hand, there is no real story mode, but there are tutorial minigames such as "Learning how to survive". You build, you survive, you make your own goals and achieve them, which makes me think of other construction games like Minecraft, you have to figure things out on your own. I like to consider myself moderately intelligent in the field of engineering, currently I have logged over 300 hours into Space Engineers and I am still learning completely new things that I probably should have known from day 1. That said, you really, really cannot go into this game blind, you will regret doing so. If you're curious about buying this game, I'd say absolutely buy it, the options of what you can do are practically limitless, BUT, look up a beginners guide before playing, it will save you a ton of frustration. Trust me. To be fair it isn't really an engineering game so much as a creative mechanics game, because while yes, there are logic blocks and mechanical blocks you can use and program, there's hardly any real engineering going on here like you'd find in games such as Besiege. Think more like... if Minecraft was about traversing hostile space and had a wide variety of shapes rather than just blocks. I typically play peaceful games, so my main file is a customized peaceful mode which is nice. The combat of default settings can be rather unforgiving especially if you're new and don't really know what's going to happen. I still need to learn how to print things and how to automate drones, because that is a very complex thing to set up, but beyond that, it's much more of a build-and-destroy type of game, which is why learning how to print things is pretty essential; if your creations get destroyed, you'll save countless hours fixing or remaking them from scratch by learning how to print.

Recommended. This is still the best all-around survival crafting game in its class. I've played a lot of survival crafting games, and despite its numerous flaws, questionable business practices, occasionally hilarious combat, and my increasingly concerning collection of scantily clad female thralls, *Conan Exiles* remains the best all-around experience in the genre. First, the art direction is absolutely fantastic. The Exiled Lands feel like a genuinely dangerous, ancient, and often hostile world. From the scorching deserts and forgotten ruins to the frozen northern wastes and the oppressive jungles, there's a tremendous sense of atmosphere. The world feels like it existed long before you arrived and will continue existing long after something horrible eats you. There's a wonderful sense of mystery to the environments, and the developers clearly understood the assignment when it came to capturing Robert E. Howard's brutal, decadent sword-and-sorcery setting. And unlike a lot of survival games, Conan actually feels dangerous, particularly early on. You're not some chosen hero destined to save the world. You're a half-naked idiot with a rock, and practically everything wants to murder you. Even after you've established yourself, wandering into the wrong area unprepared can result in a quick and thoroughly humiliating death. That sense of lethality is something many other survival games lose far too quickly. The combat, meanwhile, is an interesting mixture of genuinely enjoyable mechanics and absolute slapstick nonsense. Sometimes you're engaged in a satisfying, bloody duel with a dangerous enemy. Other times you're watching your thrall attempt to navigate a doorway while an enemy performs what appears to be an interpretive dance before launching itself into low orbit. Hit detection can be questionable, animations occasionally have a mind of their own, and the AI sometimes seems to have suffered a traumatic brain injury. But there's something almost endearing about the jank. At least until it gets you killed. The building system is another major strength. The sheer variety of architectural pieces, decorations, furniture, and themed construction sets is outstanding. You can build anything from a miserable little desert shack to a sprawling fortress, an opulent palace, or a barbarian pleasure resort that would make Caligula blush. While *Enshrouded* arguably has the superior building mechanics, Conan's aesthetic variety and ability to create genuinely lived-in settlements are exceptional. Which brings me to the thralls. Let's not pretend this isn't also a glorified waifu collection simulator. You can tell yourself you're capturing thralls to improve your crafting efficiency, defend your fortress, or establish a thriving settlement. And sure, that's technically true. But sooner or later you're spending an unreasonable amount of time hunting down attractive NPCs, dressing them in increasingly impractical armor, and arranging them around your palace like some kind of deranged barbarian interior decorator. And I love it. The gratuitous nudity, absurd violence, dismemberment, and unapologetically adult atmosphere are part of the charm. This is Conan the Barbarian, not a Disney theme park. It's supposed to be savage, bloody, ridiculous, and occasionally horny. The game embraces that identity, and I appreciate that it doesn't feel compelled to apologize for it. Unfortunately, Funcom also knows exactly how much I enjoy decorating my fortress and dressing up my collection of barbarian murder-waifus, which brings us to the Bazaar. The microtransaction shop can be an obnoxious, overpriced cash grab. Some of the cosmetic sets are fantastic, but the pricing frequently borders on insulting. And yet, despite my principled objections to these business practices, I have personally contributed far too much money to perpetuating them. Apparently my outrage has a price, and that price is a particularly attractive set of Stygian furniture or another outfit for my digital harem. I am part of the problem. I accept this. There are other frustrations, of course. The game can be buggy, the AI is inconsistent, some systems feel unfinished, and the developers occasionally introduce changes that leave me wondering whether anyone involved actually plays the game. But the underlying experience is so compelling that I keep coming back. And that's ultimately what separates Conan Exiles from much of its competition. Valheim has its exploration and atmosphere, but its endless resource grind and tedious bosses eventually wear out their welcome. Enshrouded has phenomenal building and more fluid combat, but it never quite captures Conan's sense of danger or its wonderfully savage identity. Plenty of survival games do one or two things better, but very few manage to bring exploration, combat, survival, construction, atmosphere, and settlement building together into such a satisfying package. There's also something uniquely enjoyable about building a fortress in a hostile wilderness, filling it with warriors, craftsmen, dancers, and questionable architectural choices, and then heading out with your wife to explore some forgotten dungeon where you're both likely to die horribly. Conan Exiles is janky, occasionally infuriating, shamelessly monetized, gloriously violent, and thoroughly ridiculous. It's also still my benchmark for what a survival crafting game should aspire to be. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have to go complain about predatory microtransactions while purchasing another decorative bathtub for my fortress full of mostly naked women.

Recommended 210 hours in, single player only. I picked up Conan Exiles Enhanced a few months after its release, partly out of curiosity about Funcom’s previous major title after spending over 1,100 hours in Dune Awakening, and it more than held up. What keeps me playing is the non-linear progression and a truly open world. There is no set path: you go where you want and build what you want. The thrall system is the highlight. Tracking down and assembling the right followers is addictive on its own. Solo play works very well. The only custom setting I use is reduced stamina cost per action; everything else is at default. Downsides: gathering resources for higher-tier buildings gets tedious, though not enough to make me lower building costs. A couple of times after returning to the game, one of my thralls fell through the map and I had to use ghost mode to recover him. The Bazaar is interesting, but its prices are far too high for what each pack offers, especially compared to regional pricing. The DLCs are worth it on sale. The sad paradox of BL3 is that it features the best gameplay in the series, balanced out by the worst story to boot. Gearbox were a couple of steps away from making a generational masterpiece but somehow managed to cook up the most underwhelming narrative, annoyingly bland characters, and AI-level dialogue that silenced most of the redeeming qualities that the game had going for itself. The strangest part is that the DLC content in this game is absolutely phenomenal, and for the most part, feels like a polished product when looking back at the base game campaign. The story is what it is, but in the defense of Gearbox (yes, I cannot believe I'm typing that), there is a great game under the surface of the awful storytelling choices they made. On the other hand, the gameplay is addictive like crack cocaine, which is unironically the best in the series with its tech tree builds and unique weapon variety. BL2 andies will take offence to this, but hey, you can't win them all, so f_ck them as far as I'm concerned. Their judgement holds the same value as legendary drops in this game. I remember playing through the entire game and DLC content with one of my friends, and we had an absolute blast, which the Discord mod-level dialogue couldn't touch. Come to your own conclusions after trying it out.

【等打折】操控四人小队下地牢，讲究站位的回合制战斗很精巧，哥特恐怖的世界、美术和结局也很迷人。但英雄会承受压力，阵亡后还得补员、重新培养；我借助攻略和减负 MOD 通关，仍觉得反复刷资源、重练队伍很累。喜欢钻研配队和经营的值得玩，讨厌这些重复劳动的慎买。 踏入庄园的最初时刻—— 低沉的声音从阴影里传来，仿佛早已知晓我的下场。畸变、腐化的轮廓在黑暗中显露，我却只想再靠近一点，看清它们深处藏着什么。好奇心已经替我迈出了第一步。 刀锋的秩序 战斗自有其严苛的秩序。 双方各四个站位，技能的释放位置、目标范围都有严格限制。 麻风剑客的“挥砍”只能从己方前两位攻击敌方前两位，被推到后排就使不上。推拉改变可攻击的目标，眩晕让目标错过行动。队伍必须在这些限制中寻找配合。 我能欣赏这份精巧。坐在屏幕前，感到的却只有提心吊胆。 麻风剑客在要命的时候挥空，神秘学者在要命的时候奶不起来。 “命运重构”升满了依然可能奶零，还可能让目标流血。 指望它救回濒死的队员，就是把命交给命运。 局面一失控，我就非常火大，反复用左手横向揉眼睛和太阳穴。挫败感占满脑子。 [pullquote]战斗结束，队员尚存。那才是我的乐趣：我又亲手从古神那里，暂时吊住了一条生命。[/pullquote] 这条生命，造价不菲 我把一个主力英雄养到六级、升满技能、锁定好怪癖，得花数小时的心血和大量资金。他仍然可能死。 损失严重之后，又得招人、整队，带新人下低级本，重复刷钱和传家宝。 死者留下的空位，只能用更多时间填满。 治疗、建筑升级、出征补给，都在消耗资源。锁住“精准打击”“反应快速”这样的好怪癖，要花钱；移除固化的负面怪癖，更贵。队伍崩盘、钱袋干瘪的时候，城镇里每一笔开销都格外沉重。 骨灰盒、书架、祭坛，也值得提防。一次轻率的触碰，可能换来疾病、压力和新的治疗开销。该带什么补给，该碰什么东西，都得学。地牢连好奇心也要收费。 个别物件交互结果： “装饰瓮”里装着死者的骨灰。徒手摸可能中毒、染病，用圣水清理能找到财物。书架可能改变怪癖、提供地图，也可能增加压力。向“跛行者”祭坛献上火炬，则会召来怪物。 于是我频繁按 Alt+Tab，向攻略寻求指引。攻略帮我理清需要什么、接下来做什么。目标定了，我就能专心推进，少耗费一些心力。 我也借助减负 MOD，加快战斗和行走速度、增加资源获取量、提高物品堆叠数量、扩充背包、去掉某些负面效果。 资源忽然丰厚，起初很爽。很快，那份畅快消退，熟悉的重复又回来了。 支撑我玩到通关的，仍是对世界、剧情和结局的兴趣。庄园还有秘密，我想看个明白。 庄园的粉饰 正式冒险之前，我还给庄园做过美术装修。 创意工坊非常丰富。新增职业或引入新机制的 MOD，我嫌重新学习麻烦。我喜欢替换原有素材，把城镇 NPC 和手下佣兵换成漂亮妹妹。造型比较清凉，对领主比较坦诚的那种。 有些作者的本事令人佩服。加入更大胆的视觉元素后，仍守住了原版粗粝的黑墨线条与压抑色调。衣料可以省，阴影一笔也没少。 安装的苦工，得自己做。部分可选版本要手动找图片、改名、覆盖。我听着周杰伦的歌，一个一个换文件，枯燥地折腾了好几天，才开始玩。 漂亮立绘让我更舍不得她们死，也抚平过一部分烦躁。面容足以安慰领主，剑锋与治疗照旧听命于骰子。 领主的冷酷 我原本喜欢有塑造、有羁绊的同伴。庄园教给我的，是如何使用耗材。最初死人会心疼，死得多了，心疼便退下了。培养投入和补员成本，接管了我的判断。 “上一支小队的覆灭”“强盗为同伴断后”，都能脑补成小说。屏幕前的我却很清楚，自己只是在算怎样能少亏一点。 旁白会说： “一个聪明的将军会减少损失，然后重振旗鼓。” 我就这样学会了领主的冷酷。 通关后的得失 通关时，我觉得非常值。结局带来的震动，足以压过一路的疲惫。 如今冷静下来，再看那些重复刷取、重新培养的时间，我又觉得代价太高。 我依然超级喜欢它的世界、美术和结局。 强烈推荐给愿意钻研的硬核玩家，以及愿意花时间找 MOD 的普通玩家。 代价已经摆在这里。要不要付，由你决定。 [hr][/hr] 以下涉及后期机制和结局剧透 在“极暗地牢”中撤退，会随机选出一名英雄牺牲。我会为了保住剩下的人接受这个代价。这份损失计算，与领主的冷酷贪婪很契合。我个人不喜欢把人当耗材，仍认为这种契合做得极好。 到了“黑暗之心”面前，技能“到汝之造物主身边来”让玩家亲手点选一位英雄承受致死攻击。死者由我指定，账目由我结清。我印象里，这些耗材忽然一个个表现得像英雄。 核对官方台词后，发现他们的反应各不相同。 十字军说：“不洁的邪恶！我要和你同归于尽！” 驯犬师安抚自己的狗：“冷静，姑娘。如果叫到了我们，我们回应就是。” 瘟疫医生喊：“不要选我！我是个博学的学者！” 修女则是：“这……这太可怕了！不！！！！！” 那场告别当时打动了我。回头想，我早已习惯按培养和替换成本看待他们。告别忽然要求我感受更多，显得有些突兀。 结局开口就是： “胜利。多么卑鄙又可笑的说法。” 黑暗之心既是生命的源头，也是最终的毁灭者。人类只是“离经叛道的血肉”，由它而生，也将回到它之中。脚下的泥土与岩石，是它脆弱的外壳。群星再度排列，它还会苏醒、破壳而出。耗尽无数生命，只让灭亡暂时迟来。 祖先让你担起“毫无意义的看守之责”，片尾又响起：“……我们的家族，没落了。”开场的召唤，在结尾再次回响。我也被留在这个循环里。 求知欲凿开深渊，贪婪把诅咒留给后人。我们耗尽生命与时日，宇宙仍旧沉默。 This is in many ways a fun game. It is also a game that uses the Unreal Engine, an engine managed by Epic Games. In buying this game or any other game using the Unreal engine you thereby support Epic Games, either through providing positive metrics/attention for their engine or possibly through royalties (depending on the arrangements between the game’s developers and Epic, which I am not privy to). Epic Games’ senior leadership has publicly opposed mandatory AI notification in storefronts like Steam, on the technofatalist grounds that AI proliferation within videogame development is inevitable and that such notifications, which (especially if properly enforced) enable resistance to this proliferation by consumers, are thus pointless. In doing so this leadership (which may or may not be good etc. in other respects) has positioned itself and the company it represents as traitors to humanity in a general struggle against replacement by AI systems which is much bigger than videogaming or any one industry, or indeed questions about which toys to play with. Inasmuch as buying this game supports Epic Games’ business, as a matter of practical politics one is supporting its leadership’s continued power and advocacy for the replacement of human work and artistic agency by AI systems. One thereby, as a human consumer, commits practical treachery against one’s species. For this reason one cannot in good conscience buy this game or its DLCs. I was unaware of all this at the time of purchase and will not be playing or buying DLCs for this game in the future, in solidarity with anyone moved by this argument. This stance is grounded in something much bigger than videogaming or any questions about game quality or fun-ness. This is about having a future, for there is no tolerable future lived alongside unchecked AI proliferation. Developers caught in the crossfire of this stance have my sympathy, but I hope they will understand that this is a fight (and it is a fight, which should be fought as much as practical throughout one’s life as a worker, consumer, investor, or political agent) for their future just as much as everyone else's.

text_clean: My all-time favorite game, but I can only give it one star I’ve put hundreds of hours into Skyrim across multiple saves. Two of my old playthroughs never hit the Chillrend sound bug at all, but my newest save finally ran into it, and it’s so frustrating. Chillrend has a looping frost hiss sound when drawn. This bug happens when the audio stop command gets lost during cell changes, loading screens or quick weapon swaps. Unlike Dawnbreaker or most enchanted weapons that only play a short one-off sound, this is a looping effect. Once it glitches out, the sound sticks to your character forever. Sheathe the sword, drop it, even delete it — the noise stays. It survives restarts and save reloads. Open a menu and it quiets briefly, only to come back right after. Pull Chillrend out again while the bug is active and you stack multiple layers of the hiss, which gets painfully loud. Since I play in third-person, I only noticed this Chillrend audio bug much later, forcing me to load a save from dozens of hours back and wasting days of my playtime. The vanilla workarounds are janky at best. Using `sexchange` twice or turning into a werewolf can temporarily clear the sound, but it comes back on reload. Worse, `sexchange` breaks the Ranger archery perk and removes its movement speed boost. There’s no reliable native fix in the base game. Trying to force-trigger the stop command by sheathing and teleporting at the same time only makes it worse and adds more overlapping audio. And it’s not just the Chillrend bug. The Creation Club homes are packed with well-known issues too. Weapon racks and plaques eat stored weapons, many display cases won’t accept gear. Dragon claws float off their mounts. Some adopted kids can’t move in, pets sometimes vanish or get sent to the wrong house. Mannequins lock onto one set of armor, push out any new gear you put on them, and duplicate that old armor when you leave the area and come back. Items jump all over the place every time you enter these homes, way more so than regular Hearthfire houses. Most display cases don’t work properly as displays at all. Serana also has her own annoying bugs. She will stop following you in basements and can disappear randomly. Her hood duplicates infinitely, stacking hundreds of copies in her inventory and making trading items impossible. On top of all these bugs, the base game volume is way too low. Compared to nearly every other game, even older ones like GTA V, Skyrim’s overall sound level feels like it’s only one third as loud. Every single time I boot it up, I have to crank my system volume. When I finish playing and jump on TikTok without turning it back down, the sudden blast of sound has startled me and even gotten me complaints from neighbours. I don’t want to sound harsh, but it’s unbelievable that pirated versions of Skyrim can run better with fewer bugs. The only extra thing this official version offers is the pointless achievement system. It feels like Bethesda just doesn’t care about polishing these long-standing quality-of-life problems. The community has to make mods to patch everything for them. Players end up doing the dev team’s job instead of just enjoying the game. It’s disappointing. GTA V is just as old, yet it feels polished and optimized. Meanwhile Bethesda chases big projects like Starfield. It’s like taking a warrior and forcing them to slog through boring, drawn-out religious texts. It is my all-time favourite game, yet also the buggiest. Bethesda is just as arrogant as Valve is with CS2. But my negative review reflects my real experience. I’m here to play a game, to enjoy something as a person, not to suffer and do your work for you.

Conan Exiles – this is a game about a time so ancient that logic was yet to be born. It is a land of might and magic, legendary creatures, and desert-mountain-climbing crocodiles. A land where common sense has yet to be invented and master craftsmen make things purely by guesswork. This positive review is based on a solo, heavily modded playthrough, so let’s start with the cons first. I don’t know why, but "the game" (which is what I’ll be calling the devs from now on) really hates logic and common sense in general. It’s practically allergic to it. If you play vanilla, you are bound to suffer brain damage just from how stupid things can get in there. However, its biggest problem is that the game has a split personality and suffers from constant inconsistency because of that. Quality comes side-by-side with a careless, slapped-together mess. There is a blatant inconsistency in styles; the game isn't sure if it wants to be realistic or cartoonishly exaggerated. Those styles don't mix and realism works much better here, I hope they focus on that. Every update traditionally breaks something — and no, I am not talking about the mods. Usually it’s unintentional, but that isn’t always the case. They nearly ruined the fighting system; daggers are barely playable now, and they did that one on purpose! No one asked for it. It was a freaking whim that scarred the game forever. You will see brilliant talent and creativity right next to obnoxious laziness. Those silly attempts to sell you reskinned crap right alongside something new and beautiful make this game a living absurdity... But then, there are mods, and this is where the game starts shining. Yes, this is another beautiful example of a game saved by its players, just like Skyrim. It's a testament to what happens when players see the raw potential of a game and pour their brilliance into exploring it. Without mods, this game would be long dead, just like Skyrim. But it isn’t dead, and here is why. The recent update to Unreal Engine 5 was a success; we’ve got the same old jank, but now it looks fantastic. They are finally fixing collisions and the navmesh, the poor quality of which has plagued this game for years. There’s still plenty to be done, but I can see the progress. Of course, the update didn’t go completely smoothly — it wouldn’t be Funcom without a screw-up — but it actually went smoother than most of us expected, and it seems to be moving in the right direction. It feels like the side of the studio that actually possesses vision and ambition has taken the wheel, which brings hope. And now, for the real explanation behind my thumbs-up. The game (mods included, obviously) allows you to build your own world, and I am having a blast doing that. I create quests. I create NPCs. I’m building entire cities, and then I attack them... I turned the game into an absurdity of my own design, and there is absolutely nothing that can replace that feeling. You are only limited by your imagination, and I have yet to see the limits of mine. It can be the ultimate chill zone, a brutal challenge zone, or both. It’s entirely up to you.
