TLDR: While the parkour remains excellent, nearly everything else feels like a step back from Dying Light 1. PROS: ➕Parkour is great ➕Story-driven choices that impact the narrative outcome CONS: ➖Enemy AI seems buggy and occasionally just “Shuts off” ➖Excessive pointless zombie spawns - literally 3 melee attacks suddenly spawns multiple fast infected ➖Sorting in inventory never saves ➖Narrative isn’t that interesting ➖Most quests are boring fetch quests ➖Obnoxious and constant audio cues that you cannot disable (constantly notifies of ANY nearby event) ➖Combat skill tree is boring My review for Dying Light (DL1) is here Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] The game world takes place in a city called Villedor in 2036, 22 years after the events of DL1. The setting is mostly similar to Harran, the city from DL1. There are two main areas, a smaller village-like starting area that is a bit more rural, and the city proper, with larger buildings and a downtown-like area. Regardless of the differences, every building interior looks like every other and no matter how sheltered or locked down a place has been for decades, there’s always somehow zombies waiting for you inside. The exploration is good, and there are tons of random things to do in the open world. Think like an Ubisoft game, and all the good, and bad, that comes with it. The narrative to me was a big let down. You play as Aiden who is a “Pilgrim”. Basically what Dying Light has branded to be some sort of long-distance parkour enthusiast deliverymen. Aiden has come to Villedor to find his sister and thus begins the search. The story is just all over the place. I really like how there are (seemingly) big decision points to make, but these don’t seem to have a big effect on the story other than some slightly different cutscenes, dialogue, and the ending cutscene. I got about 20 hours into it before I was starting to get bored of the disappointing fetch quest side missions, and the main story itself. While there are some revelations near the end, the story never hit a positive note after dragging on. Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] The general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. Coming from DL1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. The parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and I think it’s improved a bit. Jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. Adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. Though DL1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. The night elements have also changed. Now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a UV light before it runs out, else its game over. The RPG-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. I didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. Speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. The combat tree I found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. The difficulty is more on the easier side. The few times I died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. Though with the combat, the Volatiles will still mess you up. The regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy Technical (Graphics/Performance) – [5/10] I found the graphics to be this weird middle area between PS4 and PS4-era fidelity. The environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. I played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. Of note is the constant bugs. I hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but I still ran into things constantly. The most egregious is the enemy AI. The AI would occasionally literally “Turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. Also the Volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the AI is at following you 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD Audio – [4/10] The music wasn’t great. In fact, I ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. There’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “Ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens all the time . I couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. The voice acting is good. Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] There is NG+ and achievements. Perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. Still, I think there’s some good replay value here. Final Verdict – [5/10] Dying Light 2 (DL2) simply isn’t a great game. It lacks something that made DL1 so special. If I had to attribute this downfall to features specifically, it would be the narrative, and the lack of nighttime danger. DL1 didn’t really have an amazing story, mind you, but the narrative here is just terrible. As I got closer to the end, it was a struggle to push on and finish when I just didn’t care about any of the characters or the ending. While I like the touch of adding major decisions to certain parts of the story, even the outcomes just weren’t exciting enough to push the narrative to anything above mid-tier. As for the nighttime danger, it’s sad because the game is literally called Dying Light . In the first game, nighttime often shifted the game from being an action game into a horror game. The tension and change were dramatic and noticeable. I never got the same feeling here. In DL2 night time is more of a stealth or parkour chase in the open world, or rummaging through samey-looking buildings due to the dangerous infected being outside. Even if you are spotted by a Volatile and a chase sequence begins, the AI is so dumb that it simply can’t keep up with the player. As long as you keep moving, there’s really nothing to fear. Just like DL1 though, the parkour continues to impress, and I do really like the traversal elements. But damn, if I only cared about the world at all. This is a hard one to recommend. As with most 5’s, I often struggle to recommend or not. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation. I love DL1, first-person games, RPG mechanics, and zombie games, so my love for the gameplay elements kept me interested enough to finish it, but barely. I would only recommend this if you loved DL1, and even then, prepare to be disappointed. Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] Yes $60 is steep. I wouldn’t pay over $15 for this game. Short version: I'm no expert in the genre, but I'd probably put this on the Rushmore of runs-based roguelites with Hades, Rogue Legacy and Spelunky. Longer: I went into this game thinking - perhaps due to the description on the storepage or the use-defined tag that stated as such - that this was a Metroidvania. It's not, not at all. There's very, very little backtracking and, similarly, no movement-unlocks that further open the world up to you. It is no more a Metroidvania than Rogue Legacy 2 would be (which, I see now, *also* has that user-defined tag; perhaps gamers just see a simple map and think 'ah, yep, that's the Metroid there'). What Dead Cells actually does, it does very well: it's a fun runs-based roguelite experience. It's frenetic, chaotic and a very good time. I have my issues with it (mostly movement related: you get 'locked out' of a double jump after falling long enough, your character feels a bit floating, you magnetically gravitate towards ladders if you hit down on a pass-through platform), but for anyone who likes runs-based games, this will certainly scratch the itch. That said, I *don't* love runs-based roguelites, haha. I think that I'm probably done after completing it once. I am certain there's much, much more that is on offer here.

Honestly, Bannerlord feels almost exactly like Mount & Blade: Warband, just with better graphics and a more modern presentation. The core gameplay, combat, and overall gameplay loop feel remarkably similar, and after playing it, I struggle to understand what makes this worth such a high price. I expected a sequel to bring more meaningful improvements and a genuinely different experience, but instead, it feels like I’m paying a premium to play essentially the same game I played years ago. The combat doesn’t feel particularly revolutionary, and much of the gameplay feels like a repeat of Warband with a fresh coat of paint. I understand that there are improvements to graphics, battles, and certain systems, but personally, they aren’t enough to justify the price. For a game this expensive, I expected more substantial changes to the core experience. If you already own Warband, I’d have a hard time recommending Bannerlord at full price unless you’re specifically looking for better graphics and larger-scale battles. For me, the overall experience just doesn’t feel different enough to justify the cost.

Squad AI is quite neglected, making singleplayer a rote and frustrating experience. SWAT members sometimes fail to react to being shot, cannot throw grenades properly, and demonstrate all the wrong initiative. Because squadmates don't understand how to safely take and secure a room - they do not recognize even the most obvious dangers and occupy vulnerable positions while monitoring the least dangerous angles - the player is forced to use wedges as a final recourse. And when a danger evolves into an active threat, they do not respond to that either. They usually only react to what is in view (and sometimes not even that). Thus, gameplay becomes a process of using wedges on every single door, as it is the only way you can guarantee security. Micromanagement rather than team coordination. But even that is difficult to do safely. Sometimes squadmates do not follow orders, and when they do, it can lead to undesired behaviour. To place a wedge, the door must first be closed. The squadmate can close the door, but if there's a downed suspect or some evidence on the other side, they may choose to reopen the door to collect the evidence/restrain the suspect (possibly dying in the process, which is often followed by you or the rest of the team dying). So it is safest to close and wedge doors yourself, but again, you cannot trust your teammates to protect you in the process without specifically ordering them to do so, which - since you are often exposed from multiple angles - requires several orders for something that any human would have done automatically and without hesitation. In the time it takes to set up those orders, a threat may have appeared from any of the thresholds you are trying to secure. But all of this could have been prevented if the AI was aware of thresholds and could identify them as threats and treat them accordingly. A big part of the issue is that most things the AI does seems to be baked into the map. Often the squadmates will delay carrying out an order because you are standing in their magical golden path when they could just walk around you while respecting your line of fire. This is sometimes fatal, as you are usually trying to provide security for them, and moving would not only endanger but often you as well. Or you may even be trying to engage suspects and they might cross your line of fire, or force you to move (destabilizing you) because you consider their task time sensitive. It isn't clear if those paths are baked or calculated, but they are too inflexible all the same. The angles that the AI hold after clearing, however, appear to be baked. Reasonable for performance and consistency. But the algorithm used to bake them isn't aware of lines of sight; It is aware of doors. The most obvious example of this is cases with windows or counters such as the lobby of the Mindjot Datacenter. The reception desk is partitioned into a separate logical room (it has a door, so this makes sense). But the reception desk "room" has a door to the kitchen. The squadmates don't know that the kitchen effectively connects to the lobby, so they don't cover it. This frequently results in suspects coming through the kitchen into the reception area, which is not covered by any teammates, leaving a nasty surprise for the player. This is compounded by the fact that two squadmates will always be standing in the corner watching the corridor door and the double doors. Those squadmates are immediately cut off from the team should a suspect move to the reception desk. This makes an otherwise safe and obvious room for double entry quite perilous, all because the squadmates can't "see" what is obviously the second most dangerous door in the room.

An absolute masterpiece and my favorite game of all time. Period! Half-Life 2 is an absolute legendary game and easily one of the greatest video games ever made. With an incredible story, unforgettable atmosphere, revolutionary mechanics, and groundbreaking physics, this game set new standards for the entire gaming industry. The story of Gordon Freeman and his fight against the Combine is absolutely fantastic. The world-building, memorable characters, mysterious atmosphere, and incredible storytelling keep you hooked from beginning to end. The story is filled with intense moments, unexpected twists, and amazing cliffhangers that leave you wanting more. The gameplay mechanics are simply outstanding, especially considering when the game was released. The movement feels great, the gunplay is satisfying, and the physics system was nothing short of revolutionary. The Gravity Gun alone is one of the greatest weapons ever introduced in a video game, making combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving incredibly fun and creative. The level design is phenomenal, offering a perfect mix of action, exploration, puzzles, and unforgettable sequences. From the streets of City 17 to the terrifying atmosphere of Ravenholm, every location feels unique and memorable. Even after all these years, Half-Life 2 still holds up incredibly well. Its incredible physics, immersive storytelling, and brilliant gameplay are a testament to just how far ahead of its time this game truly was. Overall, an absolute masterpiece that revolutionized gaming and influenced countless games that followed. One of the greatest games ever created, and personally, my favorite video game of all time. Nothing comes close to the experience Half-Life 2 delivers. A legendary achievement by Valve and an easy 11/10!

it took me 66h to 100% the game and i definitely have some thoughts The game is visually stunning with or without ray tracing (i played without), the environments feel alive, the sound design helps bring it all together and immerse you fully into the game. The enemies are tough but you always feel like you are learning and not a single enemy felt unfair (Except Earlang, f that guy) and with enough tries you will beat them, im fairly new to the souls like genre and i could beat the game fairly easily so i dont think its too difficult, which is good. The story is quite confusing at times, or maybe its because i played the game over multiple weeks but the combat was so much fun that i honestly didnt really pay too much attention to it. There are quests and missable things in the game which are not explicitly stated anywhere and you only understand with clues from dialogue (i used a checklist since its easier especially since there is no way i can beat the game 100% in one sitting) but i see this as a positive and it incentivizes exploration. Now some of the bad Some places that look like you can walk over/trough are blocked by invisible walls (not super common but i did get stuck in a few places in Ch4). if you get close to ledges that you are able to jump off, it will automatically make you jump, meaning some parts of the game with tight bridges are super annoying because a slight misstep will make you jump off and die. Sometimes id get random visual glitches that would fix themselves in a few seconds but it would mess with vision Sound would cut out if tp to a shrine to farm enemies. Speaking of RNG drops, i got very lucky and pretty much got all RNG drops in about 20-30 mins of farming but ive seen some people having to farm for hours, this for me takes away from the game a bit as i want to explore not hit the same guy for 20mins straight. The Pagoda part of Ch3 does not have enough save points, especially with the debuffs on my first playthrough it took me about as much time to beat Pagoda as it did the rest of the chapter, some people might enjoy it but for me it was the worst part of the game. Some Achievements would not pop properly so i had to do alot of extra boss fighting in NG+ purely due to the achievement not working. I did not touch the Challenge modes, though they are there and give some special weapons, but as it was not needed for 100% and im not super into tournament style battles i left it alone. Overall a great experience that im glad i came back to finish, i started the game back in 2024 shortly after release and did not enjoy it at all, but today i can say that it is worth a play and has inspired me to look into the books that this game is based upon.

So I completed Dying Light 2 on the XBOX X when it was first released and still own it on disc. It was fun, and enjoyable considering the type of games I enjoy. Post-Apocalypse games, literature and media have always interested me. Especially zombies which is a given considering what most of us grew up watching and playing games about. Harran of the original game was exciting, trying to survive by travelling by and at night avoiding the Volatiles. Villedor of DY2 is just as expansive, taking place in an Eastern European city that walled itself off to first contain the virus only for those very same walls to save it's inhabitants when the virus affected the entire world. I quite enjoyed the Faction system; with the Peacekeepers and the Survivors, deciding who to help and assist with the Renegades as the enemy faction. Discovering outposts and deciding who would get it, with different benefits to whichever faction you side with. The combat of melee being primarily your way of fighting the infected and the Renegades and other human threats makes a return, with guns coming in later in the game. Similar games have come a long way from say Dead Island, expanding in lore but also gameplay mechanics. For fans of the original Dying Light, the sequel is as enjoyable. For those who haven't played it, think Dead Island expanded upon in many different ways. I remember paying half-price for DL2 on XBOX, and I didn't regret. This being Steam there are I would say daily events and discounts, or bundles of the Dying Light franchise so it's worth buying when one is on. Get lost in a world where humanity is in a corner, against all odds trying to scratch out a life and fighting the infected and humans who wants to rule the world. A simple concept. 8/10

When I played this game for the first time, I wasn't expecting much. I knew it wasn't an easy platformer, but it was way harder than I expected. Because of that, I dropped the game at chapter 4 in 2023 and haven't thought about it since. Three years later, I decided to look through my Steam library and found this game abandoned in the dust. I decided to try it again from the very beginning, and oh man... it's freaking amazing. I can't praise enough how fluid the movement feels, with the camera naturally tracking your character. It's also not as punishing as games like Getting Over It or Jump King, as it features checkpoints and lets you practice any room you want at your own pace. You can also save your progress anytime you want and come back to it whenever you feel like it. The story is also amazing and very relatable. Our main protagonist, Mabeline, struggles with laziness and wants to prove to herself that she can accomplish anything she desires, even something as crazy as climbing to the top of a mountain. She goes through natural character development and proves to us players that if we truly desire something, we can achieve it. If you love challenging games that make you feel devastated after countless failures, but absolutely amazing after you accomplish your goal, this is the perfect game. I will keep playing to get 100% achievement completion, as it's truly worth it.

173.7小时(仅steam记录),3个周目，极暗，10年。 第1周目，盗版测试版，海湾还没出，打了十几小时玩不明白，弃了。 第2周目，开始steam记录，冠军区域boss打了一半多，手贱开庭院，被铺天盖地无法处理的血疫和狂信者逼到绝路，死档。 第3周目，用尽各种手段，尽量不死人不解雇人，220周完成，仓库里装满了财宝，祖产和饰品，望着月光下的小镇，怅然若失。 地牢是个好游戏。 双血条管理，艰难的开局，优秀的资源管理、高昂的成本，4大地区，无数的陷阱，奇物，各具特色的boss，渲染到极致的气氛，简单又令人深思的剧情，优秀的美术，马车声、钟声、铁门声、酒吧木门声、英雄们的跃跃欲试、欢乐、警惕、呓语、恐惧、疯魔，绝境中的美德，暴击，好的点太多太多....... 地牢是个坏游戏。 高昂的养成成本，永久死亡的沉重代价，无处不在的凶恶怪物、压力、红癖、血疫、疾病、随时会翻车的可能、恶性滚雪球、不解包看攻略难以察觉的种种机制，庭院超长但大量素材复用的屎尿级地图，极慢的演出速度，以及无处不在的焦躁、绝望和紧迫感，进去4个，疯了5个不只是口头说说，而是每个初见地牢人必定会感受到的真实体验。 随着探索的深入，屏幕前的我也越来越不择手段。 为了减少因不熟悉机制造成的损失，开始看各种机制攻略。 因为搞不清淹没船员怎么打而手足无措，开始看boss分析。 因为被猩红庭院和dd3的超长本折磨而失去耐心，开始找迷宫地图。 因为嫌演出太慢打了加速mod。 最终确实通关了，但并不是完全靠自己，最原初的体验通关的，总有一种难以言说的焦躁感。 地牢与我 有人说，地牢是个资本家游戏，英雄都是打工仔，能用就用，维护成本高了就放弃。 可现实中，我们普通人不也和这些英雄一样吗，为了生存、为了理想，摸爬滚打，一想到这，我就狠不下心。 所以我尽力对待每一场战斗，关注每个英雄的红癖，压力，成长，宁肯多打几十个周目都不愿放弃任何人。 我为每一位为我战死的英雄叹息。 虽然这确实浪费了很多现实中的时间和精力，并且得不偿失。 但我觉得，他们值得。 我真心感谢在第3周目为我战死的29名英雄，存活到结尾的34名英雄，被我解雇的、以及前2周目的无名英雄们。 这或许不是最完美的体验，但已经是我目前拼劲全力最好的体验。 在游玩地牢的过程中，我不只一次有强烈的丧失感。 当满血破盾者被树干猛击暴击清空血条和随之而来的dot致死时，我因想到人生不如意十之八九，厄运随时可能不打招呼而来叹息。 当一个boss,一个地图在不看攻略困难重重，看攻略后轻松解决时，我因想到自己人生常常抹黑走路，无人指导，拼尽全力，收益颇微，一路走来，冷暖自知而折磨。 当好不容易通关时，我为那绝望的终局，以及人生终将到来的疯狂和死亡而焦虑。 我们的人生或许有光芒，但黑暗无处不在。 为了生存，我们必须戴着面具演戏，在迷失、病痛、压力、衰老、疾病中走向不可避免的死亡。 我这一生如履薄冰，你说，我能走到对岸吗？

Even ten years later, core conflicts in the game are not fixed. Diplomacy is entirely useless and the best way to do it is just to ignore it entirely. Districts and wonders taking up entire tiles breaks your ability to play tall or on islands. This seems like a minor problem, but it is particularly egregious when you consider that they made poorly planned choices such as Kupe; He is an oceanic-spawning leader that is typically found on small islands, whose ability requires leaving nature untouched. In previous games where your city only took up one tile, this was possible. But with the way that Civ 6 works, his ability works directly against itself and the mechanics of the game. Diplomacy just straight up doesn't work. The game will ignore it's own systems, and it does not track very basic concepts like "you have to survive to win the game". The AI will literally refuse to hand over diplomatic favour points in order to keep playing, and choose instead to die. The AI for units also doesn't exist. They just wander about randomly on their own, there is absolutely no central command script, and they are useless. If you ever wonder why the enemy infantry gets in the way of their own siege units from reaching your city, it's because they literally are not co-ordinated in any way. There are so many of these issues in the game, it's clear that nobody was talking to each other when they made it. On their own they sound like okay ideas, but put together they make each other actively worse.

总体是好玩的，在回合制RPG同品类作品中可能无出其右了，尽管有不少让人感到可惜的地方。非常期待拉瑞安自家IP《神界》新作能大展拳脚。 除了草草结尾的第三章以外，或许是受制于DND规则，游戏其实还有不少不合理的地方： 1.在一个有“神”、“神选”、有魔法、有龙、有地狱、有恶魔、CG里看起来能随便穿位面的世界里，玩家从开头到结局，能接触到的几乎所有东西全部都是凡人（也许有不是的，但没体现在战斗或选择里）。主角开局是个没装备的1级凡人，通关是装备还不错的12级凡人。最终BOSS（以及铺垫的小BOSS）是靠平砍砍死的，开局是平砍，结局是平砍+轰鸣剑，据说好像能灭世的东西 （至少能灭城是确定的） 居然靠着武器攻击平砍砍死了，不应该灌注什么魔法施展什么强大战技之类的吗。博得之门的英雄（以及前英雄）如此孱弱，又强又弱的感觉。 2.主角团成长的感觉很弱，成长历程没有那种要追求力量、克服万难，最终成就自我的感觉。主角的战力是哪来的呢？升级送的（也许能理解为神给的？）。你只要升级，战力自动就提升了（环位、专长、职业特性），也就是理论上来说，在这个世界观里你只要上班（做任务加经验）、旅游（探索新区域加经验）就可以升到满级，就可以自动获得主角通关时的属性。而在《神原2》里，虽然升级同样是极重要的提升点，但可没有环位、职业特性这些东西，升级能够带来的各种间接提升都是需要自己去寻找的，技能也需要去找NPC才能有，而不是原地提升。 3.全程没有一个像样的法系敌人。主要威胁都是各种砍、或者射箭。这个世界好像没人会用法术杀敌，敌人用的法术主要还是控制类的，伤害类的会用的很少，而且用的主要就有限的几种法术/戏法。整个世界没有人会用法术卷轴，开个高等隐形术就能偷一堆，这个世界没一个人会？成规模的地方势力都不能批发卷轴吗，人都要死了不能给手下多发一点。但凡小怪会用火球术、火墙术、冰风暴之类的卷轴，游戏难度估计要提高不少。 4.法师的法术表看起来技能很多，但实际有用的就几个，一些技能配不上对应的环位，一些技能存在的意义不知道是什么。伤害类法术整体而言太传统、太平凡，不像《神原2》一样，里面一些技能的效果明显就不是凡人能用的法术 尽管如此，游戏还是值得200+元的价位的，游戏内容量够多，画面还不错，剧情上也会对你的选择做出基本上正确的反馈，战斗上能够让你体会到回合制游戏居然可以这样做

My only minor gripes are that the controls can sometimes cause unit movement to get wasted when clicking at the same time that the game switches focus for you, and that the in-game wiki sometimes leaves a lot to be desired. Black Myth: Wukong was one of the biggest surprises I've played in recent years. Going in, I expected a solid action game, but what I got was a visually stunning adventure packed with memorable boss fights and incredible set pieces. The combat is easily the highlight of the game. It's fast, satisfying, and gives you plenty of abilities and transformations to experiment with. While many compare it to Souls games, I found it more accessible and focused on spectacle rather than frustration. The boss battles are some of the best I've experienced in an action RPG, and every major victory feels earned. Visually, the game is absolutely breathtaking. The environments are rich with detail, the creature designs are fantastic, and the Unreal Engine 5 visuals truly shine. Playing in 4K was a treat, with many moments that looked straight out of a CGI movie. The story, inspired by Journey to the West, is intriguing and full of mystery. While some parts can be difficult to follow if you're unfamiliar with the source material, the atmosphere, cutscenes, and world-building kept me invested from start to finish. Performance-wise, the game ran surprisingly well. I experienced only minor stutters here and there, and overall the experience was smooth and polished. Bottom line: Black Myth: Wukong proves that Chinese developers are absolutely cooking right now. The level of quality, ambition, and attention to detail on display here is incredible, especially for a studio's first AAA title. It may not reinvent the genre, but it delivers stunning visuals, excellent combat, and unforgettable boss encounters. If you're a fan of action games, this is an easy recommendation. I thoroughly enjoyed it. 🔥🐒🎮

该玩，入手绝不亏 也是近500h了该测评了，一口气玩到300h时就觉得有写必要了。 广而不深：四字包罗了无人深空更新了十年的弊端，它就像极了人类现在对宇宙的探索程度，像你就知道宇宙应该更加深邃，内容应该更加丰富，但现实却只有这些还只能如此，只能怒制作组不争，等你玩进去了玩到头了，你再回顾历程时会感些许失落，因为它本来可以做得更好。 首先该说说游戏历程：从生存挖矿建家起，逐步升空得船，再到探索星球发掘宇宙，挖掘bug彩蛋，加mod，整建模。 不得不说，现在入坑的玩家能站在先人凝聚的肩膀上几乎无所不能。有着随时能摇人救援的联机模式，也有各种便利的mod,。最棒的莫过于每当你有了新的需求，你总能在各平台收集到信息后，挖掘到这款游戏隐藏着的全新的宇宙，你会发现总有人能救你所急施与援手。像N网有着各种各样的mod与工具，一些绕不开的像，存档编辑器（替换飞船种子），任务进度器（解决bug），乐土、飞船探针程序等极大的改善了游戏体验。像oogc社区存有大量建模玩家耗费心血打磨的飞船建模，能免费下载。现如今简直就是这款游戏的黄金时代。 前100h游戏体验类似 ， 之类的挖矿造家单机游戏，等做完主线解锁符文传送门能随时抵达玩家间留传的坐标时，这款游戏的魅力才会真正开始显现。 探索未知风景，寻找类地乐土建造小窝，跟随玩家坐标拿到造型帅气或者非常乐子的飞船，或者干脆狠下心装mod整建模打造真正自己想象的护卫舰。解决自动化矿场，发掘特性bug等等。这些内容足以撑饱你玩到300+h。再之后你就该去钻研钻研游戏外的神秘力量，想方设法的在玩家间留下些深刻印象了。 再说无人深空联机也不赖，作为一款半单机半网游的游戏，玩家的素质道德普遍较高，一方面是社区活跃的头部玩家们都有着极强烈的助人为乐精神，一方面价格的门槛筛选了不少人，再或许玩家们都见识过”无人“的深空会自发的维护”有人“的美好。像深空救援，异像乞讨，团建跳舞，建筑串门等等，这样互帮互助，偶尔整活，社区非常有活力，这样的氛围就是一大享受，现这样素质的社区可不多见了。 风景与奇观：各类星球环境风景迥然不同，一时半会根本看不完。再各玩家类似温馨别墅，整活建筑，甚至空间站奇观，景点真不少，就当是纯来联机旅游，也绝对不亏。像帝江号空间站，烟花星空间站，时序加速器，小明星红色教育空间站，教堂，酒吧，宾馆，别墅等等等等，无人深空有着大量会搞建筑会整建模的玩家，定会让你大开眼界的。 还有自建护卫舰：无数太空游戏玩家梦寐以求的功能，无人深空做到了，虽然大概率得借助mod甚至blender的力量才能完成心中的效果，但是他能啊，他真能开出去让别的玩家看到，能好好的在玩家聚集地炫耀一番。 总之，折后的无人深空超值，无论什么游戏你都能在这里找着影子，这里人很棒，游戏也不错。但我想如果你不是太空发烧友，可能没那么感冒，还有这半熟的玩法机制终归是要扣分的、、、 综合评价应给到四星半，次神作，该玩，入手绝对不亏。

一直在等一位对的人陪我玩《双人成行》。如今，终于等到了 《双人成行》是合作游戏中一座不容忽视的标杆。只要了解过游戏，大概率都听过它的名字。多年前看到推荐时，我便买下了它，却一直没有开始虽然有同学和舍友问过我，我没有回答默默拒绝。内心一直想等一位合适的人，一起走进这个世界。 如今，终于等到了。虽然还是很期待能并肩坐着一起玩，但开着视频、隔着屏幕通关，也成了一段相当难忘的回忆。 因为游戏买得早，不知道什么时候可以玩，最怕的就是还没玩便被剧透。可惜，中途的 大象 和结尾的 亲亲 ，还是不小心在视频里看到了。也正是因为某些重要情结被剧透，之后我便刻意避开所有相关视频，想把剩下的惊喜留到真正游玩的那一天。好在亲自踏进这个世界时，依然有太多意想不到的设计，让我们一路惊呼、一路笑着玩下去。 游戏的玩法与关卡设计确实精彩，总能在熟悉一种机制之后，又带来新的机制和玩法。一路上既要互相配合，也少不了手忙脚乱；而那些散落各处的竞争小游戏，更让我们随时从默契搭档变成不肯认输的对手 LOL。无论是朋友还是情侣，都很适合一起体验。 等了这么多年，终于把它从收藏库里的一份期待，玩成了两个人共同的回忆。

Probably in the ball park of about -1000 hours across all platforms. I've been playing 'World' on- and off now since around 2020, and have never considered the game to be bad. No matter how long my break is I always end up revisiting it for a couple of months at a time. I have beaten every monster, (excluding Safi, and Kulve*) solo; so as far as reviews go- the average solo player can look to me to get insight on what the experience will be like. I want to leave this review to really open up a gods-honest opinion, giving a good and bad part about every instance in the game. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THE GRIND: Yes, monster hunter is grindy. You should absolutely not expect to play this game without sinking upwards of 50+ hours in farming- and gear grinding. In reality, that estimate is probably much larger depending on a variety of variables. The game has tedious mechanics at times- and can definitely impact a long time playthrough without breaks, which could lead to burnout. This grind only exponentially grows throughout the game, as the base game is generally much more manage-able than the DLC. With this being said, the grind is absolutely not as demoralizing as one might expect. As far as I was concerned, I still had tons of fun farming, and sometimes- although arduous the feeling of finally getting a rare drop or finally crafting a piece of gear more than made up for the time spent getting it. You can really dump hours upon hours into creating your own builds, and experimenting with different weapons. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ARTWORK: The monsters- and characters are some of the most memorable things in the game for me. I love the artwork and design of the creatures you fight in this game, and how they embed themselves into the environment. The immersion comes from the danger, and that some monsters are outright- terrifying to come across. The nature, and geography of the locations you traverse through are also gorgeous, and have proper- depth and design. A lot of the creatures develop their powers from the locale which they are most commonly found- which helps again to build on that immersion. The design of the armor is honestly a 50/50. Some sets have stunning looks, while others can look really funny. There is no shortage of "fashion" or designs out there, so the possibility of customizing your character is really endless when it comes to color, monster parts, or themes. In-fact, a substantial amount of my playtime was also spent getting vanity gear, which includes cosmetics to drip out my character. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- COMMUNITY: Don't reference your experience to isolationists who villainize the game by targeting people who don't use their weapon. The monster hunter experience is wonderful, and is intended to be played as you see fit. Although there are definitely do's and don'ts in multiplayer, id say probably around 90% of the player-base are genuinely helpful, kind players. I love this, as coming from previous games It felt as if the community for monster hunter was a really welcoming experience when I started out. There are some utterly jaw-dropping clips, and speed runs out there. The talent of the community and the competition between fastest-speed runs never ceased to amaze me as an average player. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- DIFFICULTY: There is some stigma out there- that confuses difficulty for annoyance. Some monsters in this game are annoying to fight, with gimmicky mechanics. That is not the same as difficult monsters. Besides the obvious endgame challenges- there really aren't too many monsters that the average player couldn't beat or would have trouble fighting. Hell, even Fatalis- which took me about a month of planning fell eventually, which was done multiple times with un-optimal builds and countless mistakes. Everything can be learned, and no one should be deterred by a monster just because it seems difficult. This game is really not too challenging, and for the most part, the average monster will at-most, just keep you on your toes rather than require you to completely focus on it. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STORY: I'm going to be honest. The story in monster hunter is really nothing to go all crazy about. The characters lack depth, and have corny- random lines. The beauty in the story doesn't really come from the acting or narrative, but rather the climax. Most end-fights or fights that are big canonical moments make up for little filler monsters. For example, I really enjoyed Valkanas's ark, as well as the Shara-Ishvalda story, regardless of how their fights were. The characters do have interactions with each other but they seem quite dull, and lifeless at times. To be quite frank, the story is also really not what we want out of the game- as we more than make up for its qualities with strong combat and mechanics. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 100% TROPHY: So that just about covers it- community, experience, and game design. The last thing I wanted to touch upon is something that I myself have been apt to. There are many, people out there who consider themselves completionists. This game, naturally- comes along with a set of 100 achievements which can be completed throughout the story and the side-quests. My honest- truth is that if your are thinking about going for the platinum trophy on monster hunter-DONT. I am not even going to get started on the implications of some of these achievements, but the only thing that anyone needs to know is that a general sum of the achievements are solely reliant on RNG. RNG numbers in-fact- that are not common in the slightest. I want to make it clear that a 100% trophy in this game will come up to 600 or more hours of playtime for the average player- especially if your playing solo. I am currently at the 500 hour mark on my character, (which i started in December of 2024), and have just-now, gotten to the "endgame" achievements AKA crown hunting. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I am personally planning on completing world in the foreseeable future, getting my platinum and getting the hell out of dodge. My experience with this game has lasted me through some of the most memorable moments in my life, and because of it this game belongs to a special area in my heart. I know that deep down, I will always admire it- but I would love to move on to 'Wilds' at some point. So for those who have played 'Wilds' - and want to check out other monster hunter experiences, try World. The UI and initial loop of the game can be confusing for brand new players but in the long run- I expect that there are more than a few who might enjoy this game as much as I have for the last six years of my life.

Why Half-Life 2 Is an Uncontested Masterpiece I have completed the entire Half life game series(The Orange Box) upwards of 35 times across several different systems that I've had in the past. In fact, I’ve unlocked every single achievement across the entire saga, searching every hidden corner to wring out every last piece of lore and mechanical genius Valve packed into it. Yet, even after decades of evolving graphics, massive open worlds, and complex mechanics, this 2004 titan remains the undisputed gold standard of narrative first-person shooters. It earns the title of a true masterpiece not through flashy gimmicks, but because every single element. Its revolutionary physics, flawless pacing, world-building, and player agency works in absolute, unbroken harmony. For me, it isn't just nostalgia talking... Half-Life 2 holds a deeply special place in my heart over the years because of how effortlessly it blends physics-driven gameplay with an unforgettable storyline. Physics, Pacing, and Pure Innovation What elevates Half-Life 2 to masterpiece status mechanically is its incredible design language. The Source engine didn't just render City 17, it made the world tangible. The iconic Gravity Gun wasn't just a clever weapon, it transformed the entire environment into a canvas for creative problem-solving. Whether you're flinging saw blades through Ravenholm, clearing Combine barricades, or solving environmental physics puzzles, the gameplay feels tactile, responsive, and infinitely satisfying. The pacing is a masterclass in variety, one moment you're navigating high-tension horror scenarios, the next you're speeding across coastal highway stretches on the Highway 17 buggy or leading an antlion swarm into battle. Immersive World-Building and Unmatched Lore Beyond the mechanics, the narrative structure proves why the game is an artistic triumph. Valve famously avoids traditional cutscenes and jarring info-dumps. Instead, you experience every single moment through the eyes of Gordon Freeman, making you an active participant in the story rather than a passive observer. The lore surrounding humanity’s subjugation under the totalitarian, interdimensional Combine is delivered with incredible subtlety and weight: The chilling, hollow announcements echoing through City 17. The dystopian surveillance and bleak, industrial architecture swallowing human history. Unforgettable companions like Alyx Vance, whose genuine emotional grounding and smart AI design set a benchmark for companion characters that few games have matched since. The overarching mystery of the Combine, the enigma of the G-Man, and the silent resilience of the human resistance build an unmatched sense of scale and intriguing environment. Final Verdict Half-Life 2 isn't just a great game, it is a timeless monument in gaming history that fundamentally changed how video games tell stories and handle world interactivity. Having earned every achievement and played through the saga dozens of times across different generations of hardware, my appreciation for its brilliant world, revolutionary mechanics, and incredible narrative only continues to grow. It is, without a doubt, gaming at its absolute peak.

Dying Light 1 feels incredible to play, both its main game and DLC. Story isn't great but it feeds the gameplay well. It's also the first time during the console generation switch (360 to xbone) where I felt the game truly took advantage of its new hardware, looking incredible and feeling dynamic in both visuals and gameplay. So, snagging DL2 on the steam sale I felt it was time to finally try things out. Not only does the game feel like a mobile game, it plays worse, too. Sure, I've only played about an hour of the game, but immediately the combat feels off. Not only do the weapons have virtually no impact, there's the introduction of these quick-kills by pressing F that are sometimes short, sometimes long, and ultimately remove me from combat. Also, admittedly, the aesthetic of the game is very strange. It feels very coorporate, whereas the first game felt focused. It opens explaining the world had a cure, preventing the spread of the disease, but then a new strain wiped out the planet (so... why tell me there was a cure?) so everything's post-apocalyptic. But, also, our characters all dress in medieval wear. It all feels very LARP-coded (as in actual Live-Action Role-Play). It's not an aesthetic I would have considered "Dying Light" coded by any means. I only knew the game had a bad launch, but learning the game has been greatly altered since it released feels strange. The prologue is skippable, but I decided to try it because it's basically the tutorial of the game, but then read it has been changed multiple times. I guess I'm not that bothered by it, but it's a weird choice that kinda speaks to many other choices I've near-immediately noticed seem... off. I imagine this game went through multiple iterations, director changes, and all-in-all feels like its held together by tape and twist-ties. Idk. I'm gonna try it out for another 50-minutes, but I don't want to cross the 2-hour mark because I'm seriously considering refunding my purchase. I'll jump into The Beast since I hear that's a better game overall. It also looks more aesthetically like the original game. Cause this feels like an absolute mess. If I return it, maybe I'll rebuy it when it's VERY cheap. But after playing through the first game a second time, then playing through The Following and really enjoying a lot of that, this immediately feels like several steps backward.

Love this game. This is my favorite tactical shooter to play single player, and has no doubt revolutionized the tactical shooter genre in many ways, but the friendly AI needs some sorely needed updates. The amount of times I'll tell my team to do something for them to bug out and not do it is crazy. The friendly AI also seems to be part time pacifists, sometimes holding their lethal gun fire on suspects when they are being shot at, and abstaining completely from shooting noncompliant armed suspects trying to evade orders when my team have non lethal weapons like my beloved beanbag shotgun. Besides this, none of your team mates can throw a grenade into a room to save their lives, consistently throwing them right on the threshold or the side of the door where the cops are. The enemy AI, Especially on hard, love to hold wicked angles on you and your team to where they are pretty much impossible to hit with a pump action beanbag shotgun (Especially when they are behind a window, metal bars or pipes. This is especially infuriating on valley of the dolls, where your team loves to go up and lick the windows so all of the suspects on the ground floor can see and then shoot them). I've learned to abuse the heck out of the alt button to hold my own wicked (and probably physically not accomplishable due to spines, bones and what not) angles on suspects. Another gripe, there's been several instances where I have dumped the entire beanbag shotgun's magazine onto armed suspects and they still refuse to surrender. I can maybe understand on maps with junkies like twisted nerve, as the subject is probably high on some illicit substance and can (At least temporarily) disregard the fact that their ribs and internals have been bean bagged to the point of being a homogenized sludge and even after being shot right in the go-nads just for good measure. Sure, whatever. But when I'm going up against professional security or any other group, it seems pretty unlikely that they get right back up and continue to shoot at me after dumping a whole mags worth of beanbags into them. Easily some of the worst times I've had in this game is when this kind of thing occurs, no matter how many times you bean bag them, grenade them or melee them, they refuse to surrender. It ruins the whole mission and sometimes the whole run, and makes me want to play this game less. Also, is it just me or do suspects seemingly never run out of ammo? They seem to switch to their sidearms, but I've never encountered one actually stop shooting because of no ammo or any weapons they've dropped with the bolt locked back. And yet another note, it seems to me like the pepper ball launchers are pretty much all but unusable in comparison to the beanbag shotgun. They really just don't seem like they're worth using. And as much as I love to blast suspects with the wide variety of lethal weapons, the non-lethal weapons really need some more diversity. Three nonlethal weapons (Not counting launchers, which are also pretty middling) is honestly pretty prohibitive and can get repetitive quick, especially since in commander mode (The only mode in which I and most people play), The only way to get your team to activate their perks are basically to get S ranks on missions back to back (Requiring no dead suspects). My final but by far smallest gripe, every time you load into the department you hear a female officer say "Christ, it's really kicking off out there", In my own head canon, It's some sort of autistic fixation of hers to say those words in the exact same intonation every time Judge walks through the front doors. Some variation in voice lines for officers at the station and on your team would go a long way. Revised to change a few words around and add in a few more gripes. Love this game, hope it continues to improve and get some needed updates to the AI.

TLDR-TLDR: Humiliation Ritual: Master Cheap Collection TLDR: The campaigns are mostly fine. Multiplayer lackluster. Entire menu system sucks majorly and is a blight compared to games from 25 years ago. The MCC is an insult to oldschool Bungie's passion, Halo 4 deserves to be KILLED in a back alley, I'm A CHUD, more news at 6 Disclaimer: I can't really comment on the multiplayer because: 1.) I never play MP enough because even in the Halo 2 days I only ever got my ass handed to me and I'm not much of a MP person anyway. Most of my time was spent in local coop and splitscreen as well as Gearbox CE Multiplayer. 2.) The few times that I actually tried to get into a MP match on MCC, it was only after sitting in a queue for half an hour and setting the matchmaking filter to the equivalent of "just please god give me ANY lobby with more than 2 people in it"... So I stopped bothering and I haven't checked since. The good: So yeah that leaves me personally with just the campaigns to enjoy. And I do enjoy them, thoroughly (except 4). I appreciate that after all these years most of the bugs introduced in the Vista port of H2 and the Gearbox port of CE are finally ironed out. I appreciate that as mainly a PC gamer, I can play all the other Halo games from the comfort of my 1000W leaf blower. I f*cking also love the stuff that the Digsite team brought out. However Ask yourself: Should one be honestly be thankful about paying money to get a half baked product that got fixed ten years later? Should it take over a decade to fix a sloppy re-release of 5 old games +1 crap game? What exactly is the achievement here... Bungie handed them all the finished work on a platter. Microshaft, and 343i/Hole Studios had one job, and twiddled with their thumbs for a decade. So a large part of why this thing has good reviews now is not because this is or was a good product... it is because it rests entirely on the work of a studio from 25 years ago. Pat yourselves on the back everyone. Bonus: "Halo" 4: And honestly I couldn't give less of a sh*t about Halo 4 and anything afterwards if that wasn't apparent yet, in my opinion there was nothing worthy of the name Halo after Reach. Anything beyond is just like a bad fanfic, fight me in the comment section. Let's get hateful: My major gripe with this "Collection" is the way that this collection is collected. I should have seen it coming when I first started it up years ago; You start off being confronted with an annoying unskippable intro video from the companies that gave you nothing but pain. Thanks. Nothing new I guess but annoying nonetheless. Then you have to log in with a Microsoft account, which failed half the time due to some dumb error I couldn't care to elaborate. It's Games for Windows LIVE all over again! ...and then you get dropped into the main menu. Holy SH*T. Flashback to some people at 343 probably, roughly 2013: - Hey! Let's have Halo 4, the definitive game of the franchise, define the look of the MCC! - Remember the epic, cinematic, monolithic 3D backdrops from the old Halo menus? Let's just... put some generic actionslop with a halo 4 skin there. How about a pile of bullets for example? When people think Halo, they think piles of brass and mortar shells like in CoD! - Let's make the most horrible buttons that feel and sound like being shot at point blank with a cattle gun. We think this of our customers anyway. - We actually need this whole beast to be impossible to navigate for anyone with any sense for a smooth UX, and the player needs to be pissed off before even getting to the Pillar of Autumn! - Sane defaults? F*ck that. Let's make it almost mandatory to have to configure all settings, to get an even halfway playable experience. - Oh yeah about that. I guess people are going to want 6 separate settings screens for each game by default! ####### Settings woes: You see... Chad Warden might look down on me for this, but I just wanted to play some Halo that day. Who could've known I had to wade through several pages of settings, just so I could get a control layout that I can handle without having to relearn everything I ever knew about vidya games, because whatever is the default is not what I remember from ANY previous Halo game. And you have to repeat this process for EVERY Halo game that you want to play. Sane defaults and / or cross game keyboard layouts. Why can't we have that? Am I just too dumb to see it in the UI? Then you have to repeat the same spiel for the graphics settings PER GAME. C'mon guys. I appreciate the granularity somewhat but wouldn't it have been better to make the settings somewhat cross-game as well, for those who just want to get going, and hide the per-game graphics settings behind some kind of advanced toggle? C'MON. 25 years ago...: Have you BEEN in the main menu in OG Halo 1, 2 or 3? Were you not blinded by its majesty? Dumbstruck? The animations were smooth and the sound design was pure s6x. The music made your spine rattle. The backdrops were stunning. The layout might've as well been done by Michael Okuda (look up LCARS). The immersion - PEAK. Those menus were simply the gateways to masterpieces. Now LOOK at MCC. Clicking anything in this godforsaken menu feels like a stab in the ear and feels outright offensive to the senses. Everything is plastered with information. It is convoluted with duplicate buttons buttons buttons, (for example 2 separate ways to get to settings menu, 2 separate start buttons on the start mission screen for no reason, the list goes on) that to this day, some of the buttons I'm afraid to even click in fear of what might await me beyond. It is SOULLESS and distracting. Also, WHY is it, that when I load into a singleplayer game, I am confronted with thousands of options that honestly should be hidden by default, when most people just want to get into a normal game? How many buttons do I need to click to get into the damn game? Why does my mouse cursor need to travel the equivalent of my dad's way to school back an forth, just to launch a damn mission? WHY do I need a MP countdown timer before launching a SINGLEPLAYER mission??? Not to mention that the loading screens actively spoil parts of the story to new players (for example the flood intro is totally ruined in H1). All these questions will never be answered. Just dust and echoes. Here is my advice: Don't get this collection if you respect yourself, your money and OG Bungie's vision. There are better ways to enjoy the Bungie saga. Grab your old XBOX 360. Wait for emulators to get better. Wait for someone to vibecode a sourceport of the other games. Hell, play Halo CE, Gearbox edition with mods, or Halo 2 Vista with Project Cartographer. Anything but this sickly behemoth of corporate nostalgia milking.

game_name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
text_clean: I am reviewing this from a strictly single player perspective, please keep that in mind. That being said, I do not recommend this game for someone seeking a good single player RTS. - The AI can outpace that player at every step of the way. The first few missions in the first starter campaign are fine, but as soon as you step out of that one the AI is suddenly that same thing 90% of RTS are that focus more on single player. - "Rush the player" constantly is such an over used tactic for weak AI. You can't sit back and enjoy getting your civilization up and running because the enemy AI just keeps attacking, attacking, attacking and soon you find yourself spending 80% of your time defending yourself, repairing damage then trying to get back to setting up a farm. I don't see how this is enjoyable from a single player perspective. - Even if you focus on defense from the start, you are still running against the clock of "how soon will the enemy send an annoying force that I have to prepare for. - I get this a "war" based game, but when a human being has to jungle 30 different things at once when the AI can do the same thing in 0.5 seconds it because a game of frustration rather than strategy or tactics. - The only tactic that works at is to focus purely on military and quickly overwhelm the enemy with a massive force. How is that "strategy" when it's just "how fast can you click". I know I'm going to be the odd man out on my review, and that's fine, but there are some of us who love the setting and the idea of bringing up your civilization AND having military conflict, but this game seems to only care about the military part and all the other stuff is just window dressing. And before someone yells at me "this game is for multiplayer, yeah I get that, but it is sold and listened as single player as well, why bother with single player campaigns then? Functionally the game runs great, looks good and is pretty bug free, gameplay wise, it's just not enjoyable.

一场断断续续 为期四个月的旅程小记 坦白来说 Persona 5 并不是我心目中那个完美的折叠平成年代年轻人都市日常的作品。多处令人大跌眼镜却又难以细细推敲的关键转折让这样一个中二少年拯救世界的热血侠盗剧情只能当得起一个mediocre；味同嚼蜡的回合制战斗更是冲淡了许多作品正线中真正闪光的部分 让我算尽心机 总想着动用一些特殊手段（感谢大神）给shadows上上强度。 但放下游戏 即使我的理性可以为这段不完美的旅途找到无数的接口 感性总还剩下一种淡淡的惆怅。我所无法释怀的 依然是这样我永远无法再实现的 能够支配自己的时间 挥洒自己的青春 在为自己中二实体化的梦想努力的同时交到知心的朋友 享受一种不存在的中产文化图景式的高中生活的幻梦 以及这样美好的黄金岁月所必然结束的不舍。 文本中逐步攀登的罪恶的本质并非“大人丑恶的欲望” 无论个人想被何等满足 最终的裁决也不过是由社会道德与法律所制定的相对公义罢了。当所有看似在作恶的独立个体都被“改心”之后 主角们才发现自己所面对的不仅仅是一个个具体的 可被审判的恶 而是所有扭曲者的共通之处：当权力用标签 身份 成功学 道德标杆去定义个体 个体就不得不接受且内化。创造扭曲的从来不只是他们自己 而是整个“愚民”集体所塑造的 病态的社会价值观。因此 主角们最终所战斗的 正是这样被他者叙事所压制的 放弃思考自我奴役的大众心态。 但在那个圣诞夜之后 权力不复存在 民众们未能掌握回叙事的夹缝之时 每个人心底独属于自己的扭曲又悄然滋生。当压迫与暴力退居高阁 每一个人获得的 都是由自洽的经验 记忆与感受所织就的 高度贴合其内心创伤与欲望的最优解映射之时 当“错误”的理由本身就被剥夺之时 当浇灭反抗之火的冷水来源于自己内心之时 还有几人能守住自己的反抗之心？ 记忆宫殿在正篇中始终以扭曲 阴暗的一面示众 仿佛它天生就是一个与“现实”对立的异物 是逃避 堕落与非理性的象征。然而 这种直觉本身或许正是一种误导。现实的存在固然不可辩驳 但“什么是现实”却从来不是一个已经被固定下来的答案。我们所经验到的现实 更像是思维为了应对某个被假定为客观存在的外部世界而不断生成的内在映射：它之所以显得稳定而可靠 并非因为它绝对真实 而是因为它足够自洽 能够支撑理解 行动与生活的展开。 在这个意义上 记忆宫殿并非凭空生长于现实之外的“虚假之物”。它与所谓的现实一样 都是由经验 记忆与情感所建构的结果 只是它更赤裸地暴露了这种建构性本身。幻象并不天然等同于欺骗 它同样可以是诚实的——在自身的框架内自洽 并清楚地承认其来源与边界；真正危险的并非“虚构”的存在 而是当某种建构被伪装为唯一的真理 当它遮蔽了自身作为映射的属性 并被用来冻结可能性 强化定义 免除修正之时。也正因如此 记忆宫殿之所以令人不安 并不是因为它“不真实” 而是因为它让人第一次直面一个事实：所谓坚实不移的现实 本就建立在同样脆弱 可变且需要被不断校正的心理结构之上。 是的 在怪盗掌持正义的世界里 一切反派都被命运写定了作为主角们绊脚石的结局 只等主角们披荆斩棘 证明自己的必然性 “挺身而出 跨越难关 获得成长就能走下去” 但现实何尝有这么简单？面对不可避免的失败与痛苦 沉溺于无处可供抓手的绝望 是长大之后的少年少女多半可能的人生。丸喜提供了这样一个可能：交出你修正自我锚点的权利 换取一个永远不需修正的终极定义。当你全身心的信以为真 并且不再质疑有其他可能时 这样的“虚构”就不再能以真假而区分；既然一切都没有了“虚假”的阻隔 那么还有什么能阻止你选择一个不再有痛苦的未来？ 是的 面对痛苦 有时逃避并没有错 但“无论现实多么让人痛苦 要是连改变它都放弃的话 一切都完了”。当所有人都把实现欲望的希冀从行动转向自我的曲解与催眠之时 认知之外的 真正构建人与人之间关系的“世界”也将不复存在。 “真理”是有限的 因此人类需要“呼吸着以戏言稀释的少量真实 人才能维持健全的心”；但“自由意志”更是有限的 当意志自愿的被谎言淹没 “自由”又何谈存在？也许丸喜可以用覆盖全人类认知的方式 将所有人最本征的愿望铸造成坚不可摧的现实 让谎言这个概念本身不复存在；但当痛苦被提前消解 失败被结构性规避 个体不再需要在不完备性中建构生存的意义；拒绝让任何一个终极定义 替代持续的 自我修正的映射过程 在不可避免的失败 误判与创伤中 仍然保留重新绘制映射的权利 人类才能证明自己不灭的人格（Persona）。认识到现实的边界 是逃离“现实”的幻梦的第一步 但如果永远都无法与现实的边界所和解 永远都徘徊在自认为的现实之外 唾弃真实 拥抱虚幻 那么“现实”的幻梦依然若即若离 永远难逃其梦魇。 丸喜所建构的现实抛给所有人一个问题： 如果剥夺你改变现实的权利换取一个永恒的伊甸园 你是否愿意永远生活在其中？ 怪盗团所作出的回答是： 吃下智慧果 带着所有人回到大地之上 夺回着那个允许人类继续犯错 修正 再建构的世界。 所以 怪盗团所贯彻的美学不仅仅是简单的对与错 正义与邪恶。诡骗师们所坚持的唯一权利 就是绝不将构建自我现实的权利假托给他人 绝不放弃重新构建自我现实的权利；在承认现实的不可知性与定义的脆弱之后 依然选择行动与承担。 如果说夜之城带给我的是一种无论何时都能简单的回望 自由的探索和回忆的故乡感；异世界中的东京就像是从人生的高速列车上短暂下车 在迷茫中寻找下一程旅途的换乘站。现实中的东京是一座庞大的城市 但在 P5 的世界中 一切现代都市的体验都被精巧的折叠在了一处又一处狭小 却被人情温暖挤得满满当当的街道与店铺中。这段 detour 似乎长的望不见边际 塞满了惊险刺激的一波三折 可当你见缝插针的去读书 锻炼 泡咖啡 侍弄花草 在大街小巷吃汉堡 打街机 看电影 泡温泉之时以及把一段段偶然进入自己人生的邂逅 在契机之下 由共同的审美或追求 变成超越“泛泛之交”的关系之时 它又显得如此短暂 只等你从那个还会在涩谷站的立交结构迷路的青涩少年刚刚毕业时 列车的报站铃声就就催促你登上下一程。 我并不是一个见识广博的人 从小到大所见过的 与故乡不同的风景屈指可数。我也经常幻想着前往远方 以求冲散一切呆板 无趣的现实的万灵药 但当真正踏上离家一万公里 横跨半个地球的旅途 当真正走在一个又一个陌生城市的街头 虽然感官中总能识别出来源与距离与时间的异域质地 但目之所及的依然是无数人所共同经历的 与我的人生似乎千篇一律的生活。我又不得不承认事实的冷酷：人类所制造的交通工具并不是通往异世界的一扇门 横跨七大洲四大洋 无论在世界上的何处 我出生前二十年的全球化 现代化的余波都已经让这屿蓝色星球上几乎任何地方的人都度过着极其相仿的生活。我丝毫不怀疑 即使我有一天能够亲身从涉谷站走出 站在 Shibuya Crossing 的站前广场 我也无法感受到游戏中 JOKER 第一天上学时迷路走出那样 迷茫中莫名的亲切感。 但正是因为如此 JRPG 所描绘的世界才更是现实存在的注脚。无论是完全虚构还是多半借鉴 它让我们不断对一座座从未踏足的地域产生难以置信的归属感。也许 我还会再有机会去重温卢布朗那小小的阁楼 带着少年的反派之心去重新挑战那被欲望沾染的世界；也许 我将成为那接下怪盗团的重托 去理智而正直的改变世界的大人；也许多年以后 我也能有有幸用充足的时间去践行那浓缩在我人生五天之中 横跨一年的东京转校生涯；用也许数年的时间去探索现实的东京。有些好故事可以细细品咂 但有些故事更适合把初见时的惊艳酝酿成醉人的芬芳。我也许终有一天会忘却这段有些 cliche 的偷心之旅 但我一定无法忘怀那段放学后每日打开地铁地图 寻找无法舍弃的缘分与沉浸的日子。 在所谓 Modernity Fallen 的时代 质疑自己是否真的有能力“改变世界”也许并不重要 但至少 我们仍然可以选择去改变自己的心。怪盗团最终所守住的 并不是某种稳固不变的真理 而是一种对现实始终保持可修正 可更新的理解方式：承认现实并非铁板一块 而是由信念 经验与关系不断重绘的映射 并在变化之中保持行动的勇气。也正是在这个意义上 至死不渝的做一名otaku不再只是逃避现实的私人癖好 而成为一种极其诚实的生活姿态：在不被宏大叙事与功利逻辑完全占据的角落里 投入时间 情感与耐心 去构建一个由兴趣 审美与真挚关系支撑的小小世界。它也许无法拯救时代 却足以让个体在失序的现实中保有自我定位的坐标。 人生本就充满不确定性 而persona所给予我的“改心” 并不是要我相信某个完美的答案 而是提醒我：只要仍愿意在变化中修正自我 在幻象与现实之间保持清醒的自觉 并珍惜那些由共同热爱所连结的人与时光 那么 Life will change 绝非一句空洞的口号。 10/27/2026

I know Dead Cells is incredibly popular, but I honestly don't understand the overwhelming praise. The combat is fast and responsive, and the pixel art looks great, but once the initial excitement wears off, the game becomes an exhausting cycle of doing the same thing over and over again. The biggest issue for me is how repetitive everything feels. Dying and starting over is obviously part of the roguelite formula, but that doesn't automatically make it enjoyable. Losing a good run and having to fight through familiar areas and enemies again becomes more frustrating than rewarding. The game expects you to enjoy repetition simply because each run is slightly different, but those differences weren't enough to keep me interested. The difficulty also feels unnecessarily punishing at times. There's a difference between a challenging game that encourages you to improve and one that makes progress feel like a chore. Unlocking new weapons and abilities should make things more exciting, but the constant grind takes away much of that satisfaction. I can appreciate the amount of work that went into the game, and I understand why some people love it. Unfortunately, I found the overall experience more tedious than fun.

Sixteen Years Later, Still Setting the Standard After more than 530 hours with Civilization V, I still consider it one of the finest 4X strategy games ever made. Its enduring appeal lies not in any single mechanic, but in how successfully its systems work together. For me, Civilization has always been about building an empire, not simply conquering one. Developing a prosperous economy, advancing technology, managing diplomacy, and preparing for occasional wars all contribute to a satisfying sense of historical progression. Civilization V strikes an exceptional balance between these competing priorities. Every decision feels connected to the civilization you are creating. It is certainly not without flaws. Diplomatic behavior can be inconsistent, the AI occasionally makes questionable military decisions, and the late game can become tedious. Yet these shortcomings rarely undermine the strength of the overall experience, particularly with the Gods & Kings and Brave New World expansions. Civilization V versus Civilization VII Civilization VII deserves credit for attempting to reinvent aspects of the series. However, its changes to empire development create a fundamentally different experience. Where Civilization V emphasizes the continuity of guiding one civilization through history, Civilization VII places greater emphasis on adaptation and reinvention between eras. Neither philosophy is inherently wrong, but I find Civilization V's approach considerably more satisfying. Sixteen years after release, Civilization V continues to receive remarkably positive recent Steam reviews. This speaks volumes about the enduring satisfaction players find in its design. Civilization V succeeds because it understands something fundamental: the greatest pleasure of a 4X strategy game is watching an empire develop through decisions that remain meaningful from the first turn to the last. Verdict: Highly Recommended. Some games age. Others endure. Civilization V has earned its place among the latter.

Watch Dogs 2 is one of those games that is painfully average if you only play singleplayer, and becomes so bad it's funny if you play any flavor of multiplayer. This game is fundamentally incompatible with multiplayer in so, so many ways, and yet all my hours recently have been spent in multiplayer. I love it.

Not my favorite game from the series but definitely not the worst one. It looks good, I like how San Francisco looks and how huge it is (it brings me GTA SA memories) and I love the inclusion of drones and car hacks. Of course it has some few missteps I wanna mention. First, I wanna talk about the story and the characters. I liked the 1st WatchDogs because of its darker tone and more grounded story, not saying that making a more light-hearted story isn't good but I don't feel like WD takes much advantage with this. DedSec's whole motivation of helping people see the corruption is obviously the whole point of the group but it just doesn't feel as impactful or important as they try to make it sound. It becomes uninteresting pretty quick and it doesn't help that Blume and Dusan don't feel like a threat at all during a big chunk of the story and Dusan's appearance as the villains was too obvious during the first minutes of the game. As I just mentioned, Dusan isn't as threatening like Lucky Quinn or Damien for example, even though Ubi tries from time to time to make him look calculated and "unpredictable", all that stuff. The DedSec group isn't fleshed out either. The only one who feels somewhat interesting is Wrench but even he gets beaten up by the writing. Horatio gets killed in one operation and never mourned, nor mentioned ever again throughout the game just because Ubi didn't know how to do with him and T-Bone gets sidelined like crazy and he looks more like a cameo character that deserved to be in a side operation instead. I swear, Clara would laugh off just to see the people who formed DedSec in the first place. Lastly I wanna talk about some other stuff that I didn't like as much about the game: The money you can make feels nerfed compared to WD1, no upgrades regarding that whatsoever. Sure you have in-game activities that give you money like ridesharing and time trials but they still give you so less. It's like GTA5 all over again. Another thing I didn't like would be the lack of "research" points. Sure, those are scattered around the map but I just finished the game and I still couldn't complete every single nod. Maybe if the upgrade costs were lowered. And speaking of upgrades, I mentioned I like introduction of drones and "rc cars" and car hacks but I also like the fact that we have almost unlimited gadgets, although in a smaller number (only electros shocks, bombs and Blackouts) but why is Blackout useless in this game? Outside of multiplayer, the coolest "ability" in the game gets zero use. Also what happened to ctOS scans after heavy cop chases and the signal jammers? Welp, at least those are getting replaced by a little broken detection system by the enemies and again, car hacks. I'm not saying WatchDogs 2 is BAD, bad (unlike Legion) but not good either. Just below the first game. And whoever wants to play this game I welcome you.

如果只用一个词的话，我想用幻象来形容我在骑砍中的这几十个小时的体验。 在骑马与砍杀中，我从一个名不见经传的小角色开始，在村庄城镇招募几个士兵，扫荡劫匪，参加竞技大赛，解救哥哥和弟弟妹妹，一步一步提升家族的威望，扩大自己的军队规模，辗转各个国家作为雇佣兵而战，打出名气后成为某个国家的封臣，时机成熟时自立为王，招募家族，攻城掠地，最终一步一步称霸整个大陆。 看起来是一个很惊险刺激的游戏对吧，确实，在我的可能前50个小时的游戏体验中，骑砍已经完全占据了我的生活，以至于吃饭时，睡觉前，都在期待着下一次的游玩。那么但是，为什么要用幻象来形容我的游戏体验呢。我认为一个游戏最好玩的时候，是你沉浸到忘记这是一款游戏的时候。但是骑砍的很多细节之处，时时刻刻都在提醒你，这只是一款游戏。例如成为国王后，你亲自招募的家族中居然有不认识自己的成员，于敌军之中解救出来第一句话居然是“陌生人……”，我不想过多的去回忆游戏体验过程中让我出戏的部分，但这些真实存在的瑕疵之处十分影响我个人的代入感。 落到具体的游戏玩法上，例如潜行、城镇帮派等，如果不是在攻略中看到，我都不知道它们的存在，并且其实际对游戏整体的影响微乎其微，基本带不来多少收益且无趣。还有一些例如经商和内政玩法，过于臃肿且自由度极低。很多强制设定既无法增强沉浸感，也不够便捷，白白浪费游玩的时间。 说了这么些缺点，不可否认的是，看着自己军队逐渐壮大的满足感，攻打下一座座城池的成就感，还有自己驰骋沙场如天神下凡碾碎敌军的刺激感，都让我无法昧着真心打出低分，所以还是给出五颗星。 在这段游戏体验的同时，从社区获取的点滴信息都反应着开发商对游戏更新维护的懈怠，最近一次1.5的大更新似乎就已经占了所有更新的大部分了。不过在玩法这么有趣的底子之上，除了期待后续更完美的版本也别无他法。

玩了这么久杀机，官方能做到最稳定的游戏内容就是“稳定不平衡”和混日子客服。 游戏平衡改来改去，总能精准做到一边坐牢另一边也不爽。 账号出了问题去找客服也挺有意思： 这个不能办，那个也没办法，最后问题还在，工单先解决了。 玩家的问题不一定能解决，但工单肯定能解决。 挺好的，玩游戏练抗压，找客服练心态，一份钱体验两种折磨。 After playing for this long, I think the two most consistent features of this game are bad balance and customer support. The balance changes somehow always manage to make one side miserable while the other side is unhappy too. And contacting support when you have an account issue is also a pretty interesting experience: “This can’t be done.” “That isn’t possible either.” The problem is still there, but somehow the ticket gets marked as solved. Your problem may not get solved, but the support ticket definitely will. Pretty impressive, honestly. You play the game to train your patience, then contact support to train it even more. Two different kinds of suffering for the price of one. 長く遊んできましたが、このゲームで一番安定しているのは「バランスの悪さ」と「サポート」かもしれません。 バランス調整は何度やっても、片方が苦しんで、もう片方も結局不満になるという絶妙な仕上がり。 アカウントに問題が起きてサポートに問い合わせるのもなかなか面白いです。 「これはできません」 「それも対応できません」 そして問題は何も解決していないのに、チケットだけは解決済みになります。 プレイヤーの問題が解決するとは限りませんが、サポートチケットだけはちゃんと解決されます。 素晴らしいですね。 ゲームで忍耐力を鍛えて、サポートでもう一度メンタルを鍛えられます。 一本のゲームで二種類の苦行を体験できます。

感谢拉瑞安，满足了我一直以来渴望进行一场中土世界冒险的小小遗憾， 游戏简直超出了我的预期，我真的后悔打折买它了，原价入手一点不过分。如果你是想干翻我心目中的所有游戏，然后理所应当的拿下top 1，那么你真的成功了。越玩到最后我真的是越不舍得通关，明明你做了那么多细节满满、内容丰富的地图，但我还是觉得地图太小太少了，你也让我理解了为什么真的有人会在一个游戏上玩上1千小时。相比于结局的功成名就，我更喜欢像只小老鼠一样漫无目的在地图里面闲逛，看看不同的风景，听听无关紧要的闲聊，偶尔发现一些开发者留下的彩蛋，然后心领神会的相视一笑。 最后结局时刻，看着身边的队友各奔前程，人去楼空，回想我们曾经伟大的冒险我简直要哭出来了，也让我想起水浒传最后的收尾诗： 天罡尽已归天界，地煞还应入地中； 千古为神皆庙食，万年青史播英雄。 （ps. 求你了，快出BG4吧，我什么都会做的，实在不行也可以学学隔壁卡婊，把BG1、2重置一遍炒冷饭我也愿意，我真的什么都会做的）

上一次打开巫师三已经是三年前了，刚开始玩就觉得我是手残玩不了，有这么多不同的剑油、煎药、药水，眼都花了。同时也百思不得其解为什么守卫一直要揍我，在去跑任务的路上等级低又一直死，于是乎就直接退坑。究竟什么任务我要被揍得这么惨，后知后觉是因为当着守卫捡东西（现在想起来都觉得很搞笑），才被集体围殴的，当时根本没反应过来，处在一个超级萌新的状态中。哦对，那时候还不会玩昆特牌，其实昆特牌是很好玩嘟！-3- 虽然重制版令我游戏崩溃+吞成就了无数次，但是还是能给一个高分。这次一口气一个月内把本体连带DLC都通关了，畅快，搜了很多相关的背景故事，有好好看介绍的百科，终于逃离了超级萌新状态，就这么因为剧情坚持玩下来了。对比以前的UI界面也变好看了一点点。没变的是杰洛特还是那么脆（打了坠落无伤MOD好多了，这个必打！推荐！）。不懂为什么给Ciri中配是很软萌的女孩子的声音，很喜欢英配的Ciri和Yennefer！中后期就切成了英配游玩。游戏里有很多角色是有带口音的，中配完全体现不出来，还是英配原汁原味。除了史凯利格海上问号都做完了，不想继续了，游泳潜水和开船好无聊啊。除去以上的毛病，游戏的支线故事、美术画面、音乐渲染，都很值得去慢慢地游玩感受！就是血与酒打完觉得葡萄园的小屋子不够大了，要有更多展示的地方放我的收集品那是最好不过~ CDPR你真狠，一个是巫师三一个是赛博朋克2077，两个游戏还互相有一点联动，真让我玩爽了。(￣∀￣)

CDPR对巫师3的重置再次做到了教业界所有忘了初心但不忘赚钱的制作组和发行商做人，你们的游戏卖的不好跟什么都没有关系，老子的游戏连盗版都不用防照样卖爆！ 本人是重制版重新入坑的，游戏已经在steam里躺了很多年，初见时由于比较稀松（真实…）的操作手感、开局可怜的背包和负重、以及初期缓慢的成长节奏劝退，后来有多次想要重新入坑，但都担心自己已经没有从前的那种耐心品味这样一个慢节奏的传统RPG 还好制作组听劝，在重制版中选择性舍弃了所有所谓的真实，但从最初就是为了延长玩家游戏时长的设计，也再次证明了一款真正的好游戏是不需要这些设计的，当制作组有信心抛弃他们时艺术才真正大成 而我想说同时波兰蠢驴也是聪明的，如果没有这样的重置和免费推送，如同我这样的玩家应该是永远也不会尝试去完成游戏，最多就是继续躺在我steam的收藏夹里，而如今的我肯定不会错过明年的旧时曲 应该感谢制作组用这次重置让如我一般如今已经没有多少耐心和时间的人能够再次被一款游戏的叙事所打动，找回了不知多少年前那种吃好糠的感觉，在如今每天都有新游，每月都有大作的时代，却已经很久没有一款游戏让我觉得值得会议，或者当我做完一个任务却只奖励给我1点经验点的时候不会觉得”我C，浪费了我这么多时间“，而是回味不止。甚至会感觉在巫师3中徜徉一小时，完成几个任务，比看一个小时的猎魔人美剧更有故事感。一个RPG做到如此程度确实可以做游戏业的教科书 再说点儿实际的，我在无攻略的情况下达成了猎魔人结局，没想到养娃的心得在游戏中起了作用，对于本作的战斗手感，很遗憾即便是重制版也没有改善太多，这里推荐安装这个“菠菜冷面・BCAQ战斗增强MOD”，可以自定义战斗手感和顿帧，装上后个人感觉战斗乐趣大大提升，只是没想到把RPG元素做到这么炉火纯青的CDPR竟然在这上面还是就差这么点儿火候 我们很难知道巫师3启发了多少作品，也有很多游戏制作声称受到了巫师的启发，但真正愿意花力气去学的至少从结果上来看寥寥无几，但正因为有这样的游戏和制作组在，才让人看到了游戏业的未来 最后，巫师3仍然不是完美的，我在过程中还是遇到了一些会导致任务无法继续或人物卡住的BUG，让我想到了这几天看到的一些外媒对影之刃零的评价，如巫师3一般缝缝补补了11年的神作尚且如此，对一个新作吹毛求疵不免目光狭隘，无非是因为我们的3A和制作公司还远非主流，我们的文化输出还不够，赶在影之刃零的前一天打完了巫师3的重置，希望以后我国的厂商和作品也能继续给这个行业带来感动和惊喜！

**Not every classic holds up in 2026.** I understand how revolutionary Half-Life 2 must have been back in 2004, but playing it for the first time today has been a letdown. The shooting got repetitive pretty quickly, and the story never really grabbed me. I kept waiting for that moment when everything would click and I'd understand why people call this one of the greatest games ever, but it just never happened. It's not like I hate old games. I've enjoyed plenty of them, but this one felt like a chore to play. I eventually dropped it because I wasn't having fun anymore. A little advice for new players: Don't go into this expecting one of the greatest FPS experiences ever just because of its legendary reputation. If you're playing it for the first time in 2026, remember that what was revolutionary back then might not feel so special today. You might love it, but keep your expectations in check. Though I can still respect its historical impact without enjoying the game myself.

艾尔登法环游戏评价 前言: 我是洛云 在过去两个月里我给这部游戏《艾尔登法环》打通关了 现在距离影之刃零发布还有七小时 我决定在这个时间段卸载法环 并在Steam上发布我的第一篇游戏评价 下面对《艾尔登法环》的描述将其简称为法环 事先声明: 我不是什么专业测评媒体也不是全职游戏博主，本评价仅为一名热爱电子游戏的普通玩家结合自己的游玩体验对本游戏的所有看法和见解，每个人评分标准不同，每个游戏评分标准也不一样，所以如有不同观点欢迎在评论区讨论指正，不可能拿休闲游戏和动作游戏比操作上限，不可能拿肉鸽游戏和剧情游戏比剧情演出，最后评价如有雷同算你抄我 用一句话来概括艾尔登法环: 一场关于未知地域和神祇的宏大史诗 优点:想去哪就去哪😡 体量巨大玩法出色 同时独特的怪诞诡谲的美术和恢宏庞大的音乐风格直接给到一个夯爆了 缺点:剧情极度碎片化 对剧情的了解基本只能靠碎片去猜 有时候不看攻略根本不知道干什么 后期数值崩坏 不玩强势武器游戏体验拉完了 同时优化一坨史 综合评分:9.5分 注:综合评分取各项评分结合游戏类型加权计算后得出 玩法设计:9分 ①游戏类型和地图设计: 法环主打游戏类型开放性世界rpg游戏，每个区域都有属于自己的特色，游戏开局在推开引导之始的大门时，就能看到游戏最终目标—那棵顶天立地的黄金树。而且不管是什么建筑或者地区，基本上只要能看到的地方都能到达，能到达的地方基本都有内容，中途没有任何的空气墙阻碍，哪里能走哪里不能走做的明明白白的，只能说fs社不愧是老牌游戏公司，多年积累的地图设计功底在史东薇尔城和dlc里的幽影城展现的淋漓尽致，所有地方四通八达，可能走过了这个路口又是一个没来过的地方。但也因为这一点，法环极强的自由度也就代表了它没有太多条条框框束缚玩家，也就造成了法环游戏引导非常非常弱，不看攻略一个人探索大概率不能体验到全部内容，包括各种npc也是有各种各样的前置条件和出现时间，你不能从npc的话里面得知任何能直接听懂的信息，因为他们只会告诉你一个云山雾绕的任务目标，就这样看着我在硕大的交界地到处乱跑，稍不注意整条剧情线就直接断掉（我的罗杰尔支线就因为菲雅支线断掉了）甚至很多完整的支线攻略都是靠解包游戏文件做出来的。而且后期各种墓地和坑道同质化严重，长途跋涉+拉开关+打boss的流程让人一眼猜出接下来会怎么样，有点无聊，只有一个罗德尔地下墓地感觉设计的很不错 ②游戏流派构筑 法环里有很多的流派，我选择的是纯力战士流，可以体验到各种各样的武器，每种武器类型也有属于自己独特的攻击模组，每把武器也有属于自己的独特战技，很多武器都很帅比如尸山血海和猎龙大刀，但反而是盾戳和狮子斩巨人槌这种朴实无华的武器用的比较多，因为游戏后期和dlc的怪感觉数值都是用脚填的，等级不点高一点要么打不动怪要么被怪秒，基本上隔三差五就要往蒙格温银行跑一趟，十分破坏游戏推进节奏 ③操作体感 我是手柄玩家，一开始非常不适应魂游的这套左右肩键攻击模组，在开荒期间总是容易按到别的键位导致错失良机，而且也不支持自己改键位，所以键位部分需要适应一下 剧情演出:8.5分 ①游戏主线剧情 游戏主线剧情基本就是讲褪色者一路砍杀直到称王的故事，但如果真的从引导之始开始一路打到黄金树的话那你就会发现:这一路上我到底干了啥？这游戏到底讲了个什么故事？但如果把所有地方都七七八八的探索的差不多了，结合途中对话，所获得物品，武器和装备描述文本，能从这里面窥探出一个极其庞大的世界观—你可以知道鼎盛的黄金王朝是怎样覆灭的，群神逐鹿的破碎战争是怎样终结的，玛丽卡女王为何要反叛黄金律法？交界地为何会战火纷飞破碎不堪？在这些探索和追寻中时间就会慢慢的消磨，最后通关才发现自己原来已经玩了这么久了（但有一点很不好，就是为了游戏性把游戏设定抛弃了，比如本体中已经受赐癫火的玩家在米德拉官邸没有任何特殊剧情和对话，还有天天吃龙心用龙飨祷告也不会变成龙） ②游戏角色刻画 我个人非常喜欢各种神话故事，不同于往常书本上记载的神话，法环描述的每个神祇我们都能与之会面，我们可以在战斗庆典中看到最强半神拉塔恩，在罗德尔王城中看到身为恶兆双子之一的蒙葛特在圣树村中看到神人之一女武神玛莲妮亚，在黄金树内部看到贯穿整部法环剧情的玛丽卡女王。这些神祇不再是羊皮纸上冰冷的一个个名字，我们可以从祂们所属势力npc口中得知祂们到底是一个怎样的神？最后不断铺垫直到遇见神祇本人并挑战祂。这一套流程下来，对于会晤过的神祇印象都极其深刻，除了本体一直在铺垫的死王子葛德文。反正我是没搞懂为什么会选择拉塔恩而不是葛德文作为dlc最终boss，明明法环本体的那么多墓地和物品文本里都详细描述了这位死王子，但故事线还是没有写完，让人百思不得其解 不光是高高在上的神祇，一些凡人npc同样能让人印象深刻，我最喜欢的npc分别是本体的柏克，瑟濂和dlc的安帕赫。柏克虽实力卑微还因为自己相貌丑陋而总是感到自卑，但对救赎他的我尽心尽力，也会因为自愧而不顾死亡强行改变自己样貌。瑟濂虽然屠戮魔法学院的学子，但会在收我为徒后说出“如果没有当上艾尔登之王，就回来找我吧”她不要求我有多伟大的成就，只想着护我周全便好。最后是在人均弱智 抑郁症 狂躁症 洗脑婆的dlc中塑造形象最好的npc安帕赫，人格魅力极其伟大的一位纯血骑士，忠诚于自己侍奉的领袖，用于向亵渎自己领袖的米凯拉挑战还差点单杀，在魅惑中坚定自己信念立场，对他人想法观念表示尊重，最后死在与米凯拉的对决当中。当然塑造形象优秀npc还不止这些，比如本体的亚历山大壶dlc的埃贡也是塑造非常丰满的 但是法环各种各样的废案同样也多的数不清，比如盖利德龙墓西方的大白龙桂奥尔，除了打死拿钱以外没任何的作用了，还有别的各个地方也是，很多东西做出来都不知道干嘛的 ③cg演出 法环的cg演出质量都很高，但是我到现在还没搞懂—法环cg资源分配是怎么分的？像dlc双月骑士和花蕾圣女这种剧情占比相当大的boss为什么没有cg甚至没有描述，入场就直接开打？反而是火山官邸和别的地方就算拉个机关都要跳一段cg出来，第一次拉火山那个桥机关的时候我还以为会出现boss，结果就真的只是出现一座桥，所以有些时候真的是不明所以 ④结局分支 如果把所有支线全部做完的话，那么最后应该是有六种结局（分别是主线，群星，癫火，金面具，菲雅，食粪者） 每个结局都有各自的特点，可以根据自己对于这个时代的感受去选择怎样对待交界地，不过选择相对应的结局之后不能看到交界地到底发生了什么变化倒是挺可惜的 ⑤本地化 为了追求沧桑的神秘感，在配音上法环只有古英语，甚至连本土的日文都没有，所以没什么好讲的了。但是法环简中翻译不是很行，最典型的就是地区“湖之利耶尼亚”，甚至在米莉森支线中最后几次和格威交谈，会发现他说出来的话文本变成了繁体 美术与画质:10分 ①整体画面 法环的画质真的一般，不过法环顶级的美术弥补了这一点，统一又高级，法环整体风格就是扑朔迷离的氛围感，搭配上量大但不细化的画质，呈现出极具震撼的画面 ②游戏内各种生物设计风格具有非常独特的“魂”味，宫崎英高特别喜欢做各种各样看上去猎奇但感觉比较合理的生物 音乐与音效:10分 ①游戏中，和不同BOSS战斗时的背景音乐都大有不同，在和强大BOSS战斗时音乐也更加激昂宏伟，个人感觉前半段拉达冈的战斗曲《The Final Battle》最为震撼，中古教会调式合唱配上管弦乐队的回响，再结合游玩过程中对拉达冈的各种印象，看着沉默不语的拉达冈挥动着玛丽卡石槌，伴随着黄金律法的轰鸣声和金色特效闪烁，仿佛这位秩序化身的神明真的站在我面前 ②至于平常探索地图音效朴实无华，但都很贴合各个地区的地图特色。然后是音效真的夯神了，不管是探索交互还是战斗，每种音效都十分抓耳，仿佛真的沉浸在交界地一样，代入感极强 游戏优化:5分 法环的游戏优化直接给到一个拉爆了，很难想象一个2022年发售的游戏还只有60帧，甚至翻滚无敌帧这种游戏重要操作都和帧率绑定死了。再说优化，每次一到索尔城那个移动灵庙就卡的飞起，还有时不时就冒出来的模型变黑，特别破坏探索沉浸感 游戏体量 价格和性价比:10分 游戏本体加dlc黄金树幽影原价是368，空间大小大概是65个g左右，但是这么点大的法环可以让我玩到187h，只能说游戏体量是相当恐怖的了，加上fs社特有的素材复用，把一个庞大复杂的交界地世界缩小到这小小的65g里，性价比直接给到一个夯爆了 个人体感 如果你喜欢自己一个人自由探险，或者是体验交界地的异域风情玩家，那么法环将非常适合你，一周目保底时长都有100h 但如果你只喜欢根据设定好的线性流程游玩，或者不喜欢受苦受难和高难度游戏，那么法环将非常不适合你，因为游戏内真的充满了制作者的满满恶意 后记 虽然法环有各种各样的缺点，优化烂，剧情打哑巴迷，但通关之后一切都云淡风轻了，法环好的地方可以让我完全原谅这个游戏的各种不足，回味过来发现法环好像确实是一部好作品 总之玩的时候宫崎英高老牧师了，通关之后宫崎英高老牧活了

Beautiful story-telling wrapped in a challenging game. I very much appreciated the themes of self-acceptance, depression, perseverance, and identity in this game. The game doesn't present these topics too on the nose, nor too vaguely. I liked the challenging and precise platforming, although I don't think I will go back to get all collectibles as I know the game will only get harder in the post-game and I think I've reached my skill ceiling. I liked the pixel art that makes for beautiful environments and very distinct levels, each with their unique gimmicks and puzzles to complete. The characters are likeable and mostly shine in their full artwork. I especially love the details in Celeste's design, when you obtain the second dash, turning you from pink to blue. The ending of the game feels very gratifying and does not punish the player with the most atrocious platforming made to torture you. The controls are smooth and snappy, best experienced with a controller. Overall a very enjoyable experience with themes I much appreciated.

Important for it's time, but also kind of overrated. A very "meh" thumbs-up. The part that Dead Cells does well is that it actually tries to incorporate slightly different playstyle mechanics into it's myriad unlockable weapons and items. And this is neat because it shows the developers actually taking a moment to think about how weapons and mechanics from other platformers might mesh with their own game. This makes the game feel much less like a clumsy 'kitchen sink' crossover and instead actually influences how you might change your playstyle per-run or run-to-run. The part that Dead Cells does badly is that the platforming gamefeel of it's native game just isn't that great. It's floaty and slippery. Damage scaling is utterly absurd in the sense that on later difficulty levels it is very very easy to go from full health to instantly-dead within just a second or two of being caught in between enemy attacks due to the nearly nonexistant contact iframes that one normally sees in a platformer of this kind. There's perhaps an argument that this is where the more 'rogue' elements of the genre are paramount, that it's intended to foster a more careful play style and the development of a higher skill level. But for what, exactly? Replaying the same biomes again and again on an even higher difficulty level with even more masochistic gameplay? There isn't really a 'living' story of any note. Background details and 'lore' areas occasionally suggest at one which the game is otherwise fundamentally uninterested in exploring further. The entire last DLC literally just gave up and said 'We're doing Castlevania now'. As one of the first notable examples of the genre, I applaud it's innovation. And the inclusion of so many different accessibility and custom run options is absolutely solid on the part of the developer. And so while I appreciate coming back and revisiting it ten years later, it's just not a game that's near and dear to my heart despite the clear passion that went into making it.

By the 100-hour mark, I have successfully reached the epilogue and completed most of the NPC questlines. I am now going for 100% achievements. This is one of the first games I have ever purchased on Steam. Supergiant did a great job with the music and voice acting, especially their portrayal of Hades and the love he has for his wife. I love the core roguelike mechanics, where each run feels unique and different boon combinations lead to completely different outcomes. Even after 100 hours, there are still many things I haven't tried, such as the other weapons. I finished the main story and epilogue using only the sword, so I am excited to explore the rest of the arsenal. The Heat system keeps the game addictive long after unlocking the main achievements, making it a game with endless replay value. My personal favorite characters are Artemis, Nyx, and Dionysus. They are always a highlight whenever I encounter them during a run. The world design across the different regions (Tartarus, Asphodel, Elysium, Greece, and the Temple of Styx) is distinct and visually striking. Seeing Greece for the first time after defeating the final boss was picturesque. The main boss fight in Elysium was a bit frustrating on initial runs, but it eventually became fun. On the other hand, the main boss of Asphodel felt a bit too easy, even on my first playthrough. While the game offers a God Mode if the learning curve feels too steep, I recommend experiencing it on the default difficulty. As for characters I did not connect with as much, Ares stands out. I usually avoid his boons and pick other options instead. I completed my first five successful runs using a keyboard and mouse, but I switched to a controller after getting one. The story progression feels smooth, making it easy to play for 2 to 3 hours in a single session. It is one of the few games where I do not even keep background yt videos or podcasts playing while I play. I have not bought the sequel yet, as I want to get 100% achievements on this one first, but I cannot wait to play Hades 2. I would easily recommend this game to any fan of Greek mythology.

I have a pure, burning hatred for Brawlhalla—and somehow, I love it more than ever. This game has a special talent for turning one match into a full emotional journey. One second, I’m landing a perfect combo and feeling unstoppable; the next, I’m flying off the stage because I missed one attack by a pixel. Every loss feels personal, every opponent suddenly looks like a professional, and every time I say, “Okay, last match,” I somehow end up playing five more. But that’s the magic of it. Brawlhalla is fast, chaotic, and ridiculously satisfying when everything clicks. Pulling off a clean read or making an impossible comeback feels amazing—and just when I’ve decided the game is the worst thing ever made, it gives me one of those moments that reminds me why I keep coming back. So yes, I hate Brawlhalla. I hate how frustrating it can be, how it makes me blame the game instead of my own decisions, and how it keeps tempting me into “one more match.” But I love the competition, the chaos, and the feeling of finally getting it right. In short: Brawlhalla is the game I love to hate—and the game I hate to stop loving. If you want to jump off a cliff but have a good time doing so then play this game.
