This review has spoilers. Let me paint you a picture: You're abducted by aliens and get probed. A little while after you escape, a voice inside your head that wasn't there prior to probing starts encouraging you to seek out other probes to shove inside yourself. Much literature is written about how bad being probed is, every medical professional you speak to agrees you should deprobe yourself pronto otherwise you'll die, and you start to suffer nightmares and have hallucinations. You now have a choice: a) listen to all of the information presented to you and attempt deprobing / do not engage with further probing b) listen to the new voice in your head and continue collecting probes to insert into yourself in exchange for neat magic powers. When you use the probes, a little visual pops up of your brain turning to goo, but don't worry about that. This is the core conundrum the game presents. Sell your body and soul for power, or abstain. Guess where it leads? Nowhere. There's no negative outcome for sacrificing your humanity outside of a single pass/fail roll that you can reattempt via save/reload. If you fail, the worst that happens is a minor cosmetic change in the last leg of the game. Your choice to take the game's negative presentation of "probing" at face value actively makes your gameplay less varied by locking yourself out of a useful skill tree, and it has little to no bearing on the trajectory of the plot or the ending you receive. This is BG3 in a nutshell: a strong opening that stumbles so hard in the final lap that it actively undermines everything that came before. The combat is initially fun, but the encounter design and AI vulnerabilities frequently reward repetitive chokepoint kiting and leans heavily on initiative, leading to interesting encounters having a handful of solutions. Companions start interesting, until you find that each one you meet past the 4th got less and less dev time. You get the point. The game is frontloaded, and the accolades it's had heaped upon it have set an extreamly high bar that it doesn't quite hit. It's a 7.5 out of 10 if you're cool with the plot kneecapping both itself and your agency in the final leg, a 6/10 if you value your cerebrum. A final story: there's an eldritch chair a companion can sit on that is supposed to remove the probe. You can make a series of choices that result in the companion getting multiple permanent debuffs. The only way to cure the debuffs is convincing the companion, who is dogmatically opposed to probing, to accept a probing. If you don't, these debuffs will cripple them until the end of the game. The length of time you allow a companion to sit in a chair has stronger ramifications than offering chunks of yourself up to a hive mind alien. That's BG3.

2026.10.29 -以撒的结合，一款十年前的老游戏，其画面称不上精美，画质马赛克，文字歪七扭八，无中文无引导，局外成长稀少，操作反人类，掺杂宗教、下三滥、家庭暴力，全成就必须游玩贪婪模式与每日挑战，游戏内容绑定dlc售卖，如此看来，以撒的结合并不能称得上是一款优秀的游戏。 -尬黑了朋友们，请允许我向你介绍我心目中的神作之一、暂位居天九门之首、最优秀的肉鸽游戏，以撒的结合。也请允许我在只达成了除每日挑战与白金大神成就外的全成就时推荐这一款旷世之作。从体量上看，以撒的结合拥有17位表角色与17位里角色，717种道具，50颗药丸，54张牌，188种饰品，337种怪物，22个结局，以及各类心、硬币、房间、石头、电池、炸弹、钥匙、泪弹、属性等等等等，其他肉鸽游戏或许难以望其项背。从设计上看，各个元素环环相扣、盘根错节，但我想，我是说不明白的。因此，我想只从两个方面简单谈谈。 -其一，我认为以撒的结合在元素设计上物尽其用。以撒的结合中基本没有完全无用的元素，众多游戏（包括一些神作佳作，或是一些我喜欢的、推荐的游戏亦是如此）都或多或少地存在或设计某些元素在某一阶段失去其作用。更何况以撒的结合还在元素的设计上登峰造极，让元素不止步于有用，而是让玩家能够利用、探索运营的上限。另一方面，以撒的结合能有17位属性各异、成长各异的角色，以及每一位角色对应一位属性截然相反、或属性相近但思路却完全不同的里角色，何其精妙，既得益于创作者的大胆创新，也得益于游戏中各元素间的交互与平衡，至少我在其他游戏中闻所未闻。 -其二，我认为以撒的结合成功的另一个核心在于其在有意地分配玩家的注意力。从以撒，新手最直觉最简单的关注道具，到抹大拉尝试扣血事件，该隐关注射程与药丸效果，az随意移动但关注众多兼容等等，再到里角色凭借特殊的机制让玩家尝试更多玩法。以撒的结合的确没有教玩家如何游玩，但却在每一个角色与元素的设计中，引导玩家逐步熟悉角色，逐步了解机制，逐步深入游戏。 -慕然回首，以撒的结合的游玩时长已然超过我在steam游玩的任意一款游戏，五百小时里不断颠覆我对注意力的分配、策略的选择、爽度的感受。乐此不疲，无以言表，越是深入，越是热爱。 -以撒的结合，成就了肉鸽，或许，也终结了肉鸽。

Warframe is a fantastic game for those who look for power fantasy and grinding, and don't mind long waits and repetitive content, which is also some of it's biggest weaknesses. As a TLDR: Good things: -Interesting and unique setting, story and worldbuilding with pretty engaging characters and story beats -Great designs and mechanics which engage the player and encourage creativity and learning to master in higher level combat. -Meaningful rewards and events from every location which encourages revisiting and working with team members to collect. -Fun alternative modes like railjack and archwing which are fully fleshed out with their own reward trees. Want to be a swashbuckling space pirate? Now you can! -Cool weapons with massive customisation for all playstyles which allows for any playstyle from mass death to sly spy -Great music (personal opinion) Weaknesses: -Extremely poor explanations of...everything. If you don't look up guides for the story, gameplay and mechanics you are screwed completely and won't have a clue what's going on. As such going into this with a friend is a must I would say. -Main game is Repetitive. It's tough to design missions for a game of this type, but you have the options of: Kill everything, kill everything in a specific spot (with dlc of several spots), kill everything on the way to an objective, or kill everything but avoid the laser grids. If you want more out of this game, you won't find it. -Long. Warframe is a game that feels like it pushes for constant expansion and improvement but locks the crafting for that improvement behind 1-4 days of waiting irl. You need to constantly be crafting in order to feel like you're not being inefficient, which might be a good thing for some but I personally have a gripe with it. So that's a quick rundown, I might expand this later but this was a quick review to get it out there, hpe it helps!

There is so much I love about Palworld. It’s a complete one-time purchase without the relentless live-service grind—no forced daily chores, time gates, or paywalls blocking features - I’m so tired of that model. You just buy it and play at your own pace. The world customization is awesome. You can tweak almost every server setting and difficulty slider across different worlds, whether you want a relaxed experience or a brutal survival challenge. Best of all, I was able to host a dedicated server for my family and friends so we can enjoy the game together. P.S. To the die-hard Pokémon fans getting salty: a complete lack of competition is the exact reason Nintendo keeps giving you less for more. When there's no rival pushing them, you end up paying full price for mediocre releases. Palworld raising the bar is a good thing. I was one of those Pokémon fans who kept wishing Nintendo would release something like this, but it never happened until Palworld came around.

Palworld has been a lot of fun, and I can honestly recommend it if it seems like something you'd enjoy! Base building and crafting are cool, the world is huge and chock-full of stuff (not to mention gorgeous to look at IMO), combat and exploration are fun, and I genuinely love a LOT of the pal designs! It's been a great time, all in all, and the best advice I can give is to not try and play it like a Pokémon game, because it's not supposed to be one - It's meant to be Ark survival. If you're worried about AI, it's understandable, but I can attest that I haven't found a lick of evidence to ANY AI use in the game or otherwise. The designs look perfectly fine and honestly quite creative to me, and there haven't really been any wonky textures aside from a few low-res cliffs here and there , which kinda just seems more of a graphics thing. And, given how mod-able the game is and the fact that I haven't crashed once, I highly doubt there's any AI in the code either (though I wish I could say the same for a number of workshop mods). And, on top of that, Pocketpair has been strictly non-AI, the only use-case being some art game made by 2 guys at the company, which soon got abandoned and led to their current "No AI" policy. Overall, I've really enjoyed the game, both before and after 1.0, so if you like base building, exploration, and cool creatures, I'd say give it a shot!

With 150 hours under my belt and the Main quest now at "New Beginnings", I think a review is due. Started playing a few months ago somewhat on and off; knowing of it's history and the comeback it's made since it's debut. Man is this a great experience. From the base building and resource collecting, to having freighters and space stations. From the Companion Battles to the Corvette building. This game has so much! Even the story while very simple in execution, was very enjoyable with it's message about finding purpose in an infinite universe. As for the main gimmick of the game being the scale of a galaxy with trillions of systems, I can enjoy it's scale and variety. Though there is one negative from this. Every system and planet is procedurally generated so they should be unique (Which they are technically). But even if they are different, they do sometimes feel the same. Mostly barren planets with the creatures simply having certain assets mixed up. Maybe if there were a few planets every 30 systems that had a decently sized city or 2 on their surface with it's own gimmicks and events. Maybe if the animals had slightly better AI and more unique ways to interact with other than getting food or for Companion battles. Even with these nitpicks, I still believe that the rest outweighs them. Also, I got this on sale when it's usually $60. It was $24 which was a steal. So it's definitely worth trying it out when they do start these sales. If you like space and Base Building games, it's a no brainer. Baldur's Gate 3 is Peak Forgive me if the formatting doesn't work; this is my first time using them. I have, so far, done two incomplete play-throughs of Balder's Gate 3 and I can confidently say this game is incredible . If you ask me, my first play-through was just a continued tutorial. Now, let me tell you; the reason I started a new play-through had two reasons. 1, I didn't love how I'd designed my avatar, but that's unimportant. 2, there is a built-in mod platform for the game. A built-in way to mod the game. Safe to say, my current play-through is very modded (mostly for cosmetics to be honest). Of course, mods aren't the most incredible things ever and Baldur's Gate 3 is more than enough on its own without mods, but the fact that I can mod Baldur's gate without having to even download a single extra program? Oh, I could kiss you, Larian Studios. However, I can assure you, dear reader, that you do not need mods to enjoy Baldur's Gate 3. Mods are not needed to enjoy this beautiful, incredible game. There is so much content. When you get this game, talk to everyone, explore every corner of the map, exhaust those dialogue options, baby. Truly, the best way to enjoy this game is the wander through every inch of Faerûn. Uncover every inch of the map, do every quest you want to, get into character—I cannot even begin to describe how much I love character customization—and be your character. Develop relationships (yes, you can romance ~8 beautiful, incredible characters, depending on your choices and game, but you don't have to), make friends, meet some of the most adorable animals in existence (you can have a dog and you can play fetch , I cannot stress how happy I was when I learned this), find lost treasures, find known treasures, scam, lie, persuade, terrorize, defend, love, live, find a cure for your unwelcome passenger, have fun . I cannot explain how fun and just the sheer amount of stuff there is. There is so much content. This game is so peak. Genuinely. I love this game so much. It's so good. I would put PC specs on this review, but I'm publishing this review from a different device than I play the game on, so it wouldn't be honest. My laptop, which I'm posting this review from, can not handle this game at all. When I tired to play it on my laptop, it crashed every time. I ask too much of this 12-year-old machine to be honest. TLDR; Baldur's Gate 3 is fucking amazing I cannot recommend it enough.

Warframe is one of those games I always find myself returning to. Thanks to regular updates, patches, and new content, there's always something new to explore. Even after reaching the endgame, you can easily take a long break and jump back in whenever you feel like it. Once you've understood the core mechanics, getting back into the game is surprisingly easy. One of the most interesting features is the variety of mission maps. Since most maps are procedurally generated, their layouts change with every run, making even familiar missions feel slightly different each time. While the core mission types can become repetitive, Digital Extremes regularly introduces new game modes and mechanics to keep things fresh. Another major highlight is the incredible variety of Warframes, weapons, and modifications. There are countless opportunities to experiment with different builds and develop your own playstyle. Once you reach the endgame, you'll eventually realize that almost any build can become viable with the right combination of mods and equipment. This freedom is a huge part of what makes Warframe so enjoyable to me. Overall, Warframe is an outstanding free-to-play game with an incredible amount of content and excellent replayability. Ratings: ⭐ Graphics: 5/5 For a game released in 2013, Warframe still looks absolutely impressive. The detailed environments, visual effects, and overall design can easily compete with many modern games, in my opinion. ⭐ Complexity: 4/5 Warframe can be quite overwhelming for newcomers. Many mechanics are barely explained, and the game doesn't provide much guidance early on. Fortunately, there are now countless guides and community resources that make learning the game much easier. ⭐ Resource Usage: 5/5 Warframe is one of the best-optimized games I've ever played. Despite its impressive visuals, resource consumption is relatively low, allowing even many lower-end systems to run the game at high graphics settings. ⭐ Endgame: 3/5 Warframe doesn't really have a traditional endgame like Destiny 2 or other RPGs. Instead, it mainly revolves around farming resources, optimizing equipment, and preparing for future updates. Experimenting with different builds remains enjoyable, but the gameplay loop can eventually become somewhat repetitive. That's why my rating is a little lower here.

A few years ago, back when I finished Borderlands 3 for the first time, my opinion of it wasn't exactly a confetti bomb. I recognized how smooth and fun the gunplay was, but I abhorred the story and characters. Now, funnily enough, coming back to it as an older adult, my opinion of it has actually improved. See, I still think the main quest has horrible pacing and that most instances of conflict only happen because the characters are mind-bogglingly stupid, but it didn't bother me that much this time around. I attribute that to a personal change more than anything. I grew out of the "constantly angry nerd" phase. I play things more relaxed. I don't check social media feeds as much. And who would've thought? Our parents were right. It's the damn phone that's the problem. Now I was able to enjoy the fantastic gameplay without stressing so much about everything else. I still hope for a genuinely great main quest in the future, but BL3 is definitely worth a shot for the gameplay alone, even if everything else bothers you.

Fantastic exploration, visuals and sound design. Whoever they got working on sound effects needs a promotion and payrise, the sound in this game is amazing (I played with headphones). The game doesn't hold your hand and you have to read and interpret what the game expects you to do next, which is something I enjoy. You could call it a discount Elden Ring. There is a story but you have to go hunting for it and piece it all together. There is very little guidance. The bad is the combat is undercooked. All weapons feel the same except for having different armor penetration values, which makes the mace/hammer hands down best for everything because it has the highest armor pen. I tried switching to various other weapons but they purely underperformed. The hitboxes are bad and you have to basically hug enemies to be able to hit them which makes the spear with its range pointless. Whoever decided you couldn't repair legendary gear needs to be fired and replaced by the sound design guy, I reckon he can do a better job balancing gear and combat in this game. Yes I'm aware they added some smithy but I'm not slogging through some dungeon to repair gear. Its like they made things arbitrarily difficult to deter you from gearing yourself. Which leads to my next point. Thralls/Companions are 4-5 times more effective at combat damage than you are because you end up gearing them with all the legendary equipment since there is no durability damage for their gear. So you end up feeling like a side character while your Thrall/Slave is this juggernaut tank with tiger tank plates for armor and hits like a howitzer. Just a poor feeling overall when I'm suppose to be the one pulling their chains. Regardless of the negatives it was an enjoyable trek exploring the exiled lands. Lots to see and explore, interesting lore to uncover. If you are interested in exploration, story and Conan lore then I would grab it when on sale. Don't expect deep combat mechanics.

While this might be the best "pokemon-style" game around, the game itself is largely a disappointment. It's a matter of too much and too little at the same time. There might be hundreds of pals, but most of them are elemental variations on pals you've already seen. There might be a huge landmass to discover, but most of it isn't worth taking the time to fully explore. There might be lots of dungeons, but they're only a handful of layouts and skins for them, so it's mostly an exercise in repetition. There's a huge tech tree to explore, but you'll find little reason to actually unlock most of it. By the time my wife and I got through with the world tree stuff, we STILL hadn't tackled many of the summoned boss fights, or the harder tower fights. It's like the progression of this game is all over the place, and at the end all I could think was, "Was my experience what the game designers intended?" because I felt like I was leaving so much of the game unfinished.

game_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
text_clean: 好玩，好玩，这个11年的老游戏是我之前国庆促销买的，一开始是看价格这么低评分又这么高买的。虽然我完全是一个老滚5小白，完全没有玩过之前b社的游戏，也不太了解陶德什么的，但是玩了147个小时后依旧意犹未尽。画质很古老，不过是11年的游戏可以理解，繁体有点难受，不过有很简单的简体汉化mod，我也只是打了这一个，毕竟我算一个比较纯粹的游戏玩家，喜欢玩纯粹一点。战斗操作手法确实很没有打击感，也很不习惯，玩这么久也没有发现身体部位暴击什么的，比如打头没有暴击的感觉，当然也有可能是因为没有伤害数字什么的，只能纯看敌人血量条来判断。负重什么的很难受，不过也很真实，不可能一开始就有无限背包，要加耐力点或者专门的装备才可以提升。至于升级只给一点属性和升级慢也确实难受，不过游戏里有很多训练老师可以帮忙升级，不过要钱，技能等级升得越高钱要得越多，不过有一点很好玩的就是，有的技能训练师可以招募为随从，然后花的钱可以拿回来，可以白嫖。个人感觉最好玩的是偷窃这个技能，非常不可思议，当我把技能点满后可以对大多数npc扒光，让我对于偷窃这个技能有非常强的交互感。然后就是开放程度，虽然感觉地图很小，骑马一个小时差不多可以横跨地图（马也是真的慢，不过爬山确实好用，玩家和马简直是岩羊来的，是坡就能爬），但是npc的生活轨迹确实存在，这是现在大部分我玩过的游戏都没有的感觉，特别是好感度这个东西，现在大部分游戏的好感度系统是显性的，就是确实可以看见的，但是老滚5的隐性的，表现在拿东西这个方面，npc并不是只会在特定地方，而是有自己的生活轨迹（这点让人又爱又恨，因为找人确实有点麻烦）。最好玩的应该是动态的任务与实力系统，简单说就是没有等级限制和必须要完成的任务说法，虽然龙裔确实是主线，但是你不推也可以玩下去，我现在玩147小时只是推到要猎杀第一条龙的地步。很多看起来非常强的boss靠磨也是可以推过去的，并不需要要很好的武器或者准备什么的，我到目前为止最难的一个任务也是3小时磨过去的，不过后面等级上去，也快了很多。还有就是在游戏里的书是真的有用，虽然有的书看了会升技能导致我之前一直认为书只是升技能的，但是在我无聊看书的时候确实发现很多东西确实可以用，比如神射手这本书，还有附魔标准（应该是这个名字吧，有点记不清了），讲的东西确实都有用，还有一些书让我很惊奇，就是猩红匕首这本书，里面的人物并不只是传说，游戏里面确确实实是有相关人物的........还有太多太多给我惊喜的地方。总的来说，老滚5游戏手感还有画质差了很多，但是其他方面方放到现在依旧是一个好游戏。

This might be the only review you need if you are New to CRPGs or turn-based games If CD Projekt Red gave us The Witcher 3, then Larian Studios gave us its CRPG equivalent with Baldur's Gate 3. And I mean that as one of the highest compliments possible. I was never into turn-based combat. In fact, I avoided the entire genre because I thought it wasn't my thing. Boy, was I wrong. The combat and mechanics can feel overwhelming at first. I actually started on the lowest difficulty because I was so invested in the role-playing that I just wanted to keep the story moving. But here's the beauty of it: the game grows with you. In Act 1, you're figuring things out. In Act 2, you're discovering mechanics you didn't even know existed. By Act 3, you're still learning new tricks. And somehow, it never stops being rewarding. But the real magic? The freedom. Imagine the freedom of a CRPG combined with the cinematic presentation of a AAA RPG. Fully voiced conversations, incredible cutscenes, memorable companions, and a developer that seemingly thought of EVERYTHING. Think of a ridiculous way to solve a quest? There's probably a way to do it. Wonder what happens if you betray someone, save someone, kill someone, or simply walk away? There's probably a dialogue, consequence, or entire story branch waiting for you. This is ROLE-PLAYING in its purest form. Your companions, decisions, relationships, and even the smallest choices can shape your journey. And by the time the credits roll, you're not thinking about uninstalling. You're thinking: "What if I chose differently?" "What if I brought another companion?" "Wait... I could've done THAT?!" The branching possibilities are practically an Elden Tree of their own, except every branch makes you want to start another 100-hour playthrough. tl;dr: great game, but with a dev team so capricious it made me miss WoW. Warframe is a really fun game, with incredible gunplay, movement, and an in-depth building system that proves addicting. In fact, I'll likely return and update this review if it improves! With that being said, Warframe, as it stands, is fundamentally held back by how its devs choose to handle multiple aspects of it. This includes things like: Adding Actual Organized Group Content for the first time in years, BUT still actively refusing to add a group finder system, forcing you to use an archaic recruit chat system. Compounding this, Icebind, while incredibly fun and one of the highlights of the game right now, is partially reliant on having teammates that know basic mechanics. The baseline difficulty of the game does not prepare the average player to know what a "mechanic" is, leading to a lot of friction when combined with the group-making system that became obsolete in the late 2000s. Many things in the game reward organized and efficient group play (See: Radshares, Arbitrations, Arena nodes), but not having a large dedicated friend group means you're going to have a really bad time actually doing any of it with how fast the recruitment chat moves. Really bad time-gating, with most forms of gearing up being locked behind weeklies (Archon Hunts, Icebind, Netracells, ETA, EDA, just to name a few). I can't blame them for this- as weeklies are the best way of getting player retention. However, the current Incarnon Genesis system is obnoxious, taking NINE WEEKS to fully cycle, getting longer with each new update to the system. Combine this with how Digital Extremes often uses Incarnons as a band-aid fix for underperforming/old weapons, and each new week makes getting the Incarnon you're chasing more and more annoying? Miss a week? Too bad, have fun waiting another several months for it to come back! In addition, there's a lot of grinds in content islands that end up taking tens of hours of time-gating and grinding for... Not much apart from the very specific thing you want for your build. Warframe really doesn't respect your time, and it knows this. Warframe as a whole has terrible QoL, especially before the "endgame." Crafting times take upwards of 3 1/2 days for a new frame, not including the grind itself. A particular gripe of mine is how cumbersome the HUD can be sometimes, with no way to tell what the tens of buff and debuffs that pop up mid-fight are apart from the very short, missable text that appears when it first triggers- and even then, you don't know what it does without looking it up afterwards. The trading system, while made palatable by a third party website, shows a troubling side of Digital Extremes that seemingly expects its playerbase to do the heavy lifting in making its incredibly archaic systems work through use of third-party websites, Discord servers, and Wikis. Worst of all and the primary reason I've left, is Digital Extremes' utterly baffling kneejerk-heavy balancing philosophy. They have an incredibly bad history of nerfing anything that's not what they want to be meta into the ground, leading to an incredibly stale buildcrafting experience that's been solved since 2019. This leads to a hostile relationship with the game's own playerbase when combined with the game's premium currency, where people who spend money on builds feel as if they've been rugpulled when they get nerfed out of nowhere. A telling example of this was quite recently, with how Icebind and its primary reward, Riven Splicing, was rolled out. A few weeks after Riven Splicing was released, one of the traits only attainable by Riven Splicing was target nerfed, with a comedically low compensation given out. This pattern of whack-a-mole style nerfs effectively deleting anything that outperforms their precious Incarnon weapons, combined with making a proper build in a manner that doesn't involve weeks of grinding often requiring real money, has slowly turned the playerbase against each other. Especially with the recent Acid Shells nerf, I've seen people turn on each other and threaten to try and get each other's playstyles nerfed to keep their own safe for a little longer. This has slowly made the community more aggressive and gatekeeping over the past few years, sometimes even harassing content creators who make videos on their builds. While harassment is obviously never justified, can you really blame players for becoming more guarded about their builds? After all, the build you spent real money on can't be nerfed if you spend more money to hide your weapon names and further conceal its true identity behind a skin, right? While I don't particularly dislike Warframe nor its developers, I can't ignore that the past year has been incredibly disappointing to play- and the game still feels like it has a complete lack of direction after over a decade, with nothing but underwhelming content island updates to show for it. I still have hope, as Icebind could be a great stepping stone to a future of actual endgame content! Unfortunately, I can't give a positive review for incomplete work that's been stringing me along for years. If you're planning on playing this, give it a bit, because it's not worth it in its current state.

I am suprised that this game is still going 7 years after release. Like, I haven't met anyone mention this game just casually and yet this game is the 25th most played game on Steam! I played Apex Legends AGES ago, back when they still had gold armor and helmets. So when this game started appearing on my Instagram showing clips of people clutching the most unclutable fights, pulling some random bullshit movement tech that just breaks everyones ankles, or rizzing up japanese baddies? I knew I had to redownload and give this game a proper go! It was quite suprising for me when I got into my first game back as a lot of things had been added or changed/reworked so I did have to spend some time learning new mechanics, but they were explained pretty well and or pretty simple to use. I remember struggling on the mantle boost but after a few games I had it down to a T and felt pretty good whenever I was able to hit it. So was I able to hit some crazy clips? YES SIR!! I've had a few clutch moments and let me tell you the dopamine high was immaculate, I swear my brain shortcircuited at least once during my time playing this game due to how crazy these fights get. I didn't really get much movement tech down but what I was able to achieve was pretty fun, and I wasn't able to rizz up any japanese baddies, so no tsundere girlfriend for me. But that doesn't matter that much. I think Apex Legends does a pretty good job at achivements, as a majority of them insentivise you to give each Legend a proper go, and the rest are just unlocked naturally through playing the game. Which was great, as I didn't feel like I was doing a chore and instead was enjoying the game. The only achievement I had to go out of my way for was Decked Out which is a lot harder to get due to gold armour and helment not existing anymore, but after that? It was just smooth sailing. I felt like I gave every Legend a good chance and got to try a variety of diffrent weapons to see what I liked/didn't like. Speaking of weapons, the gunplay in this game is so satisfying. Each weapon sounds so crisp and you can feel the feedback of each bullet hitting your target. The sound effects are also really good too and you can easily tell what is happening (sometimes) during a fight. My personal favourite weapons are the R-301 Carbine, Volt, Prowler, EVA-8 Auto, Peacekeeper and Triple Take. Each of these weapons both sound good and feel good to hit someone with. Apex Legends was definitely a suprisingly fun experience for me, from wiping out squads solo to winning games, no matter what happens you will definitely have a good time. The acheivements although quite boring in nature, were pretty much perfect and to me, felt like an obligation to try out each Legend at least once. I even got a heirloom too! Which was the last thing I was expecting to get while playing this game LMAO. So I do think that I was able to experience everything that this game has to offer and I wouldn't mind playing this game again sometime. On a small note, I won the last game that I played as I hit level 50 which feels like the perfect end to my journey for now. Great game, great gunplay, great movement, no tsundere girlfriend. 8/10

Black Myth: Wukong is a compelling soulslike/action game, however, I personally had a few issues with the game. The story is set after the journey to the west, but I found it confusing to follow for the most part. Level design peaked for me in the second location and steadily declined thereafter. Levels follow a very linear pattern but don't feel particularly rewarding for exploring the few side paths as most of the time you will find upgrade materials that you end up having an abundance of by the end of the game anyway. The bosses felt like a quantity over quality situation. The major bosses are very well designed and were frankly really cool, but the other 80% of bosses felt like fodder and didn't really do much for me. There is also a major difficulty difference between every single boss except for the final boss and the secret boss , which feels inconsistent. Overall I give the game a 6.5/10, I do recommend it as the experience is quite good, but I wouldn't be urging anyone to pick it up as a must play.

I first came to know half life back in 2024 when one of my friends mentioned it because we were playing Gmod and he spawned the buggy from later chapters of the game (yes ik i was playing gmod and didnt even know what half life was lol) This then caused me to look at the steam page for half life 2, think its cool, and wishlist it, never to be seen again (until it was). At the time I didn't have a good relationship with my friends, I was always trying to fit in and do what I thought made me look the "coolest" in their eyes. And so, in an effort to relate to them, I bought the game, played it for about 30 min, loved it, and went to go tell my friends, you wanna know what they said? "ok" and "cool" that was it. From that moment on I realized that nobody actually cares what I do, they pretend to dislike you for not doing something, and then when you do that thing they care even less. So you wanna know what I did? i played half life 2, i beat half life 2, then i played half life 1, then i played half life 2 in vr, then episode 1, then episode 1 in vr, and then episode 2 in vr, and then i spent hours and hours watching half life args, mod vids, funny clips, short films, theories, becoming so obsessed with the game i would fall asleep every night listening to city 17 ambience. I'm even in the process of building my own fully functioning bullet resistant HEV suit, and all that I can say is, half life (as a series) is the greatest piece of media to ever grace this amazing planet. Half life taught me how to keep going when it's hard, how to do hard things simply because others might benefit, and most importantly, how to love myself when no one else does. After playing half life 2 I became openly a furry, and openly Bi, and i didnt care, i didnt care who thought what anymore, sure i lost some friends, but if i lost them because i became my true self, then were they ever my friends in the first place? If you take anything from this review, (other than of course playing half life lol) it's that the only person that has an opinion that actually matters is you, pay no attention to all the people that think you can't do it, be like Gordon, and do it anyway. Thank you, Half Life and VALVe.

Halo 3 is still brilliant, Reach hits differently, and the original trilogy deserves every bit of its reputation. Even the games I like less have something worth experiencing. It's not all perfect. Some levels haven't aged particularly well, Halo 4 is a bit of a divisive one, and those bloody Jackal snipers in Halo 2 can still go fuck themselves. But I love having all these campaigns together on PC, without needing to dig out an old console. Funny how games from twenty years ago can remind you what you've been missing in modern shooters. Recommended. Finish the fight. Then start another campaign.

Didn't play for two years, came back for the latest operation, and it's still just a genuinely good, fun game. I first picked up Warframe when I started high school over 10 years ago (yikes) and it's really only gotten better since, especially now that the devs who love the game and it's players are in charge. There is so much to enjoy, including some truly rich story telling (The Sacrifice)! I have never paid a penny for anything in Warframe, even after 4,000 hours, but at this point I just feel bad about it! No pay to win, just cosmetics & time; you will have to wait for things to craft, and grind for the materials to make them if you don't want to pay, or you can trade items you get with other players for premium currency. To any new players: just take it one step at a time. The sheer amount of content can be extremely overwhelming, especially for me when I come back from a long break, but if you take it one piece at a time, you'll be able to shoot & slice through it all in style! One last thing I love about Warframe is that almost everything is viable! Naturally there is a meta, but you can make so many things work without even doing anything crazy. I don't know why so many other PvE games obsess over game balance the way they do, but it makes me appreciate a game like Warframe so much more.

This game, is just, unabashedly, one of the best 'cozy farming games' out there. Like, straight up. There's a reason that every new cozy game is trying to copy this one. Firstly, ConcernedApe made this game entirely on their own. That shit is so goated- Sorry, secondly, this game has so much you get to do. If you don't like one aspect, try another. There's so many ways to make money and find enjoyment out of this. If you don't like mining, just don't mine. If you hate fishing with a burning passion, that's real! Go back to the farm. There are animals. You have pets and cattle and you can pet the animals.......... There's complexities like the seasons with different main crops and there's different sell prices and who doesn't love automation and such??? I'm just saying, if you loved the slime market from the slime rancher series you will LOVE selling stuff in this game. It is so fun getting into the numbers and how to maximize profits. Not to mention, if you DON'T like something, this game has some of the easiest modding mechanics I've seen for a game besides, like, rain world or something. This game is only beaten out by 'subscribe to item on steam workshop'. THAT'S how easy!! If you hate fishing with a burning passion! You can make fishing easier! In many ways!!!!!!! There are MULTIPLE WAYS TO MAKE FISHING REDUNDANT! HOW COOL IS THAT- Okay, I might REALLY like this game. But like......... You'll see why......................... Any gripe you have with this game, can probably be solved by the modding community. They are some of the craziest of the modding communities I have seen for games. Held off on posting a comment for a long time, but I cannot anymore. It's been 4 YEARS people, and this still feels like early access to me. As a warband veteran going to as far back as original MnB release, I have to say - don't buy it yet. If ever. I don't understand where these positive comments come from, but I believe people are just looking at it through rose-tinted glasses. This game as vanilla is boring and repetetive sometimes, but thats not the main problem with it. It relies on modding community to add to its value, but with every new release most mods get broken, and I understand why frustrated modders of some quintessential mods have just quit out of frustration. NOW, 4 years after slapping the 1.0 label on an unfinished product, breaking some of the best minor and overhaul mods along the way, you are asking me to again PAY YOU for something that anybody who has played VC has been asking for forever - ships! FFS even mods did that and in a good way way before War Sails (see Shokuho). Without mods, the game is unfinished, with mods it's unstable. But the last straw is the fact that even in pure vanilla form the game STILL crashes from time to time, and not on worst hardware (I5 12400F + RTX 5050 8GB + 16 GB DDR5 is NOT an ancient setup). MAYBE I will come back to this and change the review if I see some improvements AFTER the development cycle is over, but seriously, charging people for ships and one faction like for full game is too much. I'll stick to warband.

game_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
text_clean: 适合老人用于怀旧和回忆青春，不适合新人游玩。基于其在游戏史上的崇高地位，在那个年代对比其他游戏无疑是开创性的，但用现在的游戏眼光看狗屎的地方太多。用现在的游戏标准来衡量它无疑是苛刻的，可毕竟我玩的老游戏也不算少了，我用同时代的游戏标准来简单说明一下它的缺点——毕竟这些缺点横跨至今，且用现在的眼光来看更加的恶劣。 1、狗屎的UI设计和UI逻辑：内容如此浩大的游戏UI做的跟屎一样，这点从老滚5开始到后面的辐射系列都没有改观。超级小陶希望你用超级大脑来记住你在游戏里面干过什么没干过什么，而不是简单的添加一个未查看的红点表明。装备和武器栏的堆叠比陶德全家的乱葬岗还要混乱，我见过按最近获得时间排序，也见过按装备价值排序，实在不行你按装备类型排序，哪怕是按首字母排序也好啊。你有这么多种选择方式，我CNMD老滚选择了乱序。我永远搞不清我的装备到底在哪里，法杖里面混合着近战又混着几张弓，更别提你这sm游戏压根没设计装备栏，你脱换装备还要去背包里面一个个找。那个偏爱设置简直脑瘫，你手柄配置十字键做一个上是近战，下是远程，左是魔法，右是药水很难吗？nmlg的全勾巴堆在一起，搞这么长一列，你不觉得反人类吗？那我问你，你空的另外按键是干嘛的？留着给你妈坟头种花吗？还有那个送信的，你妈逼的不能做个当场阅读吗？给你直接塞进背包，也不跟你说道具名字，然后让你在背包你捡的一堆垃圾书里面按照乱序来找到那封未读的信，我真是cnm了。 2、sm游戏流程：首先你勾巴主线支线能不能分两个栏呢，别有的在其他，有的又在任务总览里面？而且你勾巴接的支线能不能有点合理度？显摆自己有大地图：”哇撒我们的游戏太自由了，你开局想去哪里就去哪里“。那你能不能别他妈搞成我在地图左下角接个任务，告诉我任务点在地图右上角这种事？你自己在白漫接接支线看看，你看看你这些 sm任务都在地图的哪些地方？你一方面又有地区等级和难度的设置，一方面又搞这种满天星式的支线，是不是有点过于逆天了？你们自己做完游戏自己不玩的？你们的游戏规划做到随进度发放任务对你们来说很难吗？ 3、cjb更新：你不会真觉得你游戏口碑销量双丰收，全是自己做的好吧？你B社能有现在的光景，那么多MOD作者给你们贡献了多少心血？所以我的意思，如果你们不是完全傻逼的话应该也知道mod对你们游戏的重要性。那既然如此，wcnmd你们这帮傻逼他妈的2026年还在这勾巴更新什么东西呢？你们这帮司马玩意真能更新出个三七二十一我也就不说话了，cnmd的隔三岔五搞个小补丁把mod全整失效，然后我登游戏一看：你BUG也没修啊？那我问你，你们这帮司马玩意到底在这里更新什么东西？不恶心人你们是难受是吗？ 除了这三点是这款超越时代的游戏上的超越时代的问题，你在真正游玩过程中的小问题还有很多——像是什么疾跑的时候不能跳（我不知道为什么这种地方不去做）；偷窃和犯罪系统过于逆天（你永远不知道为什么没人看见也算犯罪以及罪行不被逮住永远不清零这种逆天设定）；不明所以的随从系统（你甚至不能像古早RPG一样随意更换他们的装备外观，以及小丑AI）等等等等。所以我还是那句话，老滚五适合当年那批人用于缅怀自己的青春，怀念曾经的青葱岁月，不适合现在以及以后的新人游玩。

Cheaters everywhere: Ranked is completely unplayable. Every other match features cronus/strikeepad users on console, wallhacks, or aimbotters on PC. Solo queuing is pure misery—you're constantly thrown into lobbies against pre-made three-stacks sweating like it’s a tournament finals. Aggressive monetization: Instead of fixing core performance bugs, server desync, and audio glitches that have existed for years, the priority is clearly pumping out absurdly overpriced microtransactions, heirlooms, and gacha-style packs. Meta staleness: Balance patches take way too long to address broken Legends or weapons, while fun mechanics constantly get gutted in the name of "balance." The shooting and movement mechanics are fantastic, but everything built around them is designed to frustrate you into spending money or grinding endlessly. Save your time and sanity—play something else.

It's a game where five strangers are expected to work together like a perfectly coordinated team, where one tiny mistake can destroy a 60-minute match, and where the difference between an absolute genius and a complete fool is sometimes just one decision. Every hero has a story. Every item has a purpose. Every match has its own chaos. You can experience the most incredible comeback of your life, followed immediately by a defeat so ridiculous that you start questioning your existence. There are beautiful moments hidden between all the madness. A perfectly executed team fight, a game-winning Black Hole, an unexpected Rampage, or that one teammate who actually knows what they're doing. And then there is the other side of Dota 2... The toxicity, the endless arguments, the questionable decisions, the matchmaking, and the occasional feeling that the entire universe is personally against you. Yet, somehow, you keep coming back. Maybe it's the complexity. Maybe it's the competition. Maybe it's the satisfaction of finally pulling off something you've been practicing for weeks. Or maybe we've all just lost our minds. Dota 2 isn't a game you simply finish. It's a journey with no final destination, where even after thousands of hours, there is still something new waiting to surprise you. You don't always win. You don't always improve. Sometimes you don't even enjoy playing. But when everything comes together, there is nothing quite like it. **A beautiful disaster. An endless obsession. A game unlike any other.** Would recommend. 10/10.

Had the review thumbnail appear in my profile for absolutely ages now and always put it off because I don't really know what to say to adequately describe truly how good this masterpiece is. I've not played it in a few weeks now so I have the benefit of not wanting to play it again (temporarily), because I'd normally just click the play button. Ironically, by not actually playing the game for a few weeks it has made me appreciate even more how spectacular this game really iss. To all people that have never played any Mount and Blade game before: It's really quite tricky to describe the sort of game this is because it really is it's own genre in a way (or should be). I'll try my best, so here it goes - It is a fully sandbox fantasy medieval RPG (and I mean FULLY - the campaign mode is basically the same as the sandbox mode but it essentially just gives you tutorials and starting family members, which are really useful to have in your first play through). If you like big budget story driven top graphic RPG's, this definitely is not for you. It is none of those things. It has literally no story line - because YOU make the story. It isn't big budget - it's taleworlds. It's got fantastic battle graphics despite it's low budget, but it's not on the scale of all the big boys. What really makes this game is the literally infinite possibilities. You can literally do anything. Everybody starts off with a set of clothes and a horse. (If you do campaign mode you also start off with a brother and sisters, which help massively building your clan). The rest is up to you. If you want to become a bandit - and build a group of bandits that raid and pillage towns/villages - you can. If you want to be a trader, mind your own business, not hurt anybody, and just trade goods / buy and run your own workshops - you can. If you want to become a leader of your own band of warriors and get factions to pay you as a mercenary to fight for them - you can. If you want to be a great fighter and just wander from town to town fighting in arenas to gain renown - you can. If you want to prove yourself in battle and join a faction as a vassal, to fight for your king/liege and prove your worth and get rich - you can. If you'd rather create your own faction and gain your own lands , and eventually rule the whole world - you can. It has absolutely everything. If you'd rather not war or trade, but want to spend your time in the smithy, breaking down raw materials and/or crafting weapons for a profit or for favour with NPC's - you can! In any of these potential avenues, you can marry and have children - or not. It's completely up to you. The game environment is different every time you play it. The world economy runs as its own unique economy each playthrough. What might work one playthrough, might not necessarily work in another..Or it might?. Having said everything I have said, the game DOES revolve mostly around fighting. You WILL need to be somewhat competent as a fighter (although I know of people who have done completely pacifist saves without fighting at all as traders - but it is difficult). With this in mind, the battle/combat system is basically like playing a Total War game (any of them), except you are issuing instructions to your troops whilst being physically present as a character on the battlefield. Want to focus more on the strategy, rather than fight? You can. Want to dart about on your horse (or dismount and go on foot?) with a massive axe or crossbow ((or normal bow, 2h sword, or 1h + shield, or mace (1h or 2h), or polearm or bare knuckles)), smashing people in battle and leave the strategy to your sergeants? You can. Want to do a bit of both? You can. Then comes the absolute best bit of the battles which i didn't even mention yet - sieges. Build trebuchets, onagers, balistas, siege towers, battering rams. Operate them yourself in the siege. Climb up the ladders yourself. Command which units go up ladders, which go in towers, which go where. On the battlefield like total war, except you're actually fighting it like in an RPG. Defending against a siege? You can do the same. You can even pick up the siege ammunition without a siege weapon and throw them through the castle/settlement walls at the enemy! You can auto resolve all battles as well like in TW, if you don't want to fight a particular battle or siege. There's honestly 100 other things I can't cram in to this right now, but the main thing is there are some absolutely unbelievable mods that have been designed by the community that expand and improve QoL, but also mods that change the game entirely. All for free. if you've ever played any old M+B games before: This is an enormous upgrade by magnitudes of digits with 0's after them. Honestly one of the best games I've personally ever played.

★ ★ ★ ★ ☆ → 4.5 out of 5 stars One of those games that really shows how much better gaming can be when you have the right person playing with you. Its a duo game through & through and honestly, your experience depends quite a bit on who youre playing with. The visuals are fantastic, every chapter has its own identity and the dialogue is genuinely well written. Took us roughly 15 hours to finish and theres a surprising amount of variety throughout. I also really liked how the story approaches divorce and how much it can affect a child. Rose's perspective adds a lot more weight to the adventure than you might initially expect. And of course, Dr. Hakim is an absolute highlight, haha The gameplay itself isn't particularly difficult. It's more about getting into a flow, working together and enjoying the ride rather than sitting there trying to solve overly complicated puzzles. My only real complaint was the occasional scripting bug. Since certain sections rely on scripted sequences to progress, we sometimes had to replay parts of a level because an event simply didn't trigger, even though we had completed everything correctly. Nothing game breaking but definitely frustrating when it happens. Overall, a fantastic co op experience. Definitely one I'd recommend playing with someone you enjoy spending time with! As Dr. Hakim would say: "We are better together!"

I put off playing Baldur's Gate 3 for years because I didn't believe it could possibly live up to the hype. All I'd seen from it were clips of dialogue or exploits. I didn't expect it at all to be the most unique RPG I've ever played for one reason that stands out above all others: the sheer flexibility. Many single-player RPGs either don't allow you to bend the rules or the narrative, while others let you bend them so far that they break. Baldur's Gate 3 lets you bend every quest to the point where you expect it to break, but it never does. I cannot emphasise enough just how much the game accounts for every action you could possibly choose to take in every situation, so I'm not going to try. An aspect I hadn't seen much (if any) of was the combat, so I had no idea what to expect. I'm coming at this as someone who has zero experience with D&D mechanics. I very wrongly assumed that the inherent randomness of "dice rolls" determining every move would make the game feel random and unfun, but that's almost precisely what makes it so engaging. Your character builds all influence the bonuses your dice rolls get, so you actually have a lot of control. There are moments where you feel like the rolls are BS, but they're so rare, and they can make fights feel much more intense. Also, the fights can be LONG. I'm talking 10 minutes for basic encounters and upwards of 20 minutes for big ones. Another expectation I had that was completely wrong was that it's an open world. The game is broken up into three "Acts", which can be anywhere from 30–60 hours each in a single run. Each act takes place on a fairly big map, but it's by no means an open world. This isn't a bad thing, and I really enjoyed exploring each area of every map to find encounters ranging from small scuffles to treasure hauls. They're very distinctly different from each other, too, so I never felt as though it was a repetitive cycle. One thing I was slightly let down by was the fact that some builds just aren't viable long-term, so you can easily end up with characters who are frustratingly weak and others who are borderline broken, without intending any of it. Each class has multiple subclasses, and it's very intimidating at first to choose one based on its initial description, so you end up choosing something that sounds cool only to find out it sucks either in the short or long term. You can respec at any point, so it's not the end of the world, but it is a shame that I felt the classes aren't as balanced as they could be. Without getting into spoilers, the main narrative focus of the journey you go on is more about getting to know each of the characters you end up having in your gang. The overarching goal is more of a motivator to keep the journey going rather than the main hook that will keep you invested. If I had to sum up my thoughts on each of the characters, they would be: Astarion: Funny most of the time, but I found him to be too on the nose and in-your-face in terms of being a borderline villain. He has the funniest dialogue scene in the game in Act 1. I won't say what, but if you know, you know. I do like the conclusion to his quest a lot, but he feels very disconnected for most of the game. Gale: Nerd emoji wizard. He feels more connected to the main story, and I did like having him in my party. No strong feelings towards him. Lae'zel: Feels the most connected to the main narrative for most of the game, and is also one of the top contenders for my personal favourite. Her evolution as a character is definitely the most dramatic. I found her ignorance of the world and fight-or-die mentality very charming. Karlach: Initially, I couldn't stand her. She talks like a modern-day, quippy millennial, and I hated it. She does have some of the most dramatic dialogue and a seemingly high-stakes story, but she doesn't have much to do for most of the game in terms of a personal story. I like her more dramatic moments, though, and she did end up growing on me. Shadowheart: The other contender for my favourite of the gang. She is also very much tied to the main story in every act in the most significant way. Weirdly, she seems like the most normal and pragmatic of the bunch and is very easy to get along with. Wyll: I found Wyll to be the polar opposite of Astarion, in that he's a goody-two-shoes, sometimes to an obnoxious degree. I liked his character, though, and the dilemma he finds himself in is a very cool twist for a hero-type character. There are others who can join that I didn't mention, but they're not as deep as the main six and to be honest I didn't use them in my party so I can't comment. Each of the characters in your party reacts to your decisions in dialogue, and you actually learn a great deal about each one of them purely from the "X Approves/Disapproves" pop-up when you're in dialogue. I honestly think Baldur's Gate 3 is a little overhyped, but that doesn't mean I don't love it. If you are a diehard RPG fan who wants the truest RPG experience possible, this is your game. Everything it tries to do, it succeeds at exceptionally well. One of the ending cutscenes is one of the most jaw-dropping things I've seen in a game. I won't say in what way.

No Man’s Sky is easily one of the best and most feature-packed space exploration games out there. The sheer amount of content, freedom, and things to discover is absolutely incredible. Whether you want to explore the far reaches of the universe, build an empire, become a space pirate, collect exotic creatures, or simply settle down on a beautiful planet and build a home, this game gives you the freedom to play however you want. One of the most impressive features is the seamless transition between space and planetary exploration. You can fly directly from space down to a planet's surface without loading screens, fly like a plane through a planet's atmosphere, explore the terrain, and land practically anywhere you want. With the right technology installed, you can even land on water! And there's no shortage of places to call home. You can build elaborate bases on planets and even underwater bases, construct outposts on massive asteroids, create your own space stations, and even build and customize your own massive freighters, which essentially serve as mobile bases you can take with you across the galaxy. You can also claim abandoned or NPC-operated space stations, renovate them, expand their interiors, and make them your own. If that's not enough, you can take control of planetary settlements and develop them into thriving little cities, making decisions that affect their growth and development. The sheer scale of the universe in No Man's Sky is almost impossible to comprehend. There are 256 unique galaxies to explore, each containing roughly 4.2 billion star systems per galaxy, with an estimated 18.4 quintillion procedurally generated planets and moons across the universe. That's 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 possible worlds to discover! Each one can have its own landscapes, environments, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and points of interest. No Man’s Sky’s universe is so unbelievably massive that you could spend your entire lifetime exploring and still barely scratch the surface. You'll never come close to seeing even 1% of its universe. Exploration is a huge part of the experience. There are countless planets to discover, each with different environments, landscapes, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and sometimes extremely dangerous hazards. You can discover strange alien creatures, scan plants and animals, uncover ancient ruins, search for buried treasures, explore abandoned facilities, and stumble across all sorts of unusual discoveries. There is also deep-sea exploration, alien ocean life, submarine vehicles and underwater base building. You can even name planets, creatures, and star systems you discover yourself. Space exploration is also a huge part of the experience, and there's much more to it than simply flying between planets and star systems. You can discover and explore abandoned, procedurally generated derelict freighters drifting through space. These massive ships are filled with dangerous environmental hazards, hostile enemies, valuable loot, and technology waiting to be recovered. There's also Space Hulk exploration, where you encounter massive abandoned ships that can be dismantled and salvaged for valuable resources, technology modules, and blueprints. Using a gravity gun built into your multitool and a ship-mounted tractor beam, you can literally tear these enormous wrecks apart piece by piece. But it's not without its risks! These operations can be extremely dangerous, as you have limited time to salvage everything before the wreck explodes. You also have to be careful about which sections you remove, because pulling the wrong components can trigger an explosion prematurely. It's a fun, high-risk activity that adds another exciting dimension to space exploration. There's also an incredible amount of variety when it comes to missions and activities. The game has numerous questlines, side missions, storylines, and challenges to keep you busy. There are special community events and limited-time Expeditions that introduce unique objectives and challenges, often rewarding you with exclusive ships, cosmetics, decorations, companions, and other items you can bring back to your main save. Speaking of companions, you can hunt down, adopt, and tame all sorts of alien creatures. You can customize and genetically modify them, even introducing mutations to improve their stats and abilities. You can take them on adventures, use them as companions, and even participate in creature battles against other players and NPCs. If you prefer a more relaxing experience, there's fishing, too! You can find different types of fish, collect them, and cook them into meals that provide useful buffs. There's also a farming system where you can grow a variety of plants and harvest resources to craft ingredients, create food, and produce valuable items. Cooking itself is surprisingly extensive, with all sorts of recipes to experiment with. For those who enjoy ships and space combat, there's plenty to get into as well. You can discover, purchase, collect, upgrade, and customize different types of starships, each with its own design and purpose. From nimble fighters and explorers to massive haulers and exotic ships, there's something for everyone. You can engage in space battles, fight pirates, raid cargo fleets, participate in dogfights, and even become a pirate yourself. You can also assemble and command your own fleet of frigates, sending them on expeditions to gather resources and rewards. One of my favorite features of No Man’s Sky is the incredible ship customization. You're not limited to simply buying ships and upgrading their stats. You can actually salvage and dismantle many of the smaller starships for their individual components, then use those parts to construct and customize your own ships. This allows you to mix and match different components to create a ship with a look and style that's entirely your own. And then there are Corvettes, which take ship building to an entirely different level. These are much larger, fully customizable ships that you can purchase or build yourself by collecting the necessary parts and components. What makes them especially cool is that they're practically small mobile bases! You can walk around inside them, decorate their interiors, and install useful facilities such as crafting stations, healing stations, and storage. It's almost like having your own personal spaceship that you designed from the ground up. There are also several different exocraft vehicles you can unlock, build, upgrade and drive across planetary surfaces. These range from fast, nimble vehicles (a bike or buggy) for getting around quickly to larger, more heavily equipped vehicles designed for exploration, combat, and resource gathering. And if exploring on land isn't enough, you can even build and pilot a submarine to explore the depths of those incredibly deep oceans, discovering underwater creatures, resources, and points of interest that you wouldn't otherwise be able to reach. There's a deep crafting, gathering, and resource-management system that gives you plenty of reasons to explore. Mine resources, refine materials, manufacture technology, upgrade your equipment, improve your multitool, and constantly work toward making your character, ships, and bases better. There's also an extensive trading system, allowing you to buy and sell goods, take advantage of different galactic economies, and build up your wealth. Multiplayer adds another layer to the experience. You can explore the universe with friends, build bases together, participate in missions, visit other players' creations, and take part in community activities. The game even has a shared social hub (The Space anomaly): A social hub where you can meet other Travelers, access missions, purchase upgrades, and interact with other players and embark on adventures together. Game is a great introduction into jumping territory. Instead of dumping all the mechanics on the player at once, the game introduces them gradually, one by one. Main story route introduces collectibles which do not matter and only purpose (outside of achievements little bit) is to make the player dip into higher difficulty jumps. Once you finish the game (main storyline eta 6 hours), you are either satisfied or you want more jumping levels and this game provides that. Pros: + For the main storyline, levels are made short to be less frustrating, which worked + Great music/sfx + Pixel art for level design is a great choice, considering you have less distraction in the level while enough orientation where everything is + Cute story, good enough to enjoy it while also not really necessary to focus on + Game has great level of key imputs, feeling like most of the mistakes player makes are on him + Developers gave some generous hitboxes Cons: - Like i get it, but i really hated cycles, where you have to estimate them from start and hopefully hit them in the middle of room. - In later levels i got somewhat confused of the path i need to take. In some cases i had to search up the solution. Can be called skill issue and someone finds them as a puzzle to solve, but i would love some indicators instead. Final result for completing all achievements: 57 hours and ~16 000 deaths. Am i Proud of it? Yes, for my first jumping genre game outside of Hollow Knigh/Silksong i think i did well and i enjoyed every moment.

Not even on sale. tldr: Dying Light 1 was an action horror game featuring parkour with stealth elements and opportunities. Dying Light 2 is a stealth horror game with action elements and parkour opportunities. There's nothing in Dying Light 2 that can't be found being done better in zombie games like the first Dying Light, Dead Island, or Dead Island Riptide. If you're a fan of those games, and are hoping Dying Light 2 is going to keep the high energy parkour action going---well, it's just not. Dying Light 2 is a ponderous slog compared to its predecessor. Watch the first Steam trailer and notice how all the player POV is during DAYLIGHT . . . because nighttime is all about creeping and stealth and is boring to watch in a video. In DL1 the most terrifying and dangerous zombies haunted the darkness, so not being out at night was a primary device creating tension in the game. At night the zombies were faster and deadlier and stealth becomes a key consideration to player survival. With the exception of a couple missions, it was entirely up to the player how much of this "night game" they wanted to play, allowing for players to shape the tone and expand the action of the game for themselves. From the outset Dying Light 2 seems determined that you WILL spend a lot of time in slowly, carefully, tediously creeping around in the dark. In DL2 the "day game" "night game" choice has been functionally removed from the player. G'bye parkour-filled, action-packed "day game" fun we experienced DL1. I'm just not interested in being forced to do a lot of stealth in a game I bought for its parkour mechanics and zombie slaying violence. I'll never get my money's worth out of playing Dying Light 2 because it's not a game I would've ever spent any money on if I'd known it was going to be such a bore.

Simply put, Terraria is one of if not the most enjoyable action sandbox game money can buy. To explain the rough idea of Terraria it runs off of player curiosity and the natural urge to explore new things, you'll find yourself asking "What's this? or "Who's that?" or "Does this hurt me?" every moment you play. I'm aware of the turn offs such as "It's too grindy" or "There's no guide to progression" but thats the entire intent of Terraria, it's built for you to learn on your own through exploration, stay in certain areas to kill certain enemies for specific drops needed to progress. In nature this is a grindy and long-winded game but for all the right reasons. I'll keep it concise in a bullet point list as to what Terrarias progression looks like to the average player (my own time played totals to around 1.1k hours on Steam but 2k more on other devices). Early Game (Pre-Boss): - Make housing using the beginner tools provided - Delve into the naturally spawning caves in search of loot - Further explore each side of your world to find the two important early parts of Terraria (the jungle and the dungeon - they spawn on opposite sides of the world to each other - the jungle side towards the end near the ocean has an important but not necessary biome deep underground known as the shimmer, search it up if you want a deeper look) - Prepare arenas for upcoming bosses and events Mid Pre-Hardmode (Post Eye/Evil Boss/Queen Bee): - Talk to that guy you may have met at the dungeon and summon his curse with your well-earned gear - Explore the dungeons depths once you have beaten Skeletron - Search the gold chests with the gold key drops (can drop from dungeon pots, dungeon enemies, dungeon slimes most commonly or rarely wood chests in the dungeon) - Grab your dungeon loot alongside the possibility of an obsidian key to unlock those locked chests in hell if you've stumbled into there yet - Grab your hell loot from the chests and build a long platform in hell, you're gonna need it End Pre-Hardmode: - Find a guide voodoo doll dropped from voodoo demons in hell into a pocket of lava, if you can't get this to drop make a house for the guide to move in just above hell and cause him to fall into lava in hell - Kill the Wall of Flesh and you're officially halfway through the game (at least in my eyes) I'll leave it at this as to not ruin the exciting changes hardmode brings, bare in mind hardmode is not a difficulty changer but does bring stronger enemies while keeping the previous ones you've fought. Message me if you'd like someone to help bring you into this game (I love teaching others to play this game thats given me endless wonder for many years and many more to come). If you end up beating Terraria and doing everything you want to, Great! Theres a wonderful modding community over at tModLoader that has endless content for you to enjoy (I'm making my own mod but my personal favourite choice is the Calamity Mod that practically doubles Terrarias content). I hope I was convincing enough, please do buy this game we need to crack top ten games of all time. <3

就冲波兰蠢驴的次世代，重制+新dlc上，必须给一个好评。 从剧情和任务设计上，巫师三无疑是十分优秀的，无论是游戏中的次要角色，还是主要角色，都被塑造的栩栩如生，个性鲜明。巫师三的魅力永远都源自选择，从故事的最开始我们就要做出选择，这些选择不仅仅只是影响当下，有些时候我们做出的选择，会在后续的游戏一直影响着我们。游戏偏中世纪的风格与法术的结合，给出了一种完全不同的中世纪体验。 但巫师三作为一款已发售十余年之久的游戏，自然存在一些问题，战斗系统稍繁冗且单一，总结起来就是叠buff+法印+砍砍砍。巫师道具是这个题材的一大特色，但是作为一款需要上百小时通关的游戏，会不会有点太单一了呢，虽然技能树以在一定程度上改变法印的效果，但是仍旧显得平平无常。近几年广受好评的游戏，就拿cyberpunk2077举例，游戏里无数的枪支类型与流派搭配，可以让玩家花费很大的经历去研究，但这一点显然是巫师三最大的诟病。 overall，作为一款2015年发售的游戏，波兰蠢驴对这一ip的重视我们都有目共睹，剧情的叙述，角色的构造和任务的设计都是十分出色的，但游戏的战斗玩法在如今百花齐放的2026年显得过于单一。

我好像做了一场梦, 置身于一座陌生的城市, 以旁观者的视角, 看着每一个充满代价的选择, 一段成为传奇的经历, 两个不完美人格争夺一具身体, 最终迈向注定死亡的悲剧. 这场梦越到后来越不像冒险, 而像一场缓慢的清算. 夜之城用霓虹许诺自由, 却用账单、义体维护、公司合同和生存期限把自由折算成价格; 它让人相信身体可以更换、记忆可以购买、意识可以上传，却从不回答替换血肉之躯后“我”还剩下什么. V 与强尼共用一具濒死的身体, 一个想活命, 一个想赎罪, 一个用谎言争取时间, 一个用愤怒证明存在；互相入侵、互相辩驳、互相在对方身上留下无法擦除的影子. 当我以旁观者之名按下选择, 实则每一次选择都在分配失去：失去朋友、失去身体、失去记忆、失去自我，或失去让“自我”继续存在的可能. 所谓传奇，不过是夜之城把一个人的挣扎包装成可消费的故事；所谓结局，也没有胜利者，只有不同形式的代价. 在高科技、低生活的社会里, 技术没有兑现救赎, 只是把压迫做得更精密, 把人的身体、情感与意识逐项标价. 当技术成为权力、身体成为商品、意识成为数据, 人便被迫在最狭窄的缝隙里回答那个古老而残酷的问题——我是谁? 而赛博朋克最冷峻之处正在于: 它不提供完美选择, 只逼你在不完美的世界里, 带着代价确认自己曾经活过、爱过、反抗过，并在系统收走一切之前, 留下一个未必胜利却仍属于“我”的答案. 梦醒之后, 夜之城依旧灯火通明. 只是我已分不清哪一段记忆属于 V, 哪一段属于强尼, 哪一段属于真正的“我”. 全成就通关, 感谢陪伴.

Dota 2 is a great MOBA that's being held back by nothing more than its player base and mediocre management. Before you're allowed to play ranked, you're forced to endure 100 hours of unranked matchmaking. Doesn't sound too bad in theory, until you realize that unranked is essentially a free-for-all with absolutely no standards. You'll be matched with players who can barely manage to breathe without choking on their own saliva, as well as players with over 7,000 games under their belts. You'll encounter smurfs and players who don't care about winning. Not necessarily because they don't want to win, but because they refuse to learn, hiding behind the classic excuse: "It's unranked, bro." While unranked isn't something you're supposed to take particularly seriously, when you're still grinding through those 100 hours, you don't really have a choice. You're effectively being held hostage by people who have absolutely no respect for your time. Furthermore, there isn't a single good region to play in, as each one comes with its own unique brand of toxicity. Play on EU East, and you'll be greeted by four egotistical morons suffering from main character syndrome, who refuse to play support and wouldn't buy a ward to save their lives. Play on EU West, and you'll be met with four misfits who refuse to communicate in English. Play on NA, whether East or West, and there's a 50% chance your match will contain bots. And no, I'm not talking about Valve's bots. I'm talking about mediocre, third-rate scripts that run down lanes and die repeatedly. "Are you sure they're not just new, bad players?" Yes, I am. Every single one of these bots follows the same naming conventions and behavioral patterns: "AdjectiveName####", usually accompanied by a QR code or a picture of a girl as their profile picture. They also constantly spam chat wheel emotes, making them about as subtle as a brick through a window. And the saddest part of all this is that the game itself is genuinely fantastic. When you find yourself in a match with nine other like-minded individuals who have even a shred of competitive spirit and genuinely want to win, there's no other game that comes close to the satisfaction of winning an intense, hour-long match of Dota. The hero design is amazing, the mechanics are smooth and satisfying, and the items are meaningful, often fundamentally changing how you approach and play the game. There's an incredible amount of depth here, and very few games can deliver the same experience. People often say that Valve doesn't care. Personally, I think Valve is ashamed of its own creation and, more importantly, the community it has cultivated. I would pay every cent I have, and every cent I will ever earn, just to gather the entire player base into one gigantic trebuchet and launch them into shark-infested waters. Game: 8/10 Players: -5/10

text_clean: 上古卷轴 5 作为一款 2011 年发布的游戏，其内容大致为扮演一个幸运的天选之人在开放世界地图上探索和冒险，顺着主线认识、寻找和完成自己的使命，并遇见不同的角色。 如果用一句话评价，我会说「这是一款具有开创性的商业化开放世界老式ARPG游戏」。 上古卷轴 5 有很多当时新鲜而现在看来则是细致的游戏机制，从在当时较为新鲜的基于双手的装备机制、各种各样的龙吼能力、有物理效果并且可交互的物品效果，到融合一体的战斗、炼药、武器打造、技能树系统，作为一个ARPG给了很高的游玩自由度，相似地玩法让人想起 Elona（一个2009年的回合制RPG，但同样有着甚至更为有趣的系统）。上古卷轴 5 的玩法即便放到今天依然不过时，可以称作是大师之作。 游戏的画面虽然在 2026 看来已经有些糟糕，但是其底子依旧有股神韵，尤其是当视角看向刚刚跳下的巨大雪山之时，看见山路和云雾缭绕很难想象刚从一个现在看起来很可能存在空气墙的地方跳下来。而除了山，各个城市的独特风光也让人印象深刻，最好的一点证明是我去一座城市就会明显感觉到这座城市和其他地方的明显不同。 因为这些基底，上古卷轴 5 即便放在今天依旧是一款不错的好游戏。但同时放在今天也会出现其所欠缺的设计问题以及其他问题。 最显然的是上古卷轴 5 的剧情和任务系统。上古卷轴 5 的剧情缺乏现在的网状叙事和多结局，而是完全的单结局，这会让现在的玩家沮丧——试想一下，有一个npc可以靠玩家的力量救下，但是选项不让你选，如果强行救下，脚本则让npc自动死亡。而另一个问题则在于剧情里面竟然有硬造困境而产生的毒点在主线上，多少是浪费了书籍和先前系列构建的上古卷轴世界观。 虽然有些剧情上的毒点，但总得来说还是值得推荐的作品。

This game might not be quite as good as Borderlands 2, but it's still a lot of fun and has a lot of content to enjoy, especially if you get both season passes. I went for 100% completion and got every achievement in the game, but I got a little fatigued from it after 197 hours and decided not to pursue every vehicle paint job, especially since some of the paint jobs are not even obtainable anymore. Parts of the game were very challenging and near impossible without finding and adding another player to the party (which can also be a challenge in itself since the game is now old and it's hard to find other players). I played Moze the Gunner in this game and had trouble trying to survive in a challenging area alone until I found out that the character, with the right spec, can transfer aggro to her robot/mech suit (called "Iron Bear") with an ability called Auto Bear, which allows you to exit the mech and still have it in the field for 15 seconds, making it a kind of NPC tank. Once the 15 seconds are over, the Iron Bear charges an enemy and explodes. But even before it does that, the ability is refreshed and you can just summon it again. Exit the vehicle immediately and rinse and repeat until you win! I also enjoy the elemental status effects, which gives you good reason to carry multiple weapons outside of the four gun slots you eventually acquire. The Shock element drains enemy shields fast, while Corrosive melts armor and Fire burns through flesh quickly. There's even a Cryogenic element that freezes and slows enemies as well as the new Radiation element that does bonus damage not only to one target but to other enemies around it. The Explosive element found in the preceding games is technically gone, but now exists as splash damage. I often found myself juggling guns and equipment around and keeping a lot of them stored in my bank because I found so many of them incredibly useful in different situations. Borderlands 3 has some shortcomings, however. For starters, the dialogue lacks the macabre humor of the first two games, and within just a few hours you grow tired of the annoying automated quips and sayings of the player character. By the hundredth hour mark you're very, very tired of it and wish you could just turn it off somehow. Another thing I got tired of was opening boxes. There must be hundreds of thousands of green-lit containers throughout the game, and you're obligated to open almost all of them, especially early on. These containers can hold ammo, money, guns, and equipment. But again, after playing for over 100 hours, this gimmick just gets really old and laborious. Overall this game is a straightforward and effective looter-shooter. If you're a Borderlands fan, I'd definitely recommend this game.

I've had NMS in my library for years. I played it once waaay back after buying it at a price that was almost nil because of the bad luck and press the devs had received starting before 2020. I THINK I played it but it might have been Elite Dangerous (ambitious but .... nah). But it always forced itself on my radar. Then I watched an old (6 YEARS!) episode of Internet Historian on YouTube titled "The Engoodening of No Man's Sky" and as old as it was? To tell the story It started off rough and then after watching Hello Games almost pushed up a giant & tall tree farmed by press and expectations (and ridiculous deadlines) into awkward and untenable positions as they climbed up and then fall hitting every branch on the way down? My heart felt for them. Having it (humorously) all broken down bit by bit and everything that led to the fall from a height that they never expected to be at when they were shoved. Then get up, dust themselves off and get back to work making the game they promised with free updates and then go beyond adding more free updates (yes even this year as we recently experienced) for almost a decade after people had completely written NMS sky off? Is an incredible and dedicated come back story that is tribute to the perseverance of everyone at Hello Games making sure their vision and the expectations of the fans (and jilted early owners of NMS) were met and vindicated. And the history I watched (as I said) was 6 years old! Then I saw a new huge update coming for NMS and decided to wait for release and finally PLAY it. I have to say I had to watch a ton of tutorial videos on YouTube (after sifting through the videos that can date up to 10 years old). It was hard catching up as I noticed what huge international player base existed. I still have my questions about certain things large and small that I have to research or just put on hold unless it is a "need to know now" situation involving gameplay or mechanics. So.... is it good? Yes, it is great. Does it have a learning curve involving a buttload of information? Yep. But I am making my way just fine. Still have stop and do research if I can't find it on my phone right away. But therein is the greatness of this game. Making tutorial to a game that is always getting updates is HARD. But getting in the game and "getting caught up" to understanding how to play the current build is worth it. If you are on the fence or have been bored by other space exploration games that were ballyhooed as the next "Big Title" that turn sour? Don't let that or anything else stop you from jumping into No Man's Sky. So much has been endured by other players and so much work has been relentlessly put into this game. Odds are, you will experience that to your enjoyment. 354 hours in, I can safely say that I recommend this game..... Haha!

游戏内容真不错，推荐给那些真正喜欢冒险剧情的玩家。次世代整整玩了3遍所有内容，重制版通关本体后才真正的感觉腻了。剧情没得说，玩了几次都很好玩，就像看电影一样怎么都看不腻。中文配音也是味真足，你觉得捧读并非是因为配音演员技术不行，而是蠢驴自己审核要求的字正腔圆，只有几处小支线的情绪表达有点儿素材复用的感觉。 战斗系统确实很不错，天赋流派设计很出色，但就是一周目很难吃饱，导致你必须开控制台或者二周目去继续体验。但二周目的数值乱填导致你非常脆皮，不玩瘾头吃煎药根本扛不住BOSS和某些小怪的普通一击，属于好机制遇到了烂数值，某种程度上还原了原著但却没完整还原。就算如此，打完二周目你也不会腻，毕竟一周目玩腻了刀剑，谁不想体验二周目的大法师杰洛特？零帧起手法印轮读毁天灭地，叶和特看到了也得说一句NB。强到你会觉得敌人太弱了，然后开启死而无憾难度，再被路边野狗一口咬死，最后老老实实的降低难度。这就是蠢驴的神秘数值设计，就像隔壁2077你不拉高难度就会觉得设定崩坏一样。所以游玩的时候不要把某种打法优化的太猛，只要自己玩的舒服就行。数值的终点是瘾头，机制的终点是法印，狄拉夫会让你见识到艾瑞汀有多丢人，二周目再教你真实的杰洛特有多脆皮。 重制版算是我的四周目了，先通了本体，剩下的放到明年等旧时曲一起玩。
