Warframe: The Endless Treadmill of Manufactured Boredom Introduction: The Illusion of Space Ninja Supremacy Developed by Digital Extremes, Warframe is frequently praised in the free-to-play market as a shining beacon of consumer-friendly game design. On paper, it promises a hyper-stylised, high-speed power fantasy featuring cybernetic space ninjas, fluid parkour, and hundreds of unique weapons. However, beneath its flashy, high-fidelity exterior lies a deeply bloated, profoundly disjointed, and structurally broken experience. It is a game that values breadth over depth, masquerading artificial time-gates and an endless, multi-layered grind as meaningful content. It is less of an interactive game and more of a beautifully rendered digital spreadsheet designed to waste thousands of hours of your life. Honestly, after dealing with the constant roadblocks and forced waits, the core structure of this game feels like a total piece os shit] . [hr][/hr] The Critical Breakdown 1. The Core Loop: A Mile Wide, But an Inch Deep Warframe’s biggest structural flaw is its complete inability to meaningfully iterate on its core gameplay. The game has expanded rapidly over the years, but instead of refining what works, the developers continuously introduce entirely separate, half-baked islands of content that are abandoned immediately after launch. The Content Island Syndrome: Mechanics like Archwing (space flight), Railjack (ship combat), and the various Open Worlds operate in completely isolated silos. The resources you spend hundreds of hours grinding in one zone are completely useless in the next, destroying any sense of cohesive progression. Total Absence of Endgame: Once you have optimized your mods and weapons to deal millions of damage, you realize there is absolutely nowhere to use them. The "endgame" consists entirely of running the exact same low-level missions you did in your first hour, just with exponentially higher enemy health pools. [hr][/hr] 2. The Progression Nightmare: Pay or Wait While Warframe technically allows players to earn everything without spending real money, the mechanics utilized to incentivize premium currency (Platinum) are aggressively anti-consumer and disrespectful of player time. Mobile-Game Style Time Gates: When you finally spend days grinding the rare components to craft a new Warframe, you are forced to wait a literal 72 real-world hours for the foundry to build it. Weapons take 12 to 24 hours. This artificial stalling serves zero gameplay purpose other than to bully the player into spending premium currency to skip the wait. The mechanics in this loop are absolute [shit] . The Inventory Slot Tax: You have severely limited slots for frames and weapons. If you do not pay Platinum to unlock more slots, you are forced to permanently delete weapons and characters you spent dozens of hours leveling up just to make room for new ones. [hr][/hr] 3. Horrendous New Player Onboarding and Systems Bloat Attempting to play Warframe in the modern era without having three distinct wiki tabs open on a second monitor is an exercise in pure futility. In-Game Obfuscation: The game refuses to explain its most critical systems. Modding mechanics, damage types, status procs, and Lich systems are buried behind opaque menus and horrific user interfaces. Unchecked Feature Creep: Rather than cleaning up the baseline experience, the game features a staggering amount of abandoned, bloated systems thrown at the player simultaneously with zero cohesion. It is an overwhelming mess of acronyms and currencies designed to induce burnout. [hr][/hr] 4. Power Creep and the Death of Engagement Any semblance of tactical gameplay or challenge died years ago. Modern Warframe is an automated clicker game dressed up as an action title. Mindless Power Creep: Due to years of unmanaged balancing, players can easily build characters that wipe out entire maps of enemies instantly through walls without ever looking at them. The Co-Op Disconnect: Playing with a squad doesn't foster cooperation; it turns the game into a visual-effects-heavy race. You will routinely load into a mission only to chase a high-level player who clears the entire map instantly, leaving you to sprint through empty hallways picking up dropped loot. It is profoundly unengaging. [hr][/hr] Definitive Conclusion Warframe is a masterclass in psychological manipulation and artificial longevity. It hooks players with exceptional movement mechanics and a flashy art style, only to trap them in a predatory cycle of grinding for the sake of grinding. You aren't playing to overcome challenges; you are playing to watch a progress bar tick up so you can unlock a weapon that lets you watch the next progress bar tick up slightly faster. If you value your time and crave games with tightly designed loops, meaningful narratives, and true mechanical depth, stay far away. Warframe is a glittering, endless treadmill that will leave you completely hollow after hundreds of hours. Critical Assessment Matrix Narrative Cohesion: 4.0/10 Progression Design: 2.0/10 New Player Onboarding: 1.0/10 Respect for Player Time: 0/10 Overall Definitive Rating: 3.0/10 — A Beautifully Painted Waste of Time.

一、核心玩法循环 玩家扮演黑客 Marcus Holloway，在旧金山湾区执行 DedSec 的行动。核心循环为：接取行动（潜入戒备森严的建筑、提取或破坏数据）→ 运用黑客工具箱化解威胁 → 完成任务 → 累积"粉丝（Followers）"→ 解锁更强力、更远程的黑客能力。 - 黑客工具箱：智能手机远程入侵（红绿灯、摄像头、ctOS 联网设备）、四轴无人机（高空侦察 / 标记）、RC Jumper 跳跳车（狭小空间潜入）、环境陷阱（爆炸管道、叉车、吊车）与社会工程。 - 三种推进风格：幽灵（全程不进入区域）、潜行、以及正面火拼——批评普遍认为战斗是最弱的一环，游戏最佳体验来自非致命的智取。 - 粉丝系统即进度机制：粉丝越多，黑客范围与强度越大，形成清晰的成长曲线。 - 任务与模式：主线行动、支线世界故事、双人无缝合作（自由漫游 / 合作行动）、可选 PvP 入侵（赏金猎杀 / 黑客竞速），以及收集品与赛车等。 - 合作与 PvP：支持双人无缝 Drop-in 合作；PvP 入侵为可关闭的可选内容。 二、画面与音效表现 画面：明亮、鲜活的旧金山湾区复刻（金门大桥、渔人码头、硅谷写字楼），街头动态（涂鸦、路人、撑伞市民）营造出"城市旅游模拟器"般的真实感；美术风格为风格化写实，氛围轻松。不足：复杂场景中视觉信息密度高，守卫的红色描边难以辨识，影响潜行判断；过场为 16:9 带黑边，超宽屏与 HDR 需借助 Mod 才能较好支持。 音效：原声与电台配乐广受好评，贴合科幻 / 恶搞基调；环境音与黑客提示反馈到位。整体"不拖后腿"，但无突破性表现。 三、性能与优化 - 硬件门槛低：官方最低为 GTX 660 / HD 7870 + 6GB 内存，推荐 GTX 780 / R9 290 + 8GB；50GB 安装体积。在主流及旧硬件上 1080p 流畅，PC 移植在早期被评价为顺畅。 - 物理帧率上限：游戏物理按 60 FPS 设计，高于此帧率可能导致布娃娃 / NPC 异常。 - 现代硬件已知问题（2026 年玩家需重点关注）： - NVIDIA RTX 30 / 40 / 50 系严重闪烁：天空盒与阴影持续高频闪烁，官方至今未修复；社区 workaround 为 NVIDIA Profile Inspector 驱动级覆盖，或 DXVK 包装（但会禁用联机 / EAC）。 - AMD 显卡崩溃：可通过修改 WD2_GamerProfile.xml 中 DeferredFxQuality="pc" 缓解。 - 卡顿：建议装于 SSD、关闭多人功能或 EAC、对进程关闭 Control Flow Guard。 - Windows 11 24H2 启动异常、现代 Core i9 的 E-core 调度问题（可用 Process Lasso 仅保留 P-core）等亦见报告。 - 综合来看：本作在"能跑"的旧硬件上体验稳定，但在新 GPU / 新系统上需手动调校，门槛主要体现为兼容性问题而非性能不足。 四、付费模式与 DLC（买断制） - 性质：一次性买断制，非免费游戏；DLC 为额外付费层。原价约 $60/£40，现常年深度折扣（完整 Gold 版在促销期常低于 $5）。 - 版本差异： - 标准版：游戏本体。 - 豪华版（Deluxe）：本体 + Deluxe Pack（仅外观）。 - 黄金版（Gold）：本体 + Deluxe Pack + 季票（Season Pass）。 - 季票内容：十二宫杀手任务、Defalt 套装、载具与武器皮肤、T-Bone 内容包（含 Mayhem 合作难度）、Human Conditions（3 段世界故事 + 精英合作）、No Compromise（俄黑帮世界故事 + Showd0wn 合作模式）。 - 外观包：大量 Mega / Supreme / Ultimate 等捆绑包，均为纯外观；Ultra 材质包免费。 - 内购标注：Steam 页面带有 "In-App Purchases" 类别（Ubisoft Connect 内可能存在少量便利 / 外观向消费），但核心玩法不依赖微交易，无抽奖 / 抽卡机制，也无侵略性付费墙。 - 客观评价：作为买断制作品，其变现克制，主要付费点集中在 DLC 剧情扩展与外观，且当前价格极低，性价比高。 五、新手体验 - 门槛较初代更低：基调轻松、角色讨喜（Marcus、Wrench、Sitara、Josh），粉丝系统提供明确成长反馈，黑客工具箱有引导。 - 战斗短板影响手感：角色偏"脆"、掩护系统尚可但敌人爱绕侧、无翻滚闪避；若依赖枪战，新手容易受挫，更推荐以潜行 / 智取推进。 - 潜行识别困难：部分批评指出无人机侦察偏"流程化"，且场景中难辨敌人， stealth 体验偶有挫败。 - 联机入侵建议关闭：入侵模式常匹配到经验老到的玩家，对新手体验不友好，多数建议初期关闭。 - 启动摩擦：Ubisoft Connect + Denuvo + EAC 三层叠加，且新硬件需额外修复步骤，首次上手有一定门槛。 六、长期可玩性 - 内容体量：单人主线约 30 小时，叠加世界故事、季票与合作 / 在线模式后显著拉长；开放沙盒鼓励"整活"式自由实验。 - 衰退因素：支线活动被认为有育碧"罐头"重复感；主线冲突张力偏弱、反派脸谱化；部分玩家指出刷粉 / 任务结构后期趋同。 - 维护现状：游戏已发售约十年，育碧基本停止主动维护，RTX 闪烁等已知问题长期未获官方修复，社区普遍认为 IP 已被搁置。 - 价值定位：在深度折扣下，其开放世界品质与创意黑客系统仍被视为育碧开放世界口碑高点之一，长线"性价比"突出。 优点 1. 创意黑客沙盒：幽灵 / 潜行 / 强攻多路径，自由度高。 2. 鲜活、有生命的旧金山湾区开放世界，氛围与配乐出色。 3. 角色讨喜、基调轻松，粉丝进度系统反馈清晰。 4. 合作体验佳（无缝 Drop-in），PvP 为可选且可关。 5. 买断制、无侵略性微交易，无抽奖；当前价格极低。 6. 在适配硬件上 PC 移植顺畅、配置门槛低。 缺点 1. 战斗 / 射击手感最弱：角色偏脆、无翻滚、敌人绕侧明显。 2. 现代硬件兼容性差：RTX 30/40/50 闪烁、AMD 崩溃、W11 24H2 启动、E-core 调度等需手动修复。 3. DRM 叠层（Ubisoft Connect + Denuvo + EAC）带来启动摩擦。 4. 潜行偶有"流程化"感，场景辨识度低影响体验。 5. 支线重复、主线张力弱、反派脸谱化。 6. 已停止主动维护，已知 Bug 长期未修；物理锁 60 FPS。 适合玩家群体 适合： - 喜爱开放世界沙盒、强调"自由解法"的玩家； - 偏好潜行 / 非致命智取、厌恶无脑枪战的玩家； - 看重合作 PvE、轻松幽默基调与实验性玩法的玩家； - 趁深度折扣低价入库、追求性价比的玩家。 不适合： - 以枪战手感 / 射击爽快度为首要诉求的玩家； - 期望现代游戏持续维护、开箱即稳的玩家； - 反感启动器 / DRM 摩擦、需要原生超宽屏或 HDR 的玩家； - 追求强叙事张力或 PvE 终局深度的玩家。 小结：作为一款约十年前发售的买断制开放世界作品，《Watch Dogs 2》凭借创意黑客系统、鲜活的旧金山湾区与轻松基调，仍是育碧开放世界中的高点之一；其低价格与克制变现构成显著性价比。主要不确定因素来自两方面——一是战斗手感偏弱、叙事张力不足，二是现代硬件（尤其 RTX 30/40/50 系）上的兼容性 Bug 需玩家自行修复。是否入手，主要取决于你能否接受"手动调校 + 智取优先"的游玩方式，以及是否看重折扣期的极低入手价。

First and foremost I'm a life long and very absorbed student of weapons and war - both by education and passion. For absolute breadth there is no game like it and it's absorbed me for countless hours. It's an addictive hobby, but no more so than most others military history nuts come into. The vehicles are amazing and it's a gorgeous game. For sheer cinematic value on average hardware nothing can beat it. That said War Thunder is far from perfect - the attention to crafting the vehicles and weapons is immersive. The battlefields might as well come from Star Fox or Battletech and the community can be more than a little toxic as it includes a lot of youngsters with out any supervision. Arcade mode is just that, and can be a blast - air arcade has some of the most imaginative battlefields and landscapes out there but it's also nuts and you have to just laugh when you get taken out. Ground arcade is just a simplified mode of ground 'Real Battle' with easier aiming and quicker game play. For old eyes like mine it's a go to. If you're not someone who needs a million miles a minute and can cope with slower gameplay, Naval is awesome - and some of the extended conflict matches (bigger maps ~ 2hr games, but you can duck out whenever) are the best game modes War Thunder devs have ever made. Depending on the state of the game it's possible for opposing spawn points (your choice to spawn there) to occur with in less than 5km of one another. For battleships this can be a thrilling point blank 'broadside' fight that is as much a test of fortitude as it is skill. Calling a mode 'Real Battle' is a bit of a farce as well - air consists of a map for ~ 60 aircraft, 30 per side, lined up at 70km distance for jets, and a line of 'ground targets' (very simple firebases) There are 'supply bases' that can be bombed, but both Air Arcade and air 'RB' are filled with dogfight obsessed players, many of whom cannot comprehend why aircraft are included (now to include strategic bombers) that cannot dogfight. High tier featuring many of the slick, modern aircraft featured in promos is nothing but 'missile spam.' Missiles begin flying like a medieval arrow storm at anywhere from 50km on in, and though some claim one can be skilled enough to avoid or dodge (and there is much insulting and name-calling if one cannot dodge how other players think it should be done.) At lower levels air RB can be fun but it gets repetitive. You have no choice of what map you're flying in and you must have your battle lineup selected before time. There is less focus on fighters only but bombers almost always fly alone as there is no real insentive to do otherwise. As a matter of fact there is no real reason to play the game according to militarily accurate tactics at all. Other than a voice comms linked group of up to four can utterly dominate air or ground if the players are adequate and good at covering one another. People from some areas in the world are accused at length of cheating because their gaming culture is competitive and collaborative - there are highly developed 'clans' or squadrons that have extremely well thought out and coordinated 'battle nets' allowing even randomly spawned 'allies' to coordinate and work efficiently. For lone wolf players this can be frustrating to the point of infuriating and cause...again...toxic behavior and words of team chat. Sim is the 'redheaded stepchild' of War Thunder and only Air Sim is worth mentioning. Play is strictly first person (from the cockpit) and the maps range from 64 x 64km to 128 x 128km. Battles are long, and there is bigger balance between strike & bomber players, and fighter pilots. Flight models can vary radically from RB and often planes that are dogs in that mode shine in Sim. 90% of content creators, especially those famous for rating vehicles, ignore this mode as the younger crowd looking for short games considers it 'boring.' For the most part the sim community is small enough that you get to know other regular players - the best part being you aren't restricted to a random map and bunch of players. If you don't like a particular map, choose another. If you find someone you detest in the lobby, go to another one. Gaijin, War Thunder's developer, has a very puzzling if straight forward business model...and they also listen way too much to 'the mob' on their forums. Besides their ability to take any new game mode and ruin it: a new 'nuclear escalation' mode is populated by respawning and rage-inducingly accurate SAM sites that are very difficult to eliminate thanks to a unrealistic mechanic where something like 90% of the weapons launched at them are successfully intercepted. One of the main marketing tools is 'snail rage' (Gaijin's logo is a snail) where players end up so angry at the game they either uninstall...or buy a premium vehicle. Which used to help for a while as they tend to be more powerful, but not so much anymore. Further, today's 'top gun' will eventually get either raised in battle rating so it's operating against far tougher (to the point of invulnerable) opponents or have weapons 'nerfed.' Always claiming some new data, game devs routinely take a weapons system that preforms reliably better than others and make it worse. Sometimes it's because the hue and cry of the mob of players (most who are young and often toxic) sometimes it's to sell a new premium vehicle. Last, a word of advice: Free to Play is wholly misleading. Some players pride themselves on climbing the ranks with out paying a dime. They cry about 'pay to win' players but often this is because they don't have a job and don't comprehend that the game is developed as a business. For those playing in places with depressed economies, there is no scaling of costs however and for someone somewhere else in the world paying $80 for a premium vehicle is insane, where as here it's less than a day's wages.

《DOTA2》是一款极其矛盾的游戏。它可能是市面上最不欢迎新手的MOBA，却也可能是这个品类里，一旦玩进去就再也回不去的终极形态。 门槛确实高得劝退。 超过120名英雄、繁复的装备主动效果、反补与拉野机制，再加上天赋、魔晶、A杖以及先天技能等层层叠加的系统，让新手在前几十个小时里几乎必然处于茫然状态。论坛里常有新人抱怨，装备搜索功能至今不够顺手，中文输入法下想找“金箍棒”都搜不明白。匹配体验也不总是友好，炸鱼玩家和强度失衡的ELO机制，会放大新手期的挫败感。 但跨过那道坎之后，它给的回报也是别的MOBA给不了的。 深度首先体现在“每一局都不一样”：超大的地图、密集的野怪营地、几乎每个英雄都能胜任多个位置，再加上装备选择面极广，意味着你很难用一套固定公式赢下去。操作要求反而没有想象中那么苛刻，很多时候更吃的是思路和时机判断，而不是单纯拼手速。更难得的是它的公平性：全英雄免费，付费内容几乎不触及战力，商业化在同类游戏中克制得近乎“不合群”。游戏还在持续“自我革命”，大型版本更新会不断推翻旧理解，让学习本身变成一种乐趣。加上内置的观战系统和强大的游廊自定义内容，即便不打天梯，也有大量可玩的东西。 简单说，DOTA2把几乎所有的“不舒服”都堆在了门口，但门后的世界，是MOBA品类里最深邃、最自由、也最经得起反复咀嚼的那一个。它不讨好你，可一旦你理解了它，就很难再看得上更简单的东西了。

you have a strange relationship when it comes to this game once you've played it long enough. it starts out boring, starts, as a negligible time waster, but then you finally get a run that reminds you what kind of game this is. Then it annoys you, for telling you that you must do this thing, 11 times. then it intrigues you, because by then you will have forgotten that there is more to this than you were told. keep going, and there is even more. go further, and you see your corpse. It's interesting, to see your own dead body moments before you realize you're dying. it's sad, to see what most would call a grace, turn a child's life, into a malevolent cycle of memories fusing together due to oxygen deficiency. it's terrifying, to see the static horrors of mystery men on the telivision tell you what you must prepare for when you die, and that you most likely prepared wrong. it's depressing to call yourself evil. it's bad to say you deserve the torment you went through. it's surreal to see the good memories attack you. it's annoying to pick up marked during curse of the blind.

117小时全成就。 先说缺点：战斗上来说不是一个很有意思的玩法系统，战斗中的演出也并不好看。宫殿的地图虽然设计得不错，但是视觉上以及玩起来都有点无聊。印象空间纯纯负分，要不是有龙司的coop技能，这个真能无聊到把人劝退，而且那个印章，跑一遍居然收集不全，要反复跑，并且随机刷新，太蠢了。 但是这确实本质上是一种galgame啊，日常做得太棒了，真的是角色扮演的感觉。白天的课程、放学后的冒险、晚上的约会，时不时的考试、外出旅游，以及暑假，各种店家和日常事件，加上“台面下”的黑暗涌动，换上怪盗的身份拯救世界，游戏从一开始就以绝对的情绪推动力和代入感将玩家拉入这个世界。虽然有些剧情有点太宅了，有的多少有些诟病，但是日常、coop、以及大部分主线都挺好的。主角实实在在地与各位配角们生活了一年，确实也建立起了感情羁绊，每一个人都很有趣，每一个人到了最后都不想分开（除了明智）。 在原版基础上新增的皇家版内容的话，反派塑造很好，但是动画和演出质量下降很多，学妹的路人感也十分幽默。

Played The Witcher 3 more times than I can count. All the way back in 2015 on PC(GOG) and I’ve also completed it on PS4. When I heard about the remaster and the new DLC coming out in 2027, I knew I had to go back one more time. Having 100% completed it, I can now safely say this is easily one of the greatest games of all time. No one tells a story quite like CDPR and everyone should experience the Bloody Baron questline at least once in their life. There is truly nothing else like it. That said, the remaster isn't without it's issues. Visual bugs pop up, environments(especially indoors) can be excessively dark and performance takes a hit with ray tracing or path tracing enabled. In Novigrad, the framerate drops to nearly half of what it is elsewhere in the game. Going for all the achievements was also a headache, particularly with Gwent cards tied to NPC's that occasionally become unresponsive. These bugs have been around since day one and have never been fixed. Still, these are minor complaints for a game that remains pure joy.

Rust scratches an itch that no other PvP game can. I genuinely love playing this game, but it desperately needs another serious performance overhaul. It's honestly amazing how a game that's been around for this long still struggles to push past 60–100 FPS on most servers unless you're running a newer CPU or one with 3D V-Cache. I can play plenty of other modern titles and comfortably push 150–200+ FPS, yet Rust is one of the only games I play where I'm lucky to consistently break 120 FPS. And apparently, because my CPU doesn't have that magical "3D cache," I'm just out of luck.What's even more frustrating is that it feels like nearly every major update makes performance progressively worse. I understand Rust is a demanding game, especially with large maps, massive player counts, and player-built structures, but at some point, optimization needs to become a bigger priority.I'm not expecting 300+ FPS on a populated server, but I also don't think it's unreasonable to expect consistently good performance on hardware that's still more than capable of running modern games.Please, Face punch, give Rust the performance overhaul it desperately needs. I'd love to enjoy this game without having to sell my organs on the black market just to afford a new motherboard, ram and CPU.I love Rust, but I shouldn't need to build an entirely new PC every few years just to keep up with its declining performance. (This is also the reason I don't have more hours because my performance is so unbelievably terrible that it makes it really unfun to play)

This is the type of game I have wishlisted for a long long time and then end up getting it gifted one day cuz "why not?" and actually end up enjoying it. The game is definitely something I'd call a classic, it's been out for such a long time that my review won't exactly give any more information that there already is, hence why I was hesitant to write it in the first time. It's another roguelike (we love em), a very effective one at that. The amount of items and characters and challenges available even just in base game is insane, I never felt like I was getting bored (not that it's easy to stay nonchalant when everything is shooting your ass) and the more you achieve, the deeper you get to progress. In fact, what left me a bigger impression was not the gameplay itself but the art and the story- it is all so grotesque yet at the same time I feel so curious to understand what can each entity represent. The religious elements, the nudity/exposure of both outside skin and inside organs makes me feel so bad for Isaac, knowing he's just a child filled with so much fear and shame, the more items he picks up which can either be something like maybe cool sounding to just something related to the idea that he is disgusting, stained with his own sins. While my family was never this extremely religious, small part of me relates to how awful it can make you feel. This is something no child should ever go through and it weirdly reminds me of Stephen King's "Carrie". Both being made to feel like they are monsters and nothing more, both having fanatical mothers raise them to think exactly this and, of course, symbolism of blood. The story, for how simple it seems at first, it extremely tragic and has great visual perception of how a child cannot differentiate neglect/emotional and physical abuse and tries to embody it into something more understandable to the child: monsters, devils, spikes. I don't want to exactly spoiler anything but finding out that isaac suffocated in that very chest he hid in and all the dungeon runs were just his imagination during his last moments is really dark but I think the story would not be the same if that wasn't the case. Overall, a game that should be talked about, easy replayability, great story, charming artstyle and the gameplay is not hard to learn but it is hard to master. If you are unsure if this is your cup of tea, you can buy it during a sale and try it out, earlier runs don't take too much time compared to later stuff you end up doing just for a new item and ending :)

Looks good, has nice music, and it sure is entertaining, well, for a time. I enjoy Roleplay, I love Dungeon and Dragons, sadly, both these things are streamlined here, I certainly understand that, they wish to appeal to a bigger crowd. So if you are like me, totally into RPG, branching story, the world, story and people in it changing according to your decisions, you will be disappointed, at some point, it feels shallow. I did play the Pathfinder games, especially Wrath of the Righteous, and as a Roleplayer, I found exactly what I was looking for there, sure, you have to read a lot, it does not look as fancy, but it is filled with content, you can be good, the hero, you can be the most evil monster consuming the world, and both paths are filled with story, the world and people change, and there are so many different classes and paths you can take in between, you can feel the game was made by true Roleplayers, for Roleplayers. As a Roleplayer at heart, I cannot recommend Baldurs Gate 3, if you are into looks, action, shallow Roleplay and watered down D&D experience, I am sure you gonna love this one.

I gave this game a negative review because apparently players are expected to fix it themselves! If, like me, you're experiencing severe LOD (Level of Detail) and texture pop-in issues, here's a potential fix: Press Win + R and enter: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ReadyOrNot\Saved\Config\Windows` Open Engine.ini and add the following lines: [SystemSettings] r.ViewDistanceScale=5 r.StaticMeshLODDistanceScale=0.1 r.SkeletalMeshLODBias=-2 foliage.LODDistanceScale=3 Save the file and restart the game. These settings increase rendering distances and force higher-detail models to remain visible at greater distances, reducing noticeable LOD transitions and object pop-in. Be aware that this may reduce performance depending on your hardware, although I personally haven't noticed any measurable difference. It's ridiculous that players have to resort to manually editing configuration files to fix such obvious graphical issues. This is something the developers should have addressed themselves, not left to the community to figure out.

Before writing any review, I wanted to finish the game properly. And that took me over 150 hours; 150 absolutely AMAZING hours of adventure, filled with unforgettable moments and so many positive emotions. When I first started playing and got into my first battle, I wasn't exactly impressed. The turn-based combat system didn't convince me at all. I guess nostalgia for the good old combat system from Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 was simply too strong. But I decided to give it a chance, and once I got used to it, I realised it actually adds a whole new dimension to the game. The same goes for the party size. Having only four characters instead of the six we had in BG1 and BG2 was initially a bit disappointing. Again, nostalgia talking. But after spending some time with the game, I realised just how brilliantly balanced the four-character party actually is. It adds another layer of complexity, forces you to think more tactically, make better use of every character's abilities, and really get the most out of your party. And then there's everything else... The depth of the game. The seemingly endless possibilities. The decisions and their consequences. The dialogue. The incredible characters and their personal stories. And this is where the game truly shines. Every major character you meet, especially your companions, has an incredibly detailed story of their own, one you can gradually uncover and become deeply involved in. But what makes it so special is that you're not just watching their stories unfold. You're actively shaping them. Depending on your choices, their personalities, relationships, beliefs and ultimately their fates can change dramatically. Who they become and where their stories lead is, to a remarkable extent, in your hands. And those decisions don't exist in isolation. They have consequences, sometimes immediate, sometimes much later when you least expect them. They shape your companions, your relationships, the dynamics of your party and ultimately your entire gameplay experience. It's this incredible sense that your choices genuinely matter that makes the world feel so alive and every playthrough so personal. And, of course, a wonderful dose of nostalgia when Jaheira and Minsc showed up. Seeing those two again was something special... #corememoriesunlocked. :) To spare you another essay, I'll get straight to the point: This game, without a single doubt, is the best RPG I've ever played and easily among my top three games of all time. And the best part? After finishing my first playthrough, I'm already excited about what comes next. Honour Mode, different origin characters, different choices, different approaches, and all the things I haven't even discovered yet. In fact, I've already started my second playthrough. And despite knowing that the main storyline remains the same, thanks to the incredible variety of possibilities, it already feels like I'm playing an entirely new game. So here's to another 150, 300, or even 500 hours of adventure. And somehow, I have a feeling even that might not be enough. :) AN ABSOLUTE MASTERPIECE!!! 100/10!

Elden Ring is bellow average overrated overhyped mediocrity that didn’t deserve GOTY 3.5/10 1. STORY 3/10 Has interesting lore if you watch youtube videos but that is expected to be extra and not something you are obligated to do to understand the story, the story in game is for most part absent… that alone disqualifies the game from 10/10 even if everything else was perfect (everything else is indeed not perfect, actually not even close to 10), even when environmental story telling is used as an excuse, it still does very poor job at it, dark fantasy on its own doesn’t work once its removed from high fantasy setting where usually its just a small part of much bigger world… lord of the rings works because you can see the contrast… when you make the entire world look bleak it doesn’t make you feel anything anymore, and no it has nothing to do with morally ambiguous characters, i prefer those actually, what i don’t like is expecting me to feel something about a world that looks exactly the same… speaking of world 2. WORLD 2/10 Just straight up a chore, want to reach that lake? To bad you can’t glide so you have to go all the way around, fall in a ditch? To bad you can’t climb so you have to go all the way around… want to negate fall damage with the horse double jump? to bad you can’t… like im a missing something here or fromsoft still hasn’t discovered the most core mechanic of double jump… i get that jumping is alien tech to this guys so i guess that explains why it feels so bad, they copied the entire world from breath of the wild but didn’t bother copying the core traversal tools necessary to make the world enjoyable to traverse… other things such as all biomes just morphing into one made me lose complete track of time, everything looks the same (DLSS 5 is not the reason for that) there are so many reused enemies, assets and dungeons that doing any form of side content is not worth it… like its so bad that the map feels procedurally generated but somehow it was hand made? The world is nowhere near as big as people made it to be… pick a farm, milk it until you get as many runes as physically fast as possible for the shortest possible time and min max your character so you can finally do the “campaign” this is literally the entire progression system of the game, speaking of progression 3. PROGRESSION 0/10 Actually horrible, just straight up unplayable without external guide, going blind here would’ve made me uninstall and refund the game…. I never follow build guides for games and beat all the pinnacle bosses in poe 2 and not even once followed a build guides… but here its mandatory to even play the game… NPCs say bunch of nonsense… rarely if ever explain things and for most part ignored them or didn’t even find them… No quest side window or markers means you have no idea what you are supposed to do, world and NPCs don’t make it any easier either… Loot feels horrible which makes no sense for an ARPG, like thats literally the whole point of an ARPG… the loot… how do you screw this bad to the point that the only way to progress is to follow build guides and have to look the individual weapons, items and gear on a website map to find them… no side content such as cave or fortress felt rewarding… (all who were reused assets of course) 4. UI/UX, CONTROLS, CAMERA 0/10 My gosh, the most horrific controls i have ever endured… probably second worse after crimson desert (Thank god didn’t buy that steaming pile of trash) everything is wanky and weird and the UI is atrocious… like there is no way there is no key for inventory… thats straight up disrespectful towards the player… it costs the devs nothing to do that and somehow its missing from the game… game is locked at 60fps and has no DLSS SR forcing me to use mods and also no mini-map, seriously? It doesn’t make the game more realistic or quirky… its annoying af, the whole UI is convoluted and just straight up horrible… even compared to old games its terrible… you know what else is terrible? Camera… can’t imagine that camera with all the AoE garbage in the DLC, good thing is i don’t even plan to find out (even tho i did bought the DLC) 5. GRAPHICS 4/10 They are fine, but they are not as good as people make them, the lighting and skybox is over compensating for the otherwise bellow average mediocre graphics and man there are moments where the textures are so bad it looks like a ps3 game… its so bad that even DLSS 5 doesn’t know what to do with it so it turns it into a giant blob of liquid noise unlike anything I’ve seen before, sure could be a mod problem but toggling it off absolutely showed horrible textures in that spot that don’t match the resolution of the tiles or bricks nearby… creating inconsistent resolutions in the same room… the render distance is bad and the texture quality completely deteriorates on distance the moment you look in any view of the world that wasn’t intended to be used as advertising material (such as limgrave door view) 6. MUSIC 3/10 Aside from the limgrave one, main theme, tree sentinels one and malenia’s song, everything is boring, mid and forgettable… genuinely disappointing music… 7. PLATFORMING -10000/10 don’t ever include platforming section in your games ever again 8. DUNGEONS 2/10 Repetitive, boring and short… same layout for most part… same style, same material… everything just blurs together, the difficulty of the game is extensively used to make the cleaning of this areas far slower to dilute the actual size and length of the dungeons (just like the rest of the game)… there a few that stand out like Stormveil Castle that are medium size but still tiny compared to Zelda standards… overall the dungeons are extremely disappointing and often the way the developers have designed the levels feels like they are making it on purpose unclear so you miss out on “big things”… 9. DIALOGUE, VOICE-LINES, BEHAVIOUR 3/10 I get that Japanese games always have goofy and corny voice lines in their games but elden ring setting and tone is supposed to be serious yet the moment a boss says something its always some non sensical goofy garbage, while the NPCs having those type of lines is sometimes fine, the bosses completely ruin the tone of the game, fromsoft has failed at the first step of making bosses if a boss doesn’t feel scary… and no its appearance is less then 10% of what makes a boss scary, its behaviour and how they speak as well as their ambition is the primarily factor… it feels like fromsoft doesn’t know what it wants elden ring to be, do you want the world to feel cruel and unjust? Then why no encounter ever feels personal? 10. CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP 0/10 Boring, repetitive and unfun, there is no point of killing any of the enemies because they will just respawn every time you go on a bonfire leading to feeling like you are not doing any form of progress, why bother with them if you can optimise for specific farm and only do that instead? And for the items you need you will just follow build guide so you know where to go and how to get what you need… bosses are same story… keep repeating the same thing over and over again until you finally beat it or over level your self so much that you demolish it… no fun middle ground… everything feels like artificial way of increasing the playtime and length of the game. The game has nothing other then difficulty to offer did git gud and beat malenia but to bad the game never got better, tried to like the game but its just not a good game and I don’t think i will be playing anymore (unless i use mods that very heavily alter the gameplay), fromsoft has failed to modernise and keep up with modern standards and thats even more apparent with Nightreign… a game that had massive potential. Also i-frames suck and is the reason why bosses have obnoxious long attack combos as form of corny punishment… no idea what fire giant is and have zero intentions on finding out Also horse armour DLC, you serious?

text_clean: Great Elder Scrolls game. very big world, so many quests to pick and different factions to join although it may get to feel repetitive between the quests like when in the companions where we either ask vilkas or aela, radiant quests they call it, and it feels repetitive with the same type of task but different people and location. But i still like the game so much. restarting a new character then growing him/her into a great figure as we progress through the game (ends up as stealth archer anyway), and the broken exploits like making a ring that has 7856574 carry points or peasant clothing that gives 99999 life is amazing even though i haven't tried it myself haha. it's a way more overhaul and upgrade from the previous game like Oblivion or Morrowind. but to be fair, we all agrree that there are many aspects in both Morrowind and Oblivion that are great and not included in Skyrim. even to me that the voice-acting in Oblivion sounds crispier and more sharp, bold and masculine/feminine than in Skyrim. Nevertheless i'm glad that i repicked up this game a few years ago after feeling that it was a weird game then refunded it, eventually i bought it back. and boy, thank God for the mods especially Beth.INI to make us who have low spec devices to run at decent experience.

本来不想这么早（2024-10-24）玩这游戏的，可实在是太火了，连上小学生的侄子都知道，说要来我家玩，所以就提前下载安装并游玩了。游戏质量确实是够硬，画面质感很棒，怪物设计也各有特色，很多需要对应的解法，以及埋藏了不少的隐藏要素，需要根据NPC提示解开。 其实第一周目的前几关，玩得并不是特别爽，技能太多，技能点不够的问题之前在古剑里，现在在黑神话中又出现了，就导致需要频繁洗技能……看似很人性化的设计，为强迫症玩家带来给多纠结。而且，就算是更高级的技能，在伤害方面没有明显的提升，也会感觉爽度不太够。导致这问题的还一关键在于对敌人的技能不熟，高周目打的时候，敌人虽然难了，但看机会破招，以及各种技能的叠加，也很容易把BOSS玩死（除了大圣）。 最后为了刷成就，我居然打了四个周目，就是因为下毒手这武器。一周目我基本没看攻略，根本不知道有这玩意。二周目我是打完了才想起来有这么个东西。三周目我是以为打断两只手就有……结果发现是因为看错了条件，需要打断四只手……由于这自动存档系统的设定，害我又得来一周目，解锁了所有根器，体验了只有在四周目的大圣模式（然总体并没有多大变化）。还要吐嘈一点的是泡酒物这该死的掉率，我刷了几百个人参才出来，然后发现很多攻略其实并不全，如果程序里是给某颗参100%掉率而其他不掉那我就原谅你而去怪那些攻略视频了。 关卡设计方面前四关都各有各的不错，第五关和第六关却有点敷衍了，特别是第六关刚上筋斗云应该是个很兴奋的设计，然而飞上天没几下就迷路了……这大片的森林设计得真心迷。 人物设计方面除了主角是个哑巴之外都不错，二郎神、弥勒、蜘蛛精等等。真的，主角不会说话代入感还是缺了那么一点点。以至于特别喜欢八戒在身旁的时候，有个人一直陪伴吐槽的感觉很好。 总之，这游戏的巨大成功是件好事，应当对国产单机游戏有很强的推动力，像是仙剑、古剑这种老牌游戏都难产的情况下，更能激励新单机的诞生。

BE THE LEGEND 在全成就达成的今天，写下这篇评价。 其实感受有太多，根本不是几段话能写完的，聊记一二吧。 想起游玩的初期，觉得现实和游戏的差距似乎不太远了，科幻即将变成纪录片，但深入吸收剧情、芯片、广播和数据库的内容之后，地区、阶级、阵营、冲突等概念在脑海里编织成网，回过头才发现自己已经在这个世界里沉浸得那么深了... 感谢CDPR制作出如此伟大的游戏，我永远也不会忘记玩2077的这三个月了。T T 简评一下本体结局吧，最先达成单刷荒坂塔的太阳结局，省时间、战斗爽、无亲友伤亡，最畅快的一条路！非常喜欢任务标题“以我残躯化烈火”，轰轰烈烈地活过，成为城市传奇，也不负时日无多的生命了。没想到会在最后见到蓝眼睛先生，可惜CDPR并没有做水晶宫的内容，V只能在太空遥望一下了。 恶魔结局确实是叛众离亲了，不过这条线的对话非常有意思，一路上会欣赏到荒坂塔的室内和景观设计；和竹村并肩战斗的感觉很棒，如果不是立场和原则的冲突，应该能和他能一直做好朋友吧。赖宣和华子关系微妙，三郎复活过来还挺令人毛骨悚然。结局烂完了，草间太啥哔了，只比个中指我觉得自己太文明了，拧魔方更是吓我一雷。 星星结局也是一路战斗，但不那么流畅，阿德卡多是真把我当家人啊，不过习惯了独来独往，竟然感觉需要适应这种群聚共战、别人乐意为我牺牲的状态。最后坐在魔蜥上吹夜风，很美的镜头啊。 关于DLC，剧情和任务质量已经和本体不在同个档次了。我心所选的是权杖国王结局，高塔结局太让人难受了，经历之后彻底领悟到“窝囊活不如壮烈死”。圣杯国王结局这条线视觉和故事性拉满，虽然在Cynosure设施里搞追逐战太阴森了，但补全了公司战争的背景，流窜AI传信设计得相当对味。如果不体验全结局，会错过很多好剧情。 总之，目前2.5版本更新的任务没做，车和枪都没体验够，我还会常回家看看的。 如果能到2077年还在更新就好了，会是本游戏最酷最赛博的一点。XD

Worth every cent of the $15. There's just so, so many routes and too much stuff to do. Just when you think you're getting closer to the end of the game, the more content it has. Each and every friendship heart interactions are just so unique, and I might even say this game is making me fall in love with these RPG, simulator-like games. Even if you've maybe gotten married, had kids, all of that stuff in just one save file, you can just make a new save file and this time, do it all again, but with a different person and different interactions. The only bad thing I have left to say about this game is probably that it NEEDS voice actors, though there are already mods for it. I know I'm late by like.. 10 years, but I couldn't care less, I just really enjoy the game.

the witcher 3 is a gift that keeps on giving and remains my favourite game to this day. i started a new playthrough when the remaster update rolled out and ended up putting in 150+ hours. coming back to white orchard felt so nostalgic. this game is still one of the most beautiful and immersive worlds i've played, and toussaint looks absolutely stunning in the remaster. i didn't really play gwent the first time around, but got into it this time and it was so much fun. i don't usually do many side quests in games unless i need the xp or a specific item, but the stories behind the side quests in this game are so well written that they're hard to pass up. the choices you make throughout the game have lasting consequences, some of which don't reveal themselves until much later. the only real choice that matters is yen over triss. a few bugs still persist despite the remaster and all the hotfixes. the swamps in velen are one of the areas where you'll still run into the occasional bug and get stuck. even years after your first playthrough, you'll keep discovering new things about this game. it never really gets old, and i'd happily clock another 100 hours next time. props to cdpr for remastering a game that was already this good.

这个游戏承载了我太多的回忆，记得刚开始玩时因为找不到风漂龙退游了很多次，之后在一个朋友的怂恿下又下了回来，并选择了太刀这把武器，从此便一发不可收拾（唉，太刀）......刚开始连成功见切这种操作都难以打出，很多怪都是朋友带着打过的，居合这种高风险高收益的操作更不用说，刚进入冰原时甚至差点一度被虐到退游，不过还是坚持了下来，直到我遇到一个叫“再会了，雷狼龙”的任务......雷狼龙真是太适合太刀练习了，在不断狩猎雷狼龙的过程中我终于可以熟练见切和居合怪物的招式，也逐渐体会到了太刀这把武器真正的魅力。再根据攻略做完了炎王龙校服后终于开始挑战黑龙了，刚开始失败了很多次、使用了各种手段后才艰难战胜P1，最后还是呼叫了天尊，过了第一只黑龙。在攒出黑龙套后决定独自挑战，那时每天刷手机都会看各种太黑攻略，终于在一个星期的不断尝试后用时28分钟独自击败了传说中的黑龙，心中的喜悦难以言喻！之后又去尝试了各种帅气的处理和登龙点，太刀也是玩得越来越熟练了，我也开始冒充天尊帮新入坑的朋友们开荒打怪，那段时间很快乐，电脑完全就是怪猎启动器，集会里非常热闹，出任务时有人被打出大毅力就会有圣人撒粉，有人猫车大家就会狠狠嘲笑......虽然后面因为各种原因大家都淡游了，很久都没有打开过怪猎了，但想起那段难忘的时光还是会很开心！第一次听到月辰据点的背景配乐时，我感到其乐融融，很和谐，现在再听却徒增了一缕淡淡的忧伤，真是怀念那段无忧无虑的日子啊！

game_name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
text_clean: I would like to preface this by saying I love Age of Empires 2. It's my favorite RTS, and one of the best games of all time. The Definitive Edition is arguably the best way to play it That said, I hate how fragile the multiplayer is. It's not possible to re-join a game. This affects team games the most because if a player drops, their team will likely lose This was acceptable in 1999 - friends were playing via LAN. If someone dropped, they could use the "restore game" function It doesn't work in 2026 - strangers are playing via modern matchmaking, if someone drops, they just continue playing It takes one disconnect to lose a 3 hour team game. It doesn't help that the game is prone to crashes As far as I understand DE is based on the original code from 1999. The developers did a great job modernizing most parts. But the multiplayer is just not up to modern standards PS: please fix shift queuing walls

Stepping out of the Stranded Graveyard and into the blinding light of Limgrave for the first time is a moment burned into my brain. The game doesn’t hand you a mini-map cluttered with task markers, nor does it drag you through a two-hour tutorial on how to press buttons. It just places a towering, golden Tree Sentinel in front of you—who will promptly crush you into dust—and whispers, “Go figure it out.” That raw, uncompromising respect for the player's intelligence and curiosity is why I fell in love with Elden Ring. Exploration isn't a chore list; it’s genuine discovery. You see a colossal, decaying castle on the horizon or a faint purple glow down a random elevator shaft, and four hours later you’re deep underground in a subterranean starry night sky fighting a celestial ancestor spirit. Every victory feels earned, and every hidden ruin feels like a secret meant just for you. What truly cements it as a masterpiece for me, though, is the unmatched depth of player freedom paired with FromSoftware's legendary lore and combat design. Whether you want to wield a colossal slab of iron, cast star-shattering gravity magic, or bleed your enemies dry with lightning-fast katanas, the game lets you define your own path to strength. When a boss like Radahn or Malenia pushes you to your absolute limits, it forces you to adapt, learn the cadence of their swings, and master the dance of combat. That cycle—going from getting completely obliterated to seamlessly dodging every strike and landing the final hit—delivers a rush of pure dopamine that very few other games can match. Woven through all of it is George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki’s tragic, haunting world of fractured gods and outer cosmos, turning every ruined church and obscure item description into a piece of a tragic puzzle. It’s relentless, unforgiving, and visually breathtaking—an unforgettable journey from Tarnished nobody to Elden Lord.

I Came for a Tactical Shooter. I Left a Different Person. There are games you play to pass the time. There are games you play because you're bored. There are games you play because your friends are online. And then there is Ready or Not. I genuinely don't know how to put into words what this game has done to me. I installed it expecting a tactical shooter. I expected guns, missions, suspects, some good old-fashioned door kicking and perhaps the occasional questionable decision from my teammates. I was not prepared. I was not prepared for the silence before entering a room. I was not prepared for the sound of footsteps on the other side of a door. I was not prepared for the moment when a suspect refuses to surrender, when a teammate shouts for cover, or when everything goes horribly wrong in a fraction of a second. But most importantly, I was not prepared for the emotional journey. Every mission feels like it means something. Every corner feels like it could be your last. Every time I hear someone shout "POLICE, DROP YOUR WEAPON!" I feel a little part of my soul leave my body. And yet, I keep coming back. I have laughed. I have screamed. I have questioned my intelligence. I have stared at a loading screen wondering where my life went wrong. I have watched my carefully coordinated tactical operation collapse because one person forgot to check a corner. But I have also experienced moments of genuine brilliance. The feeling of clearing a building with your squad, covering each other, communicating properly and somehow making it through an entire mission without everything descending into absolute chaos is something I struggle to find in any other game. There is something special about a game that makes you slow down. A game that makes you think before you act. A game that reminds you that sometimes the most important thing you can do is NOT pull the trigger. And that is what makes Ready or Not so special. It isn't simply about shooting people. It is about restraint, responsibility, teamwork and the weight of the decisions you make. The atmosphere deserves its own appreciation. The sound design, the lighting, the environments, the voice acting, the tiny details scattered throughout every mission. Everything contributes to an experience that can be genuinely uncomfortable in the best possible way. There are moments where I have genuinely forgotten that I am sitting at a computer playing a video game. I am no longer thinking about my keyboard or mouse. I am thinking about the room ahead, the people inside it and whether my squad is going to make it out. And then someone on my team gets stuck in a doorway. Immersion shattered. Humanity restored. I also want to acknowledge the people behind this game. To the developers, artists, sound designers, programmers, writers, animators and everyone else who contributed to this project: thank you. I know that making a game is not easy. I know that behind every little detail that players might overlook are hours of work, problem-solving, frustration and dedication. Most players will probably never stop to appreciate the amount of effort that goes into making a single mission feel believable. They might never think about the sound of a distant gunshot, the positioning of an object in a room or the way an environment tells a story without saying a single word. But somebody made those decisions. Somebody cared enough to make those details exist. And somebody, somewhere, spent an unreasonable amount of time making sure that a door opens in a particular way. I hope those people know that their work matters. Because it does. Games like this remind me why I love gaming in the first place. Not because of graphics, not because of achievements, not because of how many hours I can put into something, but because of the experiences that games can create. The memories. The ridiculous moments with friends. The missions that go perfectly until the final thirty seconds. The missions that go catastrophically wrong from the very first door. The times when everyone is silent because something genuinely terrifying just happened. And the occasional teammate who thinks a flashbang is a substitute for basic communication. I don't know how many more hours I will spend playing Ready or Not. I don't know how many more missions I will complete, how many more times I will get shot through a doorway, or how many more times I will have to explain to my squad that perhaps we should try a slightly different approach. But I do know one thing. Years from now, when I look back at the games I played, I suspect Ready or Not will be one of the ones I remember. Not because it was perfect. Not because every update was flawless. Not because every mission went according to plan. But because it made me feel something. And that is becoming increasingly rare. So, to everyone at VOID Interactive: thank you for creating something that people can genuinely lose themselves in. Thank you for putting so much detail into a game that could so easily have been just another shooter. Thank you for giving us something worth talking about, laughing about, getting frustrated with and returning to. And to whoever designed the AI that can somehow identify my exact location through three walls, a filing cabinet and what I can only assume is divine intervention: I hope you sleep well. You have ruined my life. In the best possible way. 10/10. Would risk my entire squad's wellbeing again. Ready or Not. Because apparently, I wasn't.

母牛：“小明！你的被动好碍事啊！”小明先是一愣，然后马上就理解了母牛的意思，大笑着按了一下shift，说：“哈哈！尽管来吧！”母牛同样大笑着拍上了小明的肩膀，在他之后战甲们也不再拘谨，都带着轻松的笑容，为小明送上自己的祝福。“去吧！笨蛋帽子！”“去证明你不是靠优雅吃饭的男人”“如果很辛苦就换我上吧！”“要赢啊！小明先生！”“鲨客！！”有趣的是，因为缺少双腿的关系，ash只能坐着轮椅撞向小明… 面对浑身裂隙能量喷涌而出的小明，被誉为虚空之王的墙中人，恍惚感受到了犹如排山倒海般的压力【亿万年未有的紧张感再一次浮上心头】。小明的拳头毫不留情砸向拜勒斯（20级适应mod)，致命的红色数字亮起。仓促间用杀妈刀格挡的拜勒斯身体不禁后退，墙中人猛地回头，惊疑不定的表情充分暴露在小明面前。小明利用打出红色暴击（高达三位数的红暴)时进入的【自毁境界】（100万匹力量！！！)将自身状态拉满——暴击发出的一瞬间，平常需要刻意进行的裂隙能量操作都会变得如呼吸一般自然。那是仿佛除自己外的一切都围绕着自己旋转的全能感（实则是被抽陀螺了)。小明死死钳住墙中人的手腕砸向拜勒斯，两者交叠之际，第四发暴击如期而至。拜勒斯用身体护住墙中人连退十数米，借着短暂摆脱纠缠的时机，小明开始近距离吟唱咒词。“招笑”“技能强化”“避难所”——小明就已经抬手对准了天际。墙中人惊慌失措地喊出了拜勒斯的大名，下一秒，拜勒斯像喷气发动机般追放逐而去。眼看拜勒斯已呈败势，墙中人立刻出现，将目标锁定在移速缓慢的放逐上。既然停滞的必经之路挡着小明这尊大佛，那就用【超宏大爹】将放逐无效——无论无效哪一个，只要能阻止四技能能量攒够就可以了。墙中人的身体被小明一拳打歪，可卓越者全家桶还是奔向了天际的放逐，小明望着极速飞行的超绝dot发射器翠玉激光，叹息之墙冰盾，敌方地图炮火圈，逆天伤害火柱，超绝破盾棍母电球，逆天穿盾毒。再次吟唱：“招笑”“花里胡哨”“停滞”。墙中人瞳孔放大，一股寒气扑面而来。在被压缩的时空中，墙中人明白，自己再也没有任何机会阻止灾变的诞生了

First off I have bought this game twice now and have about 200 hours in it. With that experience I can comfortably say the game is fantastically well polished with immense amounts of content. Including story and quest lines, monthly expeditions, system battles, ship and planet hunting, freighter and frigate acquisition, base ship and freighter building, fishing, music making, (Pokémon like) fauna battles, garbage disposal, and much much more. Some things to note are: The initial quest lines are a bit extraneous but that is to be expected for being a decade old. Resource gathering, and travel are a major part in this game, and base building can be limiting for knew users, due to the required steps to get all of the currently obtainable components, and limited un-gliched placement options. While the addition of corvettes does certainly help this argument, if you are playing for the building sandbox experience, I would look else ware. This game is definitely more enjoyable when playing with friends, due to the often repetitive nature, and long story lines if you choose to do them. The first few hours can feel slow, without sufficient amounts of currency or recourses, but it isn't too hard to obtain trillions of units, millions of nanites, and resourced are gathered just by playing, at witch the survival game feels similar to creative mode. Additionally Hello Games is now very consistent with there free updates, so it's not unreasonable to say you can expect new content to be dropped every few months. The downside is it can be a lot to pick up as a knew player. Though YouTube guides are abundant, and didn't take me too long to learn about three years back. Overall my experience with the game is great, however if you are running a lower end pc such as myself, you can expect a bit of struggle, though nothing that ruins the experience. (It is playable on Nintendo, and now mobile after all). I would personally prefer a bit more freedom when it comes to base building, and customization of such. - But hay that's what Minecraft's for. If you have yet to give this game a try, I greatly recommend it. 7.8/10

In short, this game is well worth the money for offering a cozy farming gameplay, with a lot of optional challenges and assets that you can utilize to create your ideal country life. As for a lengthy review however, i would like to mention about my first exposure to this game. It was around 2020 when i was watching a youtuber who playthrough of minecraft modpacks. Suddenly one day, he posted a video series about Stardew Valley. Seeing something far different from the usual contents that the youtuber made, i was pretty hooked and then watched the series myself. The vibe of the game felt so fun for me, someone who at the time still find farming flash games to pass the time, with its top-down perspective and colorful design. Sadly however, the series only lasted until summer yr 1, and the youtuber himself moved back to doing minecraft modpacks. Feeling a bit upset that i couldn't be able to see more about the game itself, and mind you, i myself back then didn't even know Steam's existence, which further makes me want to try the game myself. Fast forward to 2022, i finally get myself a PC, and i get to know some "unusual ways" to "install" games onto my PC, so i tried to get Stardew Valley onto my desktop as quick as possible. Even though 2 years have passed, my experience with the game itself doesn't change at all. The vibrant color design, the cozy feeling of a country side farm, which further fuels my excitement to finally get an experience of the game. First time getting into the game, it was a bit tough for me to understand the story and how some buttons work. But by utilizing my experience from watching the video series, i did manage to plant some parsnips and greet all the villagers. Fast forward to day 3, i finally set my foot to the shore to meet the fisherman, and he gave me a fishing pole. And oh boy, i spent so many days fishing for extra cash. Many people in the community may consider the fishing minigame to be hard, but that's the thing that hooked me, the pain of trying to get a catfish at lvl 1 fishing was so worth it. After a while, i finally checked the mailbox after countless days of fishing, just to see that the very first event of spring, the egg hunt has already passed away. i was a bit upset over that fact, so i went to the central town to check the calendar if there're any other events coming up and slapped straight to my face was the community center cutscene with mayor himself. We went inside to see how ruined the community center was, and the mayor asked me to help repairing the community center, else he was gonna sell it to a nearby establishment. I thought to myself, "guess i should check this out after-" and right at that moment, a apple-looking creature appeared behind the mayor. My character was shocked, and so do I. Looking at how the mayor said i was probably sick or something made me so annoyed, since the creature is literally right behind him all the time, made me yelling "IT IS BEHIND YOU!!!" so loud that my mom came to check what i was doing. After some explanation to my mom, i went back to the game and checked around the community center, which was when i found a tablet that was written in whatever language that i couldnt even google translate it. After that, i went out of the community center and check the calendar to see the next event is the flower dance, which is in the 24th, and it was the 19th when i checked the calendar, so i went back to the beach to enjoy my past time with my fishing pole. The very next day, when i was about to do another fishing trip, i saw the the mail notification. I went to check it to see a letter from a wizard wanting to meet me at his hut in the forest. So instead of going to the beach, i went to the forest to check on him, The wizard was a bit rude to me, and gave me a strange brew that made me hallucinate a bunch of trees here and there. But after all that, he told me i could understand the tablet. Leaving the hut, i made my way to the community center to check the tablet again, and indeed i could read it now. The first tablet had a bundle that requires spring forageables, which i already have some at home, so i fulfilled the first bundle to unlock the next one. One by one, i get to see myself skipping so many aspects of the game. First was farming, i barely planted anything other than the first parsnips the mayor left for me to begin my farm. Second is mining, i wasnt paying attention that there is a mine i could work on. But hey, i left those all behind, because i liked fishing more than anything at the point. I then again fished until the 24th of spring, where i participated my very first event. Seeing the villagers anticipating such a gorgeous event with beautiful flowers and happy dancing couples was fun, though it was sad that i couldnt get anyone to dance with me, since i spent all my time fishing, meaning my relationship with everything was low, aside from the fisherman himself, since i gave him some of my catches whenever he passes by. And after that event ended, i had to end my playthrough right there due to some complications within my family. Now, moving to the year 2026, being in college with some free time and money i can spend for hobbies, i recall of Stardew Valley, so i grabbed the game on Steam when a sale happens. Even though i can buy the game and play it for however long i want, one thing that i miss having is the carefree mindset i had back in the day, to spend so much time fishing without a care of other aspects. Even though i missed the feeling, i still think that by reaching perfection and finishing the achievement tab, i have fulfilled my desire to experience the game fully back in the day. All and all, grab the game and enjoy a cozy farming experience. 🏠

Dead Cells is probably my favorite *whatever*. Metroidvania? Rougelite? Platformer? Its all three in equal measure, and it does a fantastic job of blending them together in a rewarding way that seems to keep the player coming back for more punishment. The gameplay will largely revolve around what build you want to play, and features a really fun system with three archtypes that you can either focus individually on, or blend at your discretion. This system rewards experimentation, and you'll be unlocking new items and abilities as you progress. Weapons, magical abilities, passive/active buffs, traps, companions, and the means of unlocking new routes thru the game. I really enjoy the way this game *works*. There's always a part in my reviews where I say something akin to "this game is eye candy", and I feel the same way about Dead Cells. Most of this game is visually stunning, provided you enjoy pixel graphics. Light is thoughtfully distributed throughout the dark tunnels, stretching corridors and dead keeps of the castle walls. Each of the "biomes" are visually unique, sporting bright and well placed colors that please the ape brain. This only reinforces the varying challenges that different routes can present the player. I'm a sucker for good parallax scrolling and this game masterfully uses multiple layers in some areas to make the land feel expansive and lived in. The story is probably the weakest part of Dead Cells, but I don't consider that to be a hard negative. While most of the "big reveal" is pretty upfront, there's a ton of hidden backstory and implications that revolve around the player character, the kingdom, and the king who ran it. I thought that was pretty fun, as I tend to enjoy *earning* my story breadcrumbs at a time. What I DON'T like about this is it means most people will never see the full picture, because they won't feel like completing this very challenging game upwards of 5 times, scrounging for flavor text and bits of lore along the way. All in all this is a fantastic (now unhidden) gem that finds itself in my rotation every few years. 8/10

Slay the Spire relies heavily on luck. Two runs can be similar but aren't the same. There's a lot riding on your first Act because it doesn't matter what build you want to play, there's either going to be a build you get to play or a death if you don't make it come together. Along with deck order being pre-determined as a fight starts(a wise move to prevent save scumming, just noting the mechanic) it's a management game long term more than anything. In order to be truly good at the game, you need hours and hours and dozens and dozens of runs for true progress. Because the game is geared on that it really feels more like I'm zoning out hoping for a good run or managing a dead run mid to late game. While it does excel at small rewards to keep the player invested including progress on death I won't pretend it's a style of gameplay I'm super into. But for it's genre I think it's done very well. This isn't my genre but I think it excels at what it wants and if you get it on sale specifically you'll be pleased for at least your first dozens runs. Tips and tricks for the interested: -Large decks are usually a trap, burying the best cards or your intended build under energy wasters. 15-20 cards or less is my advice -I almost always try to gun for Events and Rests over Elites after Act 1 -During Rests, if you can, I'd recommend upgrading cards. Specifically any beyond the basic Defense and Attack you start with -Avoid bias with your deck and adapt. Re-evaluating even endgame can help win your fights, and never expect to get the exact build you are looking for

Hollow Knight is a good game that every other Indievania took the wrong lessons from. The correct lesson they should've taken is that sequence breaking and nonlinear exploration is a fundamental core of the genre, yet most Indievanias complete forget this feature ie they've never actually played a METROID game before. Hollow Knight itself is more like a 6.5 out of 10 than anything else. If you do just the core content its an enjoyable experience, however the side content as zero appeal to me and I find it actively a reason I don't return to it often. Almost all the side content is higher end combat driven or platforming, two things I think that aren't very good in this game. Ghost's jump is tight enough but the dash feels awkward and his nail is such a stubby piece of trash that while the game really isn't hard it just ends up making the combat feel limp. Thats the other thing is that the game really isn't very hard, the optional stuff is sure, but the main content isn't which might be a blessing cause of my prior statement honestly. On top of this while I like the exploration as a whole package I would argue the game kind of has a bad map, areas simply have too many rooms that makes exploration a little tedious at times, on top of the fact that I think the entire right side of the map is completely trash in layout but is made up for by the entire LEFT side of the map being great.

Very fun! There's a surprising amount of depth that goes into these ghosts when you're not just looking for evidence. 游戏评测：《木筏求生 (Raft)》 综合评分：8.5 / 10（蔚蓝汪洋中白手起家的漂流史诗） 画风与感官氛围 (8.8/10) ：清爽的明快卡通视听，将海洋的孤独寂寥与碧海蓝天的度假感奇妙融合。 资源收集与循环 (8.5/10) ：极具魔性的“勾垃圾”核心反馈，从单人前期手忙脚乱过渡到多人的快乐拆迁。 建筑自由与深度 (9.0/10) ：强大的网格建造系统，支持玩家在漂流地基上生生手搓出一座移动的海上赛博堡垒。 [hr][/hr] 中文评测 在度过了无数个被鲨鱼咬碎地基、满海面拿钩子打捞塑料和木板的漂流夜晚后，我认为由 Redbeet Interactive 打造的《Raft》在百家争鸣的沙盒生存领域中，写下了一段独一无二的“空间限制”求生奇迹。它不同于传统生存游戏对无垠陆地的圈地征服，而是将玩家的命运死死绑定在了一座不断移动的生存母舰上。 [hr][/hr] 五大核心维度深度整合评测 (中文版) 1. 糖衣包裹的硬核危机（画面风格的奇妙反差）： 游戏的视觉采用了非常清爽、明快的卡通渲染风格。碧海蓝天、椰林树影，初看极具惬意的海岛度假感。但在这层无害的外表下，游戏塞满了各种极具压迫感的生存指标：高频消耗的饱食度与口渴值强迫你每天必须准时捕鱼、蒸馏海水，海鸥会偷吃作物，而海面下泛着寒光的鲨鱼则随时准备对你张开血盆大口。这种“画风越萌，死得越快”的反差感让生存前期充满了策略张度。 2. 从“黄金矿工”到自动化的魔性循环（核心收集机制）： 游戏最绝的设计，就是让玩家在一块 2x2 的木板上靠一把塑料钩子白手起家。扔出钩子、精准拖回飘来的塑料、木板、树叶和木桶，这种高度成瘾的交互逻辑极似3D版的“黄金矿工”。而随着科技树的解锁，当你终于能成排地铺满“自动收集网”，躺在躺椅上看着垃圾自己源源不断入库时，那种打破前期瓶颈、实现“垃圾收割自由”的爽感让人欲罢不能。 3. 违背地心引力的漂流奇迹（网格建筑深度）： 游戏基于网格坐标的建造系统赋予了极高维度的发挥空间。你的地基只是一座木筏，但你却可以通过立柱、楼梯和天花板，在公海上盖出一座几十层高的海上摩天大楼、航空母舰甚至是赛博朋克风的水上城堡。中后期加入的发动机、方向舵和锚固系统，更是能让你带着这座移动的“重工业奇迹”自由逆风航行，将“家”的移动城堡属性推向了极致。 4. 逼真的人工环境熵增压力（大白鲨 Bruce 的生态威慑）： 大白鲨（玩家戏称为 Bruce）是整款游戏关卡设计的神来之笔。它不仅会在你试图下海开采泥土、铁矿等核心资源时疯狂追杀你，更会定期浮出水面去啃咬、毁灭你的木筏地基。它是不可能被永久消灭的（杀死后几分钟内会重新刷新），这种永恒的、合理的自然威胁为游戏注入了高明的“熵增”压力，逼着你必须做出防御枪、不断用加固铁甲去强化每一块边缘地板。 5. 非线性“水下考古”叙事（剧情探索体验）： 与常规求生游戏的漫无目的不同，本作有着一条设计非常精妙的明线剧本。通过搭建雷达接收器与三根天线，在绿色的屏幕上定位一个又一个独特的剧情坐标。从荒废的海上高塔、被淹没的废土都市到盘踞着变异生物的科研海岛，每一个故事目的地都是完全独立的箱庭关卡。通过散落在各个角落的日记纸条、邮件，像侦探一样拼凑出人类世界被洪水淹没的后末日真相，剧情代入感极佳。 总结 ：总而言之，《木筏求生》用极低门槛的魔性操作，包裹住了一个宏大且极具纵深的海上重工业建造梦。无论你是想和好朋友来一场互相折磨、手忙脚乱的爆笑航海，还是渴望独自一人靠一把钩子撬动整座赛博海洋堡垒，它都是绝对不容错过的行业标杆级神作！ [hr][/hr] English Review Raft by Redbeet Interactive is a triumphant, defining masterclass within the open-world survival genre, beautifully constructing an empire out of pure oceanic isolation. Shifting away from massive terrestrial landmasses, it forces players to tie their biological and creative survival entirely to an evolving, customizable floating home. Armed with nothing but a basic plastic hook to dredge drifting debris, you slowly climb a steep, industrializing tech tree while constantly warding off a relentless, ever-present shark threat. It masterfully fuses a bright, colorful cartoon aesthetic with intense mechanical stakes and non-linear, post-apocalyptic narrative ruins. It is an incredible, immensely addictive journey that treats the classic "zero-to-hero" crafting loop with absolute mechanical respect. [hr][/hr] 5 Core Dimensions Integrated Review (English Version) 1. Hardcore Crises in Candy Wrapping (Visual Style Contrast): The visual presentation utilizes a clean, vibrant cartoon-rendered aesthetic. The azure sky and tropical island silhouettes initially evoke a relaxing resort holiday vibes. However, beneath this harmless veneer lies an oppressive array of survival metrics: rapidly depleting hunger and thirst bars force you to fish and distill water constantly, seagulls pillage your crops, and a razor-fanged shark relentlessly patrols the perimeter. This sharp contrast between a cute art style and deadly stakes creates immense tactical tension early on. 2. From "Gold Miner" to Mechanical Automation (Core Collection Loop): The game’s absolute hook is forcing players to survive on a tiny 2x2 wooden grid armed with nothing but a plastic hook. Throwing the hook and pulling in drifting plastic, wood, leaves, and barrels creates a deeply addictive mechanical loop. As the tech tree advances, placing a grid of "collection nets" allows you to lounge around while junk automatically streams into your inventory, transforming an exhausting grind into a satisfying harvest. 3. Architectural Miracles Defying Gravity (Grid-Based Construction): The coordinate-based grid system unlocks boundless spatial freedom. Though your foundation is a mere raft, you can leverage pillars, stairs, and ceilings to construct multi-story skyscrapers, aircraft carriers, or cyberpunk-inspired floating fortresses on the high seas. The inclusion of late-game engines, steering wheels, and anchor systems turns this mobile industrial anomaly into a true wanderer, pushing the concept of a "home on the move" to its absolute peak. 4. Organic Environmental Stress (The Ecological Threat of Bruce): The great white shark (lovingly dubbed "Bruce" by the community) is a structural masterstroke in level design. It doesn't just hunt you down when diving for rare iron or clay; it periodically surfaces to violently tear chunks out of your raft's foundation. It cannot be permanently eradicated, as a new threat spawns shortly after its death. This persistent environmental hazard injects an ingenious layer of stress, forcing you to craft metal armor plates and reinforce your home's borders. 5. Non-Linear Oceanic Archaeology (Story Exploration & Lore): Departing from standard, aimless sandboxes, Raft features a beautifully paced linear narrative thread. By crafting a radar receiver and three antennas, you track glowing coordinate pings across a vast green display. From abandoned high-rise marine towers and submerged dystopian megacities to heavily guarded research eco-domes, each destination is an independent sandbox level. Piece-by-piece, players scour diaries and old emails to solve the post-apocalyptic riddle of a drowned world. Conclusion : Overall, Raft transcends the typical survival sandbox to deliver a profoundly structured, tactical experience built entirely on spatial adaptation. With its highly addictive core harvesting loop, intricate engineering progression, and beautifully layered box-set narrative encounters, it offers unparalleled late-night replayability. It stands as a flawless monument of creative survival that completely honors its mechanics and player agency. I started playing Hollow Knight just over a year ago, and yet I still remember that first playthrough like it was yesterday. Before Hollow Knight I was like a sheltered toddler in terms of what kind of games I played. A lot of Nintendo. Some Minecraft. A few indie games. So when I booted up Hollow Knight for the first time, I had absolutely no idea what to expect. The first couple hours were rough. Really, really rough. I was convinced I had finally bought a game that I simply wasn't going to enjoy. The enemies were ridiculously punishing, I had absolutely no sense of direction, and there wasn't even a clear objective of where to go next. Then, slowly, but surely, I start to get my bearings. 3 hours later, time seems to disappear and I become fully immersed in the beauty of Hallownest. Every inch of the map was something new; the game never punished you for exploring every nook and cranny. It was so rewarding, and the more I played the more I understood just how expansive the world was. Fast forward 217 hours, and I had every achievement and had 112% completed the game four separate times, including on Steel Soul. And I loved every second of it. This game is not one to sleep on. The soundtrack is immaculate . Often times you don't even notice it and it blends in perfectly with the environment. Other times it perfectly captures the scale of a cutscene, like Sealed Vessel. The art direction is also phenomenal. Every little detail is accounted for, and every area has something unique about it. There are few things more rewarding than sitting down at the hidden bench in Greenpath, with a beautiful waterfall in the background to accompany you. Or walking into City of Tears for the first time. Or brutally navigating your way through Deepnest on one singular mask and finding relief at an unexpected hot spring. The progression is done incredibly well. I would by no means describe Hollow Knight as linear, yet you can still always tell when you've made progress. The game also handles difficulty really well. Most players agree that the early game of Hollow Knight feels the hardest, even though the late and end game are objectively harder. This is because by the time you make it to those sections, they don't feel unfair, as the game has already taught you how to overcome them. I'm writing this review for my 1 year anniversary since I started playing to reminisce on what a masterpiece this game is. If you're somehow lucky enough to have never played it, PLEASE do. You will not regret it and will enjoy this game for a very long time. 10/10

What an absolutely magnificent pile of garbage. Brawlhalla is genuinely one of the worst gaming experiences ever conceived by mankind. Imagine Super Smash Bros, remove all the fun, inject concentrated rage directly into the gameplay and give every player a crippling superiority complex. Congratulations, you've invented Brawlhalla. The game has approximately 700 weapons, yet somehow every single opponent manages to use the most annoying one imaginable. Scythe mains are unemployed anime protagonists, Lance mains have never experienced human interaction, and Mordex players need their hard drives investigated. The matchmaking is absolutely phenomenal. Nothing quite compares to being matched against someone with 4,000 hours, a diamond border and the reaction speed of a fucking cheetah when you're just trying to enjoy a casual game. And the taunting. OH, THE TAUNTING. Apparently winning a 1v1 against someone with half your playtime is a monumental achievement worthy of a presidential medal. The ranked system is less of a competitive environment and more of a government-approved torture facility. You gain 20 Elo, lose 25, and suddenly your entire afternoon has been wasted. Pros: Free to play (unfortunately). Has some decent character designs (petra a baddie). Occasionally enjoyable when nobody is playing. Cons: Everything else. Scythe players. Lance players. This is the first game I've ever bought on steam, first game I've ever played on PC, and as a huge dnd nerd it was a pleasure! I was kind of scared about the turn based fighting mechanic since I'm used to stuff like Doom, RDR2 etc... but it actually gave me more time to think so it was a little bit more chill on that front and outside of the very rare bug I encountered it was incredibly smooth! The voice acting was amazing, the story was a delight and it was just overall such a fun experience that I was kind of scared was overhyped... it wasn't. I technically did 2 thirds of a run as a cleric, then started all over again as a ranger and MAN do I love the way the classes work. I did have a couple of mods for my second run just for aesthetics and 1 was actually for the number of people in your party (because I'm absolute shit at video games and I wanted to have more than 4 people) all the mods also ran super smoothly. I'll wait a little bit before diving back in as a paladin this time but BG3 has definitely become one of my favorite games (also the music and sound design are freaking amazing)

旧金山的城市底子、黑客沙盒玩法本身有可取之处，但部分主线关卡的设计和遗留bug严重消耗游玩耐心。 刚打完HAUM章节最后的逃离任务，遇到大量脚本bug：追捕状态下持枪上车交互卡死、角色原地抽搐；就算成功跑出任务划定的黄色区域，追捕脚本依旧无法正常终止，警察与直升机无限增援，杀完一批立刻刷新一批，根本不存在“清完追兵脱身”的选项。 紧接着推进到镜中世界的夏浪派对任务，预期只是拍照剧情，结果剧情结束后强制开启限时黑客连线挑战，而且进入该任务场景后主线被锁定，不完成这个挑战就无法开启其他主线案件。长段无法跳过的重复对话，叠加限时解谜压力，关卡目标转折突兀，完全没有提前给到玩家预期，反复重试还要一遍遍重看对话，大量时间被无效消耗。 可以感受到制作组想营造黑客竞赛的紧张氛围，但完全忽略玩家的节奏感受：刚从高强度追捕、bug折磨里脱身，立刻被扔进另一个高压限时任务。沙盒游戏本应给玩家选择空间，但这段流程几乎没有绕开的途径。 如果你是冲着流畅主线体验来的，这几段很容易让人心态崩溃；只想随便在城里黑客闲逛、不在乎主线进度的玩家可以酌情考虑

The parkour, and being able to get into windows on random floors — these are the only decent things in this game. And they are crippled by the fighting system which degraded so much that I simply avoid fighting zombies instead of slashing through them wherever I go. Like, it is supposed to be a zombie-slasher game, but for some reason the zombies so rarely get sliced, that most of the time you just bluntly beat them half to death before executing a finisher move that has just a couple of predefined animations. That was not the problem with Dying Light 1 — there I could aimlessly roam around the world, slashing zombies for my own amusement. In Dying Light 2 though, even just mindlessly parkouring is no fun, since there's nothing fun to explore. Therefore, my playthrough quickly deteriorated into running through the story or side quests. The problem is, neither is good. There are some decent side quests I found interesting and engaging, but even they are usually half-assed. Like that time I fetched a toy stolen from a little girl, only to NOT EVEN RETURN IT to the girl. Or like when each time I decide to snitch on a culprit, the plot conveniently makes me kill them instead. But to be fair, the plot with the lost kids and dog was a particularly well written one, and overall implemented fine. The main plot, as far as I played, could be enjoyable enough if not for the weakest illusion of choice I've seen in a game with the most absurdly written dialogs that I've simply started skipping — they didn't say much anyway, but sure used a lot of words. And that's a shame, because the characters seem interesting and memorable, and the factions have a very good composition. As for the world where the story takes place, it is so far off from the original Dying Light world, that I simply don't like it — it fails expectations set by the first game. Stylistically, that is. In general, it works well enough for the gameplay — the parkour is good enough, and the idea of having a lot of open windows to get into is very nice. What I don't like about the gameplay, is just how obviously they copied Far Cry in the various base-capturing mechanic. In the first Dying Light they had it done so well and subtle, but this game just screams "You're playing a Far Cry" as it's war cry. And it's not even "a zombie Far Cry", it is just "a Far Cry" — i didn't even notice having to fight zombies to capture a safe zone anymore. And for human bases you obviously only get to fight people. Which reminds me, that most of the main plot's fighting interactions so far were either the largely optional stealth kills of sleeping zombies, or the mandatory commiting war crimes against humanity. Which are not exactly things I'd expect to do in a zombie slasher. Also, the paraglider is not really fun, mostly just a thing you have to use. So yeah, I'm deleting this game before even getting to the grappling hook.

When I started this game for the first time, I was skeptical. I've never heard so many positive responses and reviews around one game, so I was expecting a disappointment. I didn't even realise how wrong I was... First 10 hours BG3 feels too complicated and overflowed with information that must be used and you can't catch everything that this game gives. But that's the point... The moment when you start to understand things, mechanics, ways to counter your enemies - you taste the brilliance of this product. You start seeing that Baldur's Gate 3 is not just a game, it's another dimension that can give you anything you desire. Epic fights? - No problem. Interesting plot? - Sure. Multichoice in any interaction(both combat and social)? - Of course! This game has become my personal saving from problems and anxiety in irl(and still is). Even after 1k hours of gameplay I still find something new. And that's awesome. I know that you may not be a fan of such tremendous and complicated rpgs like Baldur's Gate 3 and won't insist on playing as much as I do, but I definitely recommend you to give it a shot. As long as you proceed, the game will give you emotions you didn't expect. Hope this review was helpful. Good luck to you, adventurer! P. S. May gods have mercy on your enemies, 'cause you won't. Then and only then... Father will be proud...

I've been playing NMS since launch, and the laundry list of improvements is almost as vast as the universe it's set in. The game is very enjoyable, but I do have some gripes with it. As an example, for all the things I can do in the game, it doesn't really feel like the game is willing to let me pursue any of it, as it's always lighting up my communicator with something else it wants me to check out, "Hey" it whispers, "Go check out that thing" and not even half way through doing so I receive another ping "Hey, there's this other thing that's really cool, go look at that". Sometimes I just want to shut all quests off and pursue my own thing, but the game doesn't allow for that, and you will forever be interrupted with a to do list that is also nearly as vast as the universe in which the game is set. For another the hand holding, annoying as it is, doesn't even do that good of a job explaining what you can and cannot do. It took far too long for instance, for me to realize that you don't need to do very much gathering of basic resources in the game beyond the first hour or so because you can duplicate most everything else with certain other resources. Oxygen is a major player in this and is one of the very few resources you need to make sure you have tons of so you can just make the other stuff, but nowhere does the game inform you of this. And the list is so large you kinda just need to keep the wiki open while playing the game. These really are just minor gripes though and don't really change my opinion in terms of recommendation. Easy purchase.
